review_text:
The Grano de Oro is a truly beautiful boutique hotel. Our room though was rather cramped and came with a welcome complimentary mini bar filled with snacks and soft drinks .
The lounge and restaurant just oozes character with its rich dark wood decor. Lovely for afternoon tea, complimentary throughout the day, or to curl up with a book. What surprised us though was, as we took a walk around a few blocks, the hotel stands out as completely grandiose set amongst very ramshackle dwellings and rough paving. We didn't know if this was normal for San Jose.
Our stay here was very brief as we had an extremely early morning pick up so, although we missed breakfast, a packed take-away breakfast was left for us. We wish we could have stayed here longer to fully experience what was a beautiful hotel.

review_text: We stayed three nights at this lovely boutique hotel. It had been a huge property owned by a coffee plantation owner, now refurbished into a very stylish and welcoming hotel. Our room was comfortable and quiet. The restaurant is one of the finest in San Jose, and we enjoyed interesting and delicious food. The staff could not have been nicer. It is a walk to downtown, one we didn’t do, so I can’t vouch for the nighttime safety in the area around the hotel. Taxis to the city centre were cheap. I would highly recommend this spot if you’re travelling to Costa Rica.

review_title: Bathrooms need Updating, Dining Room is Very Good
review_text:
We expected a lot as this is the top rated hotel in San Jose and when we walked into the small, but beautiful lobby, we thought our expectations would be met. The check in went smoothly, the bellhop and front desk staff were efficient and welcoming. The room we were taken to, through a pretty outdoor courtyard, was small, though charming and well equipped but the bathroom... The bathroom may have had a new coat of paint in the last ten years but nothing else has been updated in quite a while. The bed was comfortable and the room was fine, but quite expensive compared to others in San Jose. Also, in terms of location, this hotel is kind of away from where the action is and there is not much in the area to stay for.
We would highly recommend dinner at this hotel. The menu offers a huge range of choices and we tried as many as we could manage. We did not expect an amuse bouche on the house, and as it happened, that was our least favourite part of the meal (see photo of cold fish on spoon with garlic foam). The salad was fresh and fine, though nothing special, but after that, it was all great! Delicious appetizer, delectable fish in Macadamia crust, sublime lamb shank, and an apple tart that was too much food but we simply had to eat it. Professional service in a beautiful room.

review_title: Elegant Affordable Luxury Oasis Close to Downtown San Jose
review_text: San Jose is a huge sprawling city so finding a hotel in a safe convenient neighborhood was a challenge. Hotel Grano de Oro is just such a place, a real oasis right on the fringe of the downtown area. The staff were friendly and helpful from the moment we arrived and made us feel welcome. Our room was elegantly appointed, quiet and a great plate of fresh fruit on the table when we first entered. On the last day we got a gift bottle of hot sauce to thank us. Our room also had a private garden with a fountain which not all of them do. Your experience here might vary a lot depending on the room, they have a jungle like courtyard with rooms facing it, hall facing rooms and city view rooms so be sure and investigate these locations to find the right one for your tastes. There is a great rooftop sun deck with two hot tubs and a small gym, you can see the cityscape from here. The bar and elegant dining room area is amazing, inner courtyard soaring several stories like a roman villa, very romantic especially at night. The drinks and food were excellent but not inexpensive as to be expected. Service top notch. The only drawback was the umbrellas at the inner courtyard tables, blocked the view up above a bit. The inner dining room area was warmer and no wind. Free coffee service in lobby each morning. We walked around the neighborhood but it is more commercial than anything but felt safe. Their location seems perfect for day tours, about ten minutes to downtown. There was some slight traffic noise from surrounding streets but not an annoyance and quiet at night. For me this hotel was the perfect place to stay in the city, I would definitely choose it again if ever there in the future. Well worth the cost in my opinion.

review_text:
We booked into the Grano de Oro for our first night in CostavRica. We arrived after a long flight and the customary 2 hours in SJ traffic somewhat jaded it has to be said. The building is unpretentious from the outside, but we could at least tell that it wasn’t the more usual modern tower or box, being an attractive low-rise colonial type of building instead.
The foyer is pretty impressive actually, with an enormous golden sun and some attractive use of bamboo too. Staff were all most helpful and we had a good first impression.
We had only booked the basest of rooms, working on the basis that we were due to leave at 6am for a transfer to the coast and would be no more than 10 hours in our room in any case, but the room was large and tastefully furnished, with a bath and quite traditional bathroom. The shower was not the world’s best, but no complaints and the bed was comfortable. We enjoyed a quiet night’s sleep and left the next morning very refreshed.
The restaurant and bar area are laid out around an open courtyard in the center of the property and this is a very pleasant feature. There is an array of heaters that ensure you are always warm and the restaurant is first rate.
It was a shame we were only here for such a. Short time as this is a first rate hotel, particularly when you look at what else is on offer in San Jose. It has class and character and is a great introduction to this beautiful country.

review_text:
Stayed here for a night at the start and a night at the end of my trip to Costa Rica. I was not very impressed on my first night. My room on the ground floor was quite small and basic and I didn’t make use of the restaurant because of a late arrival and early departure.
However on my second visit I had a much better room upstairs complete with “internal deck” though the bathroom was still basic for such a quality hotel. Breakfast was wonderful. The very traditional restaurant is a wonderful space, the service was good and it was a pleasure to have breakfast from a menu and not a buffet. I chose the “continental” with juice, fruit, yogurt and breads which was excellent.

review_title: Wonderful service, classic spaces, great location
review_text:
We are well traveled, and quite particular about where we stay. We loved the architecture, historic beauty, location, and warm, attentive service of the Gran Hotel. We used it as a first stop for our long weekend in Mexico City, before moving to Roma Norte.
Its Centro Histórico location- an easy 15-20 min. from the airport and within 5-10 min. walk of every major site (and top rated food and drink) in the area, was fantastic. It’s a bustling, intense, urban center- and Gran Hotel is a peaceful respite.
The room (a deluxe king) was clean, bright and comfortable. A bit dated in its decor compared with more contemporary lodging, but not in a musty, icky way- just older marble bath, carpets, etc. The
Room includes a credible coffee maker, wine cooler, nice flat screen TV, etc.
We were eager to explore recommended local food, but still had purchased the coffee and breakfast buffet - which was fresh and diverse: eggs, fresh fruit, cheese and meat, yogurts, more hearty Mexican specialities as well. Juices - a few types, including a green juice- and good coffee. When I requested espresso (to strengthen the coffee, I like it strong!), it was complimentary. Bottled water is plentiful and easy to access all over the hotel.
One evening, we had cocktails on the roof
Terrace- simple, tourist style drinks menu, but the view was lovely.
We interacted daily with lobby and reservations staff Javier, Jose Luis and Gabriella, as well as the breakfast and terrace teams- all were helpful and professional.
Overall, we would recommend Gran Hotel. We
covered most of Centro Histórico and might skip it next trip, but it’s a special place to stay in CDMX, and we recommend it highly.

review_title: Nice place to end our honeymoon
review_text: We booked the hotel as our final destination in Costa Rica and spent a single night. All in all, a lovely experience. For nearly $200 US, I would expect better water pressure in the shower, but the standard room was quite pleasant. We had an issue with noise at about 1AM when someone decided to drag their rollerboard up the stairs by our room step by step. Slowly. Very. Slowly. That, and the kids running around the halls detracted from the overall experience. Folks travel with kids all the time and there's just no reason to give them run of a hotel and have them pulling on the doors of other rooms. So, the nitty-gritty is the room was lovely. Be prepared from some noise if you book into a less expensive room. The rooms are well-designed and don't feel cramped at all. The minibar is complimentary, save alcohol, which is a nice bonus. But noise could be an issue and we found the breakfast in the restaurant to be much better than the dinner. Be sure to take in the jacuzzi deck -- it's quite pleasant. All in all, a 4-star experience.

review_title: Mediocre hotel with great restaurant and very nice doorcat
review_text:
We booked one night at this property because it looked neat and was reported to have a great restaurant.
First the good: the rooms and public areas are very clean, the bathrooms are nice, the lighting is excellent, and drinks/snacks in the minibar are free (except for alcoholic beverages, you pay for that). There is a very friendly black-and-white tuxedo cat who works out front with the bellman. And indeed, the restaurant is excellent (I will review that separately).
Now for the bad: upon checking in, the cat knew his job better than the bellman, who stood there looking puzzled as we removed luggage from our cab. He finally figured out that he was supposed to handle it, and took some of the bags (leaving the rest for us, not the proper "please go ahead, I'll handle everything).
We had a room (number 30) that opens into the interior courtyard. It has no exterior windows, and lacks privacy. We could close the windows (and curtains) to the courtyard, but still heard everything going on near by. If you stay, question what room you're going to get.
The deck with the Jacuzzis has a high fence with little sunlight. The two Jacuzzis themselves seemed to have some maintenance issues (one was soapy and the other looked stale).
There is no yard/garden or a place to sit outside and enjoy the weather except the Jacuzzi deck, which has a high fence with limited sunlight.

review_text: We stayed here twice this month, for two nights when we first arrived in Costa Rica then for one night at the end of the first half of our four week trip. Staff were amazing, so pleasant and very helpful. The room was lovely, coffee maker great and the restaurant staff would give us milk on request after dinner to use in our rooms for the coffee( I hate the powdered stuff). Hot tubs on the roof terrace were great: we used them each night of our stay. Breakfast was wonderful: a la carte and a lot of choice. The hotel looked after our large cases while we went on the first part of our trip( we were flying back from the Osa Peninsula in a small plane and luggage was limited). On our return it felt like coming home and the Christmas decorations (though early!)were gorgeous. We were sorry to leave, strongly recommend this hotel.

review_text:
What a fabulous way to start our trip. Landed in San Jose 5pm and were settled in to this beautiful hotel and surroundings by 6.30pm.
Hotel staff were very helpful so a great way to find your bearings before as we did - head out into the wilderness.
We opted to eat a light bar snack at the bar and saved ourselves for the fabulous breakfast that we had heard about - it didn’t disappoint.
Used a handy car hire company just around the corner which we walked to and collected vehicle in the morning.
Would definitely book hotel again when we return.

review_title: One of the best hotels in San Jose
review_text: This hotel small and sits in a quieter area of the city 15 minutes walk away. The building is old, comprising painted wood panelling. There is a stunning reception that leads onto a bar, restaurant and courtyard with seating. The restaurant is very well regarded amongst locals for high end food. The bar has an abundance of drinks from liquors to cocktails and everything in between. The rooms are adequate size, the amenities are just what you need for a nights stay and the service is what you expect of a hotel of this quality. Fruit is made available in the rooms, there is a stocked mini bar and a hot tub on the roof. Please take registered taxis after dark as the side roads are quiet. We recommend this hotel for couples in particular and we advise no more than 2 nights as other areas of Costa Rica have a lot not to be missed ! #exploremore #travelhustle #hotelreviews

review_text:
The attention to detail at this family run restaurant really makes you appreciate the lovely qualities of independent run businesses. I've stayed here for business as well and as for pleasure and I wouldn't stay anywhere else in San José.
I always have found that the well-appointed suites are always super comfortable and set up in a savvy way (pro tip - all the snacks in the mini bar are complementary!).
Finally, the hotel restaurant is a special treat and is one of the best restaurants in town. I've often enjoyed their breakfast in the garden (a must!) and have returned back "home" to have a delightful, locally inspired meal.
Staff is always attentive and super pleasant.
Top Notch.

review_title: Perfect place to start or end your Costa Rica trip
review_text:

Staff was friendly and very helpful.
The restaurant is also beautiful and I had a very tasty and sofisticated meal.
I would highly recommend it to end your stay in Costa Rica or as a starting point.

review_title: What a Delight with Such Professional Staff
review_text: We absolutely loved our stay here on the last night of our trip to Costa Rica. The staff went out of their way to make sure our stay was comfortable and assisted us with finding dinner reservations. Orlando was amazing. The small touches were appreciated, including free snacks and drinks form the mini-bar. A definite 5 star.....made even more special by the great helpful staff. Bravo.

review_title: Best hotel to start/end holidays in Costa Rica when flying in out SJO
review_text: Single dad traveling with my 3 kiddos aged 7, 10 and 13 - we had just returned from the Osa Peninsula from 4 days off the grid in a treehouse so we were so excited to stay at a hotel with hot water, this place certainly lived up to the press as I have read that this spot has been rated one of the top hotels in all of Central America - it did not disappoint - in every way from reservation, check in, reception, dining, all of it was top notch. We loved it all - the decor, architecture, furnishings, artwork ... the kids were even impressed with the food at their restaurant - when a place is really quality, even the kids notice - this was one of their fave hotels in CR - we will always start and end our trips in CR with a stay at Grano in San Jose - thanks to Pablo for taking such great care of us during our quick stay recently!

review_text: We spent our first night in Costa Rica at the Grano de Oro Hotel. When we arrived we were greeted by friendly staff and juice, but our room wasn’t ready yet. The hotel checked our bags and asked if we wanted directions to someplace in town. We were tired and chose to wait in the lobby. We should have taken the opportunity to wonder around the hotel to view the many old hotel photographs that lined the hallways and take in some of the history of the building. This isn’t a standard cookie cutter hotel; it is a converted mansion with many nooks and niches that give it character and beauty. Once in our room, there was an abundant plate of fruit waiting for us, I don’t know if this is standard or something the travel agent booked for us. We had a “superior” room which opened to a small courtyard. The room was spacious and very comfortable. We decided to have dinner and breakfast at the hotel restaurant, which was described as the best restaurant in town. Check out was easy and quick.

review_title: Lovely place to stay in San Jose
review_text: We stayed at the Grano de Oro on our first night in Costa Rica before starting our tour of the country.The hotel staff were very welcoming, offering us a drink on arrival and dealing with check in very promptly. The building is beautiful and our room at the front of the hotel was spacious and very comfortable with a large shower room, and a tray of lovely fresh fruit provided in the room. We ate in the restaurant in the evening and the food was delicious. As we were being picked up the next day before breakfast the hotel provided a boxed breakfast of croissants, yogurt, fruit and juice to take with us, along with fresh coffee in the lobby. We loved our overnight stay here, a great start to our holiday and would definitely recommend this hotel if you are staying in San Jose.

review_text:
From our first encounter with the doorman to our last bite at the restaurant, I was totally satisfied we'd chosen the perfect hotel to experience a little bit of San Jose. We left our rental car out front to be picked up by that agency to find that there was a bit of confusion about our room. It seems a glitch in the system booked two rooms instead of one...which was treated as a simple, 'no problem.' The desk staff could not have been more welcoming and willing to make us happy.
Do not miss a meal in this restaurant! Although no one was formally dressed, I felt like a grand dame in pearls and black velvet because the wait staff was so gracious (and willing to go along with my restaurant quality Spanish). And the food was divine. At breakfast, I enjoyed the 'typical' Tico breakfast more than the other choices, but maybe that's just me.
Our standard room was fine (OK, wish we HAD splurged on the garden suite). I can't think of another big city hotel room where the windows were thrown open to catch the breeze. Take time to inspect all the vintage photographs displayed in the halls. And don't miss the hot tub veranda.
Downtown was an interesting walk away. We enjoyed the chaos of downtown the entire way and back.

review_text: I stayed here with my daughter on our first two nights in Costa Rica. We loved everything about this beautiful hotel: the organisation, room, food, hot tubs, location, atmosphere, courtyard breakfast, warm welcoming dining room, in-room facilities, fountains. I had requested a car to meet us at the airport via our booking agency, which was confirmed personally by a named member of the front office team. The driver was there to meet us exactly as promised. Our room was so lovely, with two large beds, bathrobes, spacious bathroom; the hot tubs on the roof were welcoming and relaxing; the food was delicious with charming service; and after a "hard" day walking into town (20minutes) we felt we were coming home. It was just perfect - expensive, but you get what you pay for in every way.

review_text: Had reason to visit this hotel twice during a recent dive trip to Costa Rica. The hotel is set back in a small side street, and has real character. The welcome from the staff was warm and friendly. The quality of the rooms are spacious and quaint, mine over looked the restaurant area and had its own small garden with water feature. Each room has a small minibar with free drinks with the exception of alcoholic drinks. There is a coffee machine in the room and wall safe. The hotel has free Wifi in all areas. The hotel is of a colonial style and oozes charm. There is a hot tub and there is availability to have a massage from the spa area.All in all a very nice comfortable hotel, just a short walking distance from the town centre.

review_text: I spent a wonderful afternoon and evening at Hotel Grano de Oro – an absolute gem in downtown San Jose. The hotel staff were so friendly and made me feel very welcome. Besides the beautiful rooms, the hotel is fascinating and very eclectic. In contrast to the very modern reception area, the rest of the hotel had an “old world” feel to it. I was mesmerized by the endless passageways, staircases, hidden gardens and fountains, not to mention the delightful jacuzzi terrace. The hotel also boasts a first-class restaurant where I enjoyed a fantastic meal, and ended it off with a marvelous espresso dessert. I highly recommend this hotel.

review_title: a nice place to stay in San José
review_text:
this was a lovely hotel, with lots of positives - excellent clean room, with an actual bath albeit a small one, lots of freebies in the minibar, lovely cocktails in the bar, and superb service from all the staff. they even mended my boots after I asked where I could buy glue nearby!
the evening meal in the restaurant was top quality - admittedly it was expensive, but that's normal in capital cities and in hotels of this quality.
the most bizarre thing was the breakfast - you had to choose from several types of breakfast, and if you didn't choose one with toast, you didn't get bread or toast. in fact when you got toast, it was two tiny pieces with an equally tiny amount of butter. given everything else, this really struck as odd - if I could have had more toast free of charge, it should have been offered.
given everything else was so wonderful, I think they should look at their breakfast - if there isn't room to do a buffet, then they should think about offering more things as included, such as yoghourt, breads, preserves, cold meats and cheeses etc. it wasn't a patch on the breakfast we had at Arenal Springs Hotel, and that was a shame as it was our last night in San José.

review_title: One of the most interesting (and nicest) hotels we've stayed at
review_text:
We stayed here for one night after our flight into San Jose. It's a really neat old Spanish-style building that has been renovated into a hotel and restaurant. We had a family suite, which meant two bedrooms and a huge bathroom. The room had great AC, a big bathroom and was very quiet and clean. My kids loved the hot tubs on the outdoor deck. And we had an amazing dinner at the French restaurant at the hotel. The staff was very friendly, helping us obtain extra water, boxed breakfasts for our early departure in the morning, etc. If you are staying in San Jose, this is the place to stay.
As for the location, San Jose is a very small city. We walked to the central market and Jade Museum without any problem.

review_title: Perfect Ending to our first holiday to Costa Rica
review_text: We wanted somewhere fairly close to the airport to stay and recollect on an amazing 3 week holiday. Hotel Grano de Oro was the perfect choice. The hotel has a calm, relaxing feel to it in a busy, somewhat chaotic city. We had a late lunch on arrival, an evening meal and breakfast in their restaurant and all were excellent We did have a small problem with our television and I must say the hotel staff handled it exceptionally If you are looking for somewhere memorable to stay at the end of a holiday and before a long haul flight chose here we are so glad we did.

review_text:
The hotel is lovely, the staff lovely, the restaurant superb. A nice little gift shop helped us complete our shopping.
We had the suite which is way up on the roof. An enormous room with lounge area, jacuzzi tub, bathroom with shower, minibar etc. The room was amazing but one draw back is that you go up some stair from the public terrace/jacuzzi area and the noise of people using this facilities can be a bit annoying. Also being so high you are not shielded from the street noise and as there are major roads in both directions the traffic noise starts soon after 0500. You would be better having a room further down within the hotel where you would be shielded from this.
Breakfast was very good and could be taken either in the restaurant or outside in the central courtyard.
We would definitely stay here again if we return to San Jose and the restaurant is worth a visit even if you are not a resident.

review_text:
This place has a great atmosphere. It has the charm of an old Southern hotel mixed with a little modern eco feel. A little bit of a strange mix but fun. You almost feel like it should be haunted (and our lights did go on and off).
Check in was easy and the front desk staff was nice. They greeted us with a wonderful OJ/passion fruit juice. The room was off an outdoor court yard. It was clean with two double beds (advertised as queen but seemed smaller). Big, nice bath. AC.
The hot tub area is beautiful. Liked the little shop in front. Restaurant was just ok.
I would definitely stay here again.

review_title: Grano De Oro Suite Was Amazing
review_text: We stayed at this hotel after being in the jungle for a week. It was beautifully designed and well kept. We loved staying in the Grano De Oro suite with amazing views over San Jose. The food is fabulous- we dined in the restaurant and did room service- both were great! They stock the mini bar daily with snacks and non-alcoholic drinks. While we are glad we stayed here, next time we would probably just stay one night by the airport. There isn't a whole lot to do in San Jose. We walked to the Gold museum and had a great lunch at Tin Jo. Glad we experienced the city, but next time we will just spend more time at the ocean. The only downside is the loud road noise.

review_text: We started our week long Costa Rica trip at the Hotel Grano de Oro. As soon as we entered the reception area we were greeted with friendly faces and glasses of refreshing fresh fruit juice. The check in process was quick & easy (probably made more so by the fact we used Camino Travel to organize our trip). This hotel is immaculate with so much attention to detail. You can tell it was an old mansion which adds so much unique charm. Beautiful staircases, light fixtures, water fountains, art pieces from the time of the original mansion, beautiful orchids & lush greenery surround you. The room added the perfect blend of modern decor. The bed was extremely comfortable. Camino Travel & the hotel surprised us with a complementary dinner to celebrate our wedding anniversary; reservations were for 7:00 on the day after our arrival. That day we went on a full day excursion to the Irazú volcano/crater. We returned to our room around 5:00 pm and decided to rest for an hour before getting ready for dinner. Well we ended up falling asleep, not waking until around 8:00, missing our dinner reservation! We were so disappointed! A few minutes after waking, our room phone rang; it was the hotel asking if we were okay, noticing we missed our reservation and asking if we wanted our special dinner brought to our room! I have never experienced such a thoughtful gesture when traveling! The fact that they noticed our absence made us feel special. We placed our order and very soon after dinner was delivered to our room and laid out for us in such a caring manner. We are overjoyed even before we took our first bite of food. Now, to describe the food! I don’t have the vocabulary to describe how delicious everything was! My sister in law is a chef in NYC; she stayed at this hotel a couple years ago and raved about the food. It was perfect! I highly recommend Hotel Grano de Oro and would stay there again without hesitation. Thank you Grano de Oro for making our time with you memorable!

review_title: A comfortable, elegant choice in an unlovely city
review_text:
If you prefer a hotel with charm and individuality to a standard chain-hotel, then this is for you. It's also, I imagine, at least as comfortable as any other hotel in the city. The central building is a restored colonial mansion and the hotel retains a modicum of the grandeur sparse grandeur that San Jose once possessed. San Jose is worth a couple of nights, and by Latin American standards, it seemed to me, at least, safe and friendly. it's an easy twenty minute walk to the centre, to the gold museum, the national museum (more fun than the gold), and the amber museum (which I missed).
Breakfast is good, but not generous. I prefer a buffet myself.
Overall, this is the place to stay.

Nice hotel, with nice people.

review_title: Nicely appointed, pleasant staff, ROOFTOP JACUZZI!
review_text:
We stayed here our first night in Costa Rica, primarily because it's located conveniently close to the rental car offices where we were picking our car up. It's done up in a splendid Colonial style, lots of gilding, fountains, ornamental flourishes, etc. - very visually appealing. The staff are friendly and welcoming. The in-hotel restaurant was similarly appointed, had good service and good food. The prices did seem a bit high, but it's a restaurant in a high-end hotel, so I wasn't taken aback. The menu could benefit from a few more vegetarian options, but maybe I'm an outlier as a vegetarian guest - most of the other guests seemed to be eating meat dishes. Room was comfortable, quiet, had fast Wi-Fi and an in-room coffeemaker.
The big stand-out of this hotel, in my opinion, was, as you might have guessed from the title of this review, the two rooftop jacuzzis with adjoining sundeck! We had just flown in, and some evening jacuzzi time (the rooftop is open until 10PM, which is great) was just the ticket for me to relax and settle in. The jacuzzis are clean and prettily lit, and there's even a bit of a city view. Really nice up there.
All in all, it's a perfectly pleasant hotel with the major plus of a rooftop jacuzzi. The reason for the deducted star is the price. It's a significantly more expensive hotel than others in San Jose, and I'm not entirely sure the jacuzzi alone justifies the price increase.

review_text: We enjoyed our second visit to the beautiful, unpretentious Hotel Grano de Oro as much as our first visit two years ago. Prior to arriving there was some slight confusion about our room reservation, and in turn they kindly offered an upgraded room upon arrival with a nice outdoor patio. What impressed me once again is how incredibly clean and incredibly well maintained this property is - no signs of age or wear. review_title: Grand old facility, excellent anchor for each end of our trip
review_text:
We recently traveled to Costa Rica with most of our time spend at the Osa Peninsula and Monte Verde. We flew into San Jose and stayed one night at the Grano de Oro before heading out. We had a lovely room on the ground floor off the garden. Clean, quiet, and spacious. Breakfast was find. The staff was gracious and welcoming. We returned to stay two nights at the end of our trip. The first night we ended up in room #10, second floor facing the street. The moment we saw the room we asked to be moved, but that was not possible that evening. Despite assurances of sound proofing, we spend a mostly sleepless night listening to traffic, sirens, and other street noise. The staff did move us for our second night, and we were fortunate to get the same garden room as we originally had. If you are at all sensitive to traffic noise I strongly recommend you avoid room #10 (and room #11 directly across the hall).
I want to give a big thanks to David in the bar for his above and beyond gesture in providing this beer affectionado with the label from my bottle. He not only peeled it in one piece, he attached it to a piece of paper to insure it did not stick to anything else, and trimmed the edges. This small act spoke volumes for the professionalism and respect the staff offers to its guests.

review_text:
My girlfriend and I stayed one night at this hotel after a week on the Pacific Coast. The hotel is incredible with colonial charm and the staff was incredible. The front desk staff was very friendly, as were the restaurant staff, bell desk staff and everyone else.
When we got to the airport and realized that we left our passports in the safe in the room, the staff arranged for a taxi to promptly bring our passports to us at the airport, and also called to follow up to make sure we received them. I'm not sure any other hotel would have been so accommodating.
The room was incredible as well, with a small private patio with a fountain. You could almost forget that you were in the middle of a bustling city. The food at the restaurant was great too. Overall, it was one of the best hotel experiences I have ever had, and I have been to many, many hotels.

review_text:
We stayed at the Grano de Oro on the first and last night of our trip to Costa Rica and it was a great choice.
The hotel is beautifully appointed with a classic colonial feel. From the moment we arrived we had great service. The hotel had arranged our airport transfer and we were met by a lovely driver who gave us ideas and tips for our time in Costa Rica. Check in was quick and efficient with a welcome cold drink. Our room on the 1st night was small but well appointed. Coffee and tea facilities and a mini bar with complimentary items ( not alcoholic).
Breakfast in the courtyard restaurant was a delight with efficient service. On checkout we were not charged as the staff said we could pay the whole bill in our return visit.
When we returned 13 days later we arrived early but were still able to check in which was wonderful. We were given a free upgrade to a gorgeous room near the courtyard. Again the staff were lovely, we had unknowingly left a USB plug after our 1st visit and this was returned to us.
Breakfast again was great, I could sit in the beautiful courtyard for hours. We checked out but as we were on an evening flight we left our luggage and spent the afternoon in the city returning to collect our luggage and get our taxi to the airport, once again arranged by the hotel.
This hotel was a perfect start and end to our Costa Rica adventure and I can see why it is number 1 on Trip advisor.

review_title: Quality hotel for San Jose stay.
review_text:
This is a lovely old colonial style hotel , located just outside the city centre.
It was selected for our first night following the 11 hr flight from London. The hotel is probably about 30 minutes drive from the airport but if making the journey in the notoriously busy San Jose rush hour, expect almost 3 times this!
The hotel was lovely. Reception very efficient and understanding, we loved the room (room10) and the spacious bathroom and shower were especially appreciated. Also, the free snacks available from the mini bar were welcome. A coffee maker was available.
The breakfast location was amazing, a lovely internal courtyard with a beautiful selection of plants adding to the ambiance. The service at breakfast was excellent, although I personally would have preferred a self service buffet for the non cooked items.
The hotel can’t really justify having a swimming pool, but the twin jacuzzi arrangement was excellent.
Minor point, the traffic noise was a little intrusive starting from 5.00 am, but there is not much that the hotel could do to alleviate this.
Overall a lovely hotel with a great team of staff. Would happily stay here again.

I would rate this hotel 5 if they had King beds instead of smallish Queen beds.

review_text:
A beautiful, well maintained, clean hotel. Friendly, attentive staff. Nice jacuzzis on roof (shame they were both hot - could have done with a cooler one in the heat!) Smart, tidy room. Complimentary snacks in mini bar, replaced each day. First class decoration throughout, with interesting planting in little courtyards. Some areas were neither inside or outside, such as the dining area, so that added to the unusual atmosphere.
Food is difficult for me, as I am gluten free (coeliac) vegetarian, the breakfast was ok, not amazing, but I am usually just glad to get something whilst travelling, or indeed back in the UK. So, won’t drop any points for it, as others with less challenging diets may be more impressed. We didn’t have any other meals.
Evening bar good. Entertaining to watch bartender prepare, with skill, the many cocktails.
15 minute walk into central city area. Similar distance to good size park with lake.

review_text: After traveling from the Pacific Coast we spent our last night of a ten day trip at Hotel Grano de Oro. The very modern front entry leads to a maze of traditional rooms. We settled in to our garden entry first floor room, very quiet, quality bedding and updated marble bath. The rooftop jacuzzis sounded inviting but we were tired and there is no view of city or mountains. Instead we got comfortable at the beautiful ground floor bar overlooking a dining courtyard and had a cocktail. Later in the evening we enjoyed meal of prawn bisque, chateaubriand, mushroom ravioli and tres leches. This could only be topped by the breakfast in the morning; French toast stuffed with carmelized mangoes, great coffee and fresh mango juice. Then off to the airport and reality!

review_title: A gourmet's delight - perfect start for a holiday in Costa Rica
review_text:
Enjoyed three nights at this tropical, Victorian mansion with an excellent restaurant.
The service - from our first email enquiry, all the way through to check-out - was first class. All the staff were friendly, helpful and efficient.
The rooms and public areas, beyond the modern reception area, are full of character.
There is a small, verdant garden which had pots of poinsettia in early January. We also enjoyed the rooftop Jacuzzi.
Although breakfast is not included in the room rate, the al a carte breakfast is good value for money. It includes a choice of cooked dishes, coffee, fruit juice, delicious homemade breads and fresh fruit.
Dinners were exceptional and traditional with white linen and silver service. The standout dishes included a delicious mozerralla ravioli with ratatouille; the smoked scallop, tenderloin of pork with apple jus and the smoothest mashed potatoes. Compliments to the chefs for consistent, gourmet standards in such a busy restaurant.
Our room was spacious, comfortable and sparkling clean. The upload and downloads wi fi speeds were better than at home in the UK. We appreciated the espresso coffee and complementary cold drinks in the fridge.

review_text:
Charming hotel.
Our upper-level room (#4) was small-ish and with no outdoor sitting area, but well appointed. Complimentary mini-bar products a nice touch.
Restaurant (outdoor and indoor) and other common areas of the hotel are lovely.
Breakfasts were great.
We were a little disappointed with our dinner on New Year's Eve. Nothing very special had been done for the occasion, we felt quite rushed through our meal, and then we were told we needed to order dessert before we even finished our wine because the kitchen was closing at 10:00 pm!
The wine list was impressive, though, and the bottle our waiter helped us choose was fabulous!

review_text:
This hotel is beautiful. We had dinner in an open air courtyard. They had heaters and umbrellas (just in case of rain). Beautiful large stained glass windows. Inside were huge upholstered banquets. Nice selection on menu. Lots of fresh fish, and a very nice steak for a picky spouse ;). Rooms were nicely appointed, bath was big enough. My only complaint was there were only about 3 English channels on tv, one of which was cartoons. Arg!
Lovely bar, with local cocktails as well as nice selection of rums.
Would highly recommend this hotel.
We stayed in room 24, which was quiet and only up one flight of stairs.
Lots of historic pictures hung through out hotel were very interesting.
Staff very friendly, which is typical of Cost Rica.
Very comfortable king size bed

review_text:
Most of our recent trip to Costa Rica was spend on the west coast but we spent the last night at Grano de Oro before our flight out the following day. This was certainly the nicest hotel we stayed at during the week. They upgraded our room as a courtesy. The unique nature of the various rooms was very appealing. We found that we could quickly walk to the central market before dinner and it was a perfect evening.
Pros: A+ service and staff attentiveness, very nice unique rooms from a bygone era, Excellent value, parking available, one of the best restaurants in San Jose is on premises, very walkable to much in San Jose, easy to get to airport.
Cons: Restaurant is expensive, though worth it. City traffic around hotel is dense at rush hour. Hot tub facilities were off line when we were there.
We will stay there again.

review_title: All in all a very nice hotel.
review_text:
The Grano de Oro is a clasically styled hotel near to a number of busy roads. The area around the hotel is ok but as other guests have noted doesn't look particularly enticing at night. You have to walk several blocks to reach shops and restaurants and those are typical city type chain restaurants.
We liked the way that the hotel had several Christmas trees with lights and festive decorations.
We were given room 10 (Deluxe room) which is at the front of the hotel facing the road. The road outside the hotel is ok but there are two parallel roads that have constant 24 hour traffic, so the room suffers from very audible road noise and vibration from trucks. This could be improved by adding secondary glazing to offer guests a quieter stay.
Apart from the road noise, room 10 is spacious. The bed was very comfortable and we slept very well with earplugs.
The bathroom could however benefit from updating, especially the shower. The toiletries were contained in large dispensers attached to the wall reminiscent of the type in a health club. Not really the standard you would expect in a hotel of this quality. The room could benefit from a USB charging port.
What we did like was the free non-alcoholic drinks and snacks available in the mini bar. These were replenished daily. A nice touch.
We ate at the hotel restaurant every night. The setting is grand and service professional. The quality of the food is very good. It is fine dining but not too ostentatious. The cocktails are better value than the wine. We liked the Tico sour. We ordered coffee at the end of each of our 3 meals and every time it was served differently. Once as a cup of watery filter, another in a plunger (again with little flavour) and the best by a mile was the coffee made using the proper pressure coffee machine. It should be made this way every time! No point in having good ingredients if you don't extract the flavour.
All in all a very nice hotel.

review_title: Nice hotel from the outside, rooms do not live up to the public spaces
review_text:
Nice hotel close to central San Jose. Outside and public areas are beautiful. The open courtyard outside the restaurant inside the hotel could be considered breathtaking. The restaurant was very good and the ambience was lovely. The front desk staff was very pleasant and helpful.
Stayed in a deluxe room which was fairly small. Bathroom was pretty basic. Bed was ok. It was fine a short two-night stay, I really wouldn't stay longer than that. Didn't really feel the accommodations were worth the price, which was high for a San Jose hotel with no resort amenities. At the time of our visit there was major construction going on.
This is a pretty well-known hotel so it's easy for cab drivers to interpret when you tell them where you need to go. Located about 25 minutes from San Jose airport.

review_title: One of the most beautiful hotels in San Jose Costa Rica
review_text:
We had the pleasure of staying at the Hotel Grano de Oro on our recent trip to Costa Rica. What a beautiful hotel!
We were there on 3 separate days/nights as we toured different parts of the country.
The hotel is a beautifully restored Victorian Mansion with different rooms on different levels. I chose the Garden Room Suite and loved it! We had our own private terrace and the room was gorgeous. The staff couldn’t have been more accommodating at every level.
The restaurant was amazing-food was of the highest caliber, taste & creativity.
Would highly recommend using this Hotel as your entry and exit hotel from Costa Rica. Beautiful, luxurious & serene.

review_title: Charming boutique hotel with wonderful staff
review_text:
This hotel is a gem! It's a lovely converted colonial manor house that's well located in the heart of San Jose but feels like a little oasis. My romantic was tranquil and comfortable and there were lovely touches like a fruit platter on arrival. My absolute favourite thing was the staff, who were genuinely helpful and friendly. The restaurant is also very good. They don't have a buffet breakfast (probably because it's a small hotel) but have a la carte breakfast with a good selection and everything I had was yummy. I had dinner in the restaurant two nights in a row - it was very good both times!
I hope to stay here when I return to San Jose in a few months. I visited during low season, and unfortunately I don't think the budget will stretch to the high season rates... But fingers crossed...

review_title: Lovely hotel in converted Victorian mansion, wonderfully hidden in the bustle of San Jose
review_text:
This lovely old mansion in the heart of San Jose is a little haven of quiet in the midst of the hustle and bustle of San Jose. We arrived, were met on the street, and showed in to the very welcoming reception desk, complete with a cool drink – a big aah after the airport and drive into town. We have to say a big gracias to the desk staff who were very helpful to us as we struggled with trying to connect with our travel agent to get the right size SIM card for our phones. They placed the calls for us and spoke to the agency staff to better explain what we needed (it was the weekend and neither the on-call agency staff nor we were fluent in the other’s language, particularly when it came to technical explanations!). When the driver came with the correct SIM card, the desk could not find us (as we were exploring as you will read below), but graciously accepted the card from the driver and expressed our appreciation. They really could not have been more accommodating and helpful. We also made reservations for dinner at the hotel restaurant and arranged our transport the next morning with the desk.
Once we were checked in, we were shown up to our room on the second floor of the main building, where we were transported back to the gracious colonial past of the country. Our room was quite comfortable, even if relatively small. You walked in to the room and one wall had a luggage rack, a large old wooden wardrobe, a small table with coffee/tea makings and a TV above it, and round glass table with two chairs in the corner of the room. We had a large window that overlooked a mass of greenery with lots of birds flitting around. Along the other wall was a comfortable king-size bed with a round night table on either side. There was a rather small bathroom in the corner of the room, which contained a deep bathtub with a tiled surround, a modern toilet and an adequate vanity. The wardrobe held a safe, mini-frig, and robes. The overall ambiance was one of old-fashioned colonial charm, which was quite refreshing.
Even better were the hotel grounds, which are beautiful but constrained. There is really just the old mansion itself – there is not a big expanse of lawn with swimming pool and lounge area. You wander through the many corridors, floors, patios and nooks of the old mansion, and everywhere you look are flowers, lush greenery, orchids, fountains, and birds flitting about. You keep getting lost and find yourself poking down a corridor that you have already explored, and finding the Jacuzzi becomes a little treasure hunt in its own right. But the babbling of the fountains and the singing of the birds makes your exploration a pleasant one. We did finally find the Jacuzzis on the sunny upper floor, which also made for good bird watching.
We had reservations at the hotel’s restaurant, but we did not appear to need them at the early hour that we booked (we hadn’t eaten since our morning plane). The restaurant was lovely and had a very welcoming outdoor seating area that was tempting, but the staff appeared to be concerned about rain so we ate inside in the elegant dining room. Please see our separate review of the Restaurante Grano de Oro for details, but suffice it to say here that it was the best meal that we had in Costa Rica! We had been told that the restaurant alone was reason enough to stay at this hotel, and we believed it after our meal. The service was efficient and gracious, the food plentiful and delicious, and the price was an excellent bargain!
We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Grano de Oro, and it seem remarkably quiet considering its location in the heart of town. We enjoyed having the window to allow in the fresh air breezes and to hear the bird song. That is, until about 4 in the morning when the birds woke up again. They must have heard, like us, the honking and racket noises of the city. I guess that was our introduction to Costa Rica where the mornings always seem to start early with the wake-up alarm calls of howler monkeys and birds to tell you to get up and enjoy the cool of the morning! Loss of some sleep was a small price to pay for the experience. We know you will enjoy the Grano de Oro as much as we did.

We stayed here 1 night at the end of our tour. The hotel is a beautiful building and is kept very well. Our room was clean but not the largest and looked onto the central courtyard.
The city centre was within walking distance and the area seemed reasonably safe in the day.
The restaurant was a bit of a let down, the appearance promises a lot but the food didn't live up to its surroundings, the service could have been better too although the cocktails were good. Breakfast was ok but by no means the best I've had but the fresh orange juice was excellent.
We did find a nice local bar/ restaurant about 4 blocks away which served good beer/ cocktails and had a Cuban theme and atmosphere which was well worth a visit ( La Bodeguita Del Medio)

review_text:
We had SUCH a good time staying at Hotel Grano de Oro in San Jose! From the moment we stepped out of the car the staff was wonderfully welcoming and the 'boutique' hotel feel was warm and comfortable. The rooms are cozy and tastefully decorated - more traditional feel, which was perfect and a little indoor terrace. We were in room 5, which is in the smaller section of the hotel right over the restaurant. Absolutely perfect! Reasonable pricing. Everything in the mini-fridge (except alcoholic drinks) were included in the stay. They also gave us two drink vouchers (that could be used for alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks) at the bar. We asked to use them for non-alcoholic drinks with breakfast and they graciously said yes.
The restaurant was great. We had breakfast every morning in the restaurant and the dinner one of the nights we there. Friends that are local to the area wanted to go back for dinner on our last night in San Jose (we were staying at an airport hotel the last night, but came back for dinner). The staff was very friendly and attentive. The prices were competitive, so no problem having meals there unlike most hotels.
Spa services were really nice. The massage therapist came to the room to get me and walk me over to the spa room. I had a nice massage and well priced as well.
Service charge of 10% is already included in services, you can leave an additional tip if you'd like and the staff doesn't pressure you either way.
Location is great- less than ten minute walk to centre of San Jose. You can uber (which is REALLY inexpensive in Costa Rica) or walk. Lots of restaurants (mostly chains), shops and rental car places on the main strip.
The ONLY thing I wish was different was that there were only two towels in the room and we requested an extra one. We had to request the extra towel every night though after the room had been serviced. That being said, they brought it up immediately every time we asked.
We had originally tried to book at another hotel that wound up being under renovation. Thank goodness for that because we fell in love with this hotel and plan on staying here every time we are in San Jose in the future!

review_text:
The Hotel Grando de Oro is a really cool hotel with a great restaurant/bar and wonderful staff. During our stay we had multiple parts of family and we got to see three different types of rooms; a twin bed room, suite with water garden and suite with deck/balcony. I found the water garden room very cool and have never seen that before in a hotel. The staff and housekeeping was also great, helpful, and attentive.
The restaurant had great food that everyone in the family enjoyed. Waiters were attentive and the food came out hot and relatively fast.
Bed and sleep quality was also great with signs saying to be quiet, water fountain being turned off, comfortable beds and other nice touches that added to the stay.
While there was a lot of stairs and drops and ledges that was hard to get bags around on and people with limited mobility my have trouble with. I do believe they did have accessible rooms, but I am not sure of that.
Other nice touches like a lending library and hot tub really added to the stay! The hotel was beautiful and was near cool sights like the market, downtown and historic buildings! Overall experience was great and would definitely recommend to anyone!

review_title: Lovely hotel for a 1 night stopover in San Jose
review_text: We stayed here for 1 night at the beginning of our visit to Costa Rica and 1 night at the end (as we were flying in and out of San Jose). It is a delightful little hotel in the centre of the hustle and bustle of San Jose (but positioned down a side street, so very peaceful). The staff are all extremely polite, friendly and helpful. After a lot of travelling, we were greeted with complimentary drinks, many smiles and a room upgrade. We dined in the restaurant once and the food was very good, in smart but relaxed surroundings. The hotel is spotless and perfect for what we needed. Recommend.

review_text:
We stayed August 1-4. The property is beautiful. Our rooms were on the ground floor surrounded by beautiful local flora.
The hotel resturant is one of the best in the city. The breakfast was best, but dinner highlights included the nut encrusted beef tenderloin and sea bass. The banana coladad and pina colada were among the best I have had.
The staff are wonderful, as would be expected of a property of this caliber. They were always helpful. The only critique was they seemed less aware of things to do in the city.
Below are a few suggestions:
- You can see the main museums in a day. There is a pass you can purchase. If you are a student there is a discount.
- You can walk to the downtown area from the hotel during the day. It is a good way to get some exercise while expereincing the everyday life of Costa Ricans. This is noy a pedestrian friendly city cross streets at cornors and make sure the cars have a red light to stop. Not all corners have wall signals
- The food options are not great outside of the hotel. Lots of American fast food resturants. The cafes are hit or miss for food, but the coffee is amazing everywhere. TIP:The National Theater has a nice cafe that is worth a trip.
-If you exchange money at the hotel you will get less for the convenience. There is a bank and money exchange place half a mile from the hotel. Bring your passport.
- there is a park and sports complex half a mile from the hotel. Walk along 2nd Ave in the direction of traffic. Good place for a walk or jog. They also have paddle boats and bikes for rent. The hotel does not have a gym, so this is an alternate.
-Cabs are readily avaliable in the downtown area. The metered fare is what you pay. It is in colonas not dollars or euros. A trip downtown to the museums during the day was about 17 colonas.
-Safety: Exercise common sense and read travel advisory from your embassy. During our stay and many walks we felt safe. At night the hotel and many locals we met suggested taking cabs.You will see people who are begging on the streets. They were not aggressive usually. Be polite, but firm as needed, and generous when you can. Poverty and underemployment are a world wide problem, but especially in developing countries like Costa Rica.
San Jose is usally a first stop for tourist who are seeking to go to other parts the country. You can experince San Jose in two days. Hotel Grano de Oro is an excellent choice for your stay.

review_title: Start of our Costa Rica vacation
review_text:
We spent 2 nights at the Hotel Grano de Oro. It is a lovely hotel, very clean and the staff was wonderful! It is several blocks from downtown San Jose, but all within walking distance.
We arrived at this Victorian mansion and were given passionfruit/orange juice drinks as we waited to check in. Everyone was very courteous and gave us all the information we needed about breakfast, the jacuzzis, dinner, the TV and the minibar (which was all complementary, except for the alcohol.
There were 4 of us staying in a deluxe, double queen room. Plenty of room for my husband and me, with our two grown children, 19 and 16. The beds were comfortable and the room was quiet. We didn't think the hotel was full, but they indicated that they only had 2-3 rooms available.
We had dinner the first night in the hotel and the ambience, service and meal were all terrific. Good variety on the menu and from the warm bread to the extensive wine list, we thoroughly enjoyed our meal. It is a good value, when compared to NY prices, but I can see where prices are high compared to other restaurants in town. Breakfast is included and everything was delicious. The complementary fruit and banana bread were great!
Not much to do in San Jose, but we are looking forward to going back for our last night in Costa Rica. Oh and important for the kids was free wifi throughout the hotel.

review_text:
My wife and I stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro for two nights to start our vacation in Costa Rica. Although parts of the hotel are being remodeled, it was a comfortable and nice place to stay. The staff are courteous and professional,
So, what makes this place such a winner? The service and food at the restaurant (Note: Service is mentioned first). Although the food was fantastic, our server, Carlos Castro, added a special seasoning that enhanced the flavor. Carlos was one of the best servers we've ever had: welcoming, professional -but authentically nice, and a good Spanish teacher.
You can't go wrong by dinning at the hotel's restaurant. And the entire staff, hotel and restaurant, were great. But Carlos added a little something extra- maybe it was the Spanish lessons....

review_title: Great Hotel for long or short term stay
review_text:
We stayed here for 2 stopovers during a trip to Costa Rica. On both occasions we received complementary upgrades to garden rooms - which were very nice.
The hotel is near enough for a short cab ride to the airport, and is a 20 min walk from the centre of the San Jose shopping/museum areas, which are very lively and in fact reminded me of city high streets in the UK!
The relaxed but efficient way you are met in reception typifies everything about the hotel - very professional.
The décor in the public areas is also really well done and gives a cozy but classy feel to the building.
The restaurant is apparently well know and attracts non residents, I can understand why, we really enjoyed the food (as well as sitting outside at the small bar!)
All in all - a great place for stopovers like we did, but I can only assume it would be just as good for a long stay.

review_title: Quiet and peaceful in a big city
review_text: We had the room with the private patio and a queen size bed. What a relaxing place! There is NO noise other than the bubbling fountain in our little patio. We never heard anyone else in or out of the hotel, though we know they were there. I love the dark hardwood floors, ceilings, and cabinetry. We felt so welcomed here! We had told them our arrival time, so a driver was waiting for us at the airport. On our arrival, we were handed fresh fruit juice while we checked in. In our room was a platter of fresh fruit and a minibar stocked with free snacks and drinks. I love this hotel. We stayed five nights but I would gladly come again. The bed is very comfy and the room has a table and chairs, plus the two chairs in the covered patio. The staff is very friendly and helpful. And there is even a lending library if you need a new book to read. I love this hotel. I'm so glad we stayed here instead of in one of the US chain hotels.

review_text:
I had previously stayed at this hotel in 2004, on my second visit to Costa Rica I made a point of staying at Hotel Grano de Oro as I had liked it so much on my first visit. It is a converted mansion, the restaurant & bar areas are very attractive & the rooms are tastefully decorated. The hotel is arranged around a small central garden area with tropical plants, which adds to the overall pleasantness of this place.
2 terminals are available in the lobby area for free Internet access.
Food quality in the restaurant was consistently good, as was service.
Hotel Grano de Oro is not situated on a major thoroughfare & the surrounding neighbourhood appeared pretty quiet so guests shouldn't be disturbed by noise. Other reviewers have commented on safety issues in San Jose but I didn't feel uncomfortable walking around the town, during daylight hours anyway.
Negatives? Hotel Grano de Oro isn't a budget hotel, & restaurant prices were at the "fine dining" end of the scale, but I felt that the quality of hotel & food justified the cost.
Overall, Hotel Grano de Oro is within my top 3 favorite hotels.

review_title: Lovely luxury with quiet rooms in the midst of San Jose
review_text:
We spent 2 nights here & the rooms are just as they are pictured...we stayed in the family room which was really lovely for our family of 4. (it could easily hold a family of 5) Despite proximity to a main street in San Jose & just a 10 minute walk to the central market, it was nice & quiet. As you might expect from the photos, the linens and bath products were commensurate with the appearance as well. There are lovely little green courtyards nestled throughout the hotel & even though there was no 'view' out our windows, there were the tops of lovely palms that made you feel you were in the midst of a tropical forest.
Service was exceptional, so very friendly and helpful. The gift shop has a lovely selection of local made things & the restaurant was beautiful with good food & excellent service as well. The family that owns this hotel has also started a charitable organization to help young girls in trouble in Costa Rica, so it's also nice to know that you are staying with someone who has a heart for people...and it shows!

review_text: A delightful hotel in a quiet side road of San Jose - full of character and old world charm. We stayed there for one night before heading off early in the morning to Tortuguero. There is a garden that, from what we could see in the dark, was like a mini rainforest. Our superior room on the ground floor was tastefully furnished and had it’s own small courtyard based around a private fountain, and there are other larger fountains in the hotel – one in a small courtyard where corridors joined and one in the bar courtyard. We had read that there was a fine-dining restaurant there and we were keen to check it out - and were very glad we did. We were pleased to see that it was frequented by many local people appearing to be on a special night out. The service was excellent, the food was beautifully presented and delicious - some variations to accommodate our vegetarian requirements were easily agreed - and we had a thoroughly enjoyable evening there – it was a super way to start our holiday.

review_text: My only choice anytime in San JoseCertainly the best in San Jose, and a very good one in any standard. The Grano de Oro hotel is located in a very quiet neighborhood, 40min. approximately from the airport (hope there will not be any traffic). It is beautifully decorated, with spacious and very indulging rooms. Bed are large and so pleasantly comfortable. Bath is a real treat and you may prepare your own espresso, too. service is impeccable- Attentive and warm and friendly. Adriel and Clara, especially, as well as all other members of the reception staff made every effort to make our stay comfortable and so enjoyable. Breakfast is served in the well reputed restaurant (see my review), and the eggs Benedict with the rich truffle cream was indeed a real treat. definitely my only choice in San Jose. (i) Book in advance. (ii) Ask for room 7. (iii) Don't miss the egg Benedict in creamy truffle sauce.

review_title: Old colonial style boutique hotel, an oasis close to downtown
review_text: Boutique, old colonial style hotel with many rooms around courtyard areas about 20min walk from central San Jose. We used this as a stopover after/before flights and it works for that. Stylish and very photogenic with a lovely restaurant, small shop, no gym or pool but tiny rooftop area with jacuzzi. Avoid standard rooms which are cramped and with tiny bathrooms; superior are better, more spacious with a bath and open to the courtyard. All rooms have coffee making and a fridge where snacks and soft drinks are included in the room price. Breakfast is to order only (no buffet) and although the menu looked good the food was disappointing-my Eggs Benedict was swamped in sauce with little smoked salmon and the omelette was tasteless. Dinner had a lovely ambiance and the quality of food was good but tiny portions and expensive-approx $60 for 3 small starters. Wifi is free and fast. The staff were all really helpful. If you have to stay in San Jose this is probably the best option.

review_title: A grain of gold in San Jose
review_text:
Spoiler alert: You are probably not spending your trip in San Jose.
Like most, we used this as our decompression point out of the country. The hotel is amazing, an old plantation style home converted into a 40 room boutique hotel.... very cool. We stayed in a room with a patio and it was clean and relaxing. The restaurant in the lobby, which we skipped, was visually appealing. I had no good reason to eat there as it was expensive and I was in the hotel for less than 12 hours.
So here's what I found useful:
Can you walk to local attractions.... sort of. Do you want to... no. It is in an offshoot of a main area and at night, I did not feel the warm and fuzzy feelings of safety. That being said, the hotel had staff 24/7 and the parking was secure.
Is it close to the airport.... yes but no. Fun fact, the major bridge that you need to cross in and out of San Jose to the airport is under construction... for the next 5-7 years What that means to you is your approx 5.3 mile drive goes from 30 mins to anywhere upwards of 1.5 hrs. Plan accordingly kids! especially during rush hour.
A nice hotel, great staff and I would stay there again. Not much to go out of your way to do or see in SJO. This hotel is walking distance to fast quick eats, but I wouldn't wander to late at night. Take a taxi or uber.
Safe travels!

review_title: Lovely way to start a trip
review_text:
After the most harrowing 40 mins of my life, picking up a worn out hire car and negotiating chaotic San Jose traffic at 11p.m on a Friday night, we parked up in the secure parking 30 yards from the hotel. From then on, all was good.
Good room (32) with its own ornamental water feature out side it's window. Very good shower. 4a.m top notch coffee and a rooftop garden helps those on European times start to adjust. All the breakfasts were fantastic. We had one dinner here, very good. The bar was lovely, with good range of cocktails, enthusiastically made up to 10pm when it shut.
Everything is as you'd expect from a 5star establishment. Genuinely nice staff in an interesting building.

review_title: Old style charm in the centre of San Jose.
review_text:
We arrived at the Hotel Grano de Oro at midday, the reception staff were friendly and efficient. We were given a 'Welcome' drink and informed that our room wasn't quite ready for us. (This hotel provides a late check out time of 12.00pm). We decided to have a look round the hotel whilst waiting for our room to become available. The hotel has a Colonial feel to it, with its wooden décor, pretty courtyards, black and white photo's, tiled walls and antique furniture. There is a small roof terrace, with 2 Jacuzzi's. They have a nice gift shop with a variety of products and we picked up a few things for family back home, the prices in the shop were cheaper than the shops at the airport. (just for info)
We decided to have some lunch in the hotel but were a little apprehensive as we were casually dressed. We had arrived from a stay at a jungle lodge in the Osa Peninsula and were in shorts etc but we needn't have worried, as the staff in the restaurant made us feel very welcome and put us at our ease. The dining room is beautifully decorated with an outside courtyard area. We had a very enjoyable lunch with good fresh food.
Our bedroom was light and airy with a window overlooking a courtyard. It had all the usual amenities and a very comfortable double bed. A nice touch was the free snacks in the mini bar, the fridge was also useful.
That evening, we ate in the restaurant, this was always our intention, as it was the last night of our holiday before heading home. We had read previous great reviews about the food served here and we were not disappointed. We had a fabulous meal served with a great bottle of Malbec. The service was first rate too.
The following morning, we had breakfast which was ordered from a menu, there is no buffet style breakfast here which again was extremely good. We then walked from the hotel to their National Theatre which is an easy walk along the Boulevard. It took us about 25 mins. Their National Theatre has a lot of history to it and is well worth a visit. If you ask at reception, they will provide you with a city map. We found the reception staff very helpful but you will need to ask if you require something/information. The theatre is stunning, we did one of their tours with an English speaking guide, it was an hour long and cost $10.
We were being picked up from the hotel at 1.45pm and the hotel kindly let us keep the room on for an extra hour without charge.
We had a fabulous stay at this hotel and would have no hesitation in recommending it to family and friends.

review_title: Quirky, but in a charming and inviting way!
review_text:
This hotel has meandering halls and changes in elevation such as small stairways that will be a problem for anyone with mobility issues. That said, if you have normal mobility, you will probably find the winding halls to be quite charming. Stop and look at the photographs, to learn about San Jose during the time the house that is now the hotel was built. I promise you will find it interesting, even if history is not your thing.
The modern lobby actually blends well with the rest of the facility, perhaps because it was done so tastefully. The extremely capable staff will greet you warmly and carry your luggage wherever it needs to go. The hotel is environmentally friendly, and the rooms are attractive in the way that rooms at your grandmother's house might be if she were fairly well-to-do.
All of these things would be irrelevant to me if the rooms were not comfortable, but they were. Our room had a/c (which we didn't need), easy chairs for reading, and lots of floor space. Our french doors opened to a little garden with a fountain and the bathroom was large and well-appointed. We found the refriegerator useful and the coffemaker was handy, too. The restaurant was fabulous and I have reviewed it separately.
The beds were comfortable, neither too soft nor too hard. We will definitely stay here again, but there was one drawback: the rooms mostly come with two double beds. If this is your honeymoon, don't book until you call them and discuss this, to see if they can accommodate you.

I only ate dinner there but had great meals!! I would definitely stay here again!

review_title: Relaxing way to start our trip
review_text:
This property is a small, elegant boutique hotel in a central location of San Jose. Our room was small yet well appointed, and surprisingly quiet. Linens were nice quality and bed was comfortable. Both check in and check out procedures went smoothly. The staff were helpful and spoke excellent English. We did not have breakfast in the dining room as we had early morning pick ups on both days of our stay, but coffee was provided in the lobby beginning at 4:30AM which was a great touch. Dinner at the lovely restaurant was delicious, although the service was quite slow--we found this to be the norm throughout Costa Rica.
We will probably plan on staying here again if we travel through San Jose in the future.

review_title: A Very Nice Place to Stay in the Capital City
review_text: Like many other international travelers, we arrived here after many hours of traveling (about 11 hours) and just wanted to rest the remainder of the day. The check-in was prompt and efficient. Our room was up to date, with a small veranda that we really didn't take advantage of. Unlike others on this site, we had a small refrigerator in the room, a spacious closet and a nice bathroom. (We took advantage of the fact that the snacks were complimentary other than beer and liquor. We were booked through a travel agent and prepaid our trip, so I have no idea whether or not this is usual or not.) We had some trouble with the toilet and it was promptly fixed. After the first night, we were out all day on our first full day in Costa Rica. So, our impressions of the city were limited by the hotel and the two restaurants that we went to. The hotel restaurant is located within a courtyard and is luxuriously appointed and romantic. The food was very, very good. It is touted as one of the best restaurants in Costa Rica and I believe that it is the case as it would easily be considered a fine restaurant in the New York City area. Costa Rica is so reasonable for Americans! Two appetizers, two mains, a bottle of wine were about $150, which I consider to be cheap for a restaurant of this caliber. This is a fine hotel to start your Costa Rican adventure.

review_title: Charming hotel with a gracious staff
review_text:
We stayed for two nights and received excellent service throughout our stay. Marco, the manager, is an exceptionally gracious host who greeted us after a very long flight, offered us refreshing beverages upon our arrival, and arranged for us to be seated in their dining room immediately after our check-in. All of the staff we encountered gave us prompt and helpful service. During our stay, Marco personally followed up with us to ensure that we were enjoying our visit; we certainly appreciated his attentiveness and efforts.
The building is charming and well kept. It is a small, boutique-type establishment with a modern lobby and an attractive gift shop. The rooms are on the smaller side, but they are adequately furnished in a more traditional, antique style. Our room faced a courtyard filled with tropical plants; it created an atmosphere of peace and calm although the hotel is located in the middle of a more urban neighborhood. The room has air conditioning; opening the windows for fresh air is an option. The room was clean and quiet.
The hotel restaurant is elegant with both covered seating as well as an open courtyard. The covered seating area is rich with dark wood and comfortable chairs, while the atmosphere in the courtyard is refreshingly bright and airy. We ate breakfast, lunch, and dinner at the hotel and enjoyed every meal. The restaurant staff were very service oriented, and we enjoyed our experiences there.
The hotel is perfect for an overnight stay (or two).

review_title: DO NOT STAY HERE!! They stole money from me and won't refund it.

I arrived at the hotel to check in and they didn't have my reservation. I contacted Expedia to get a refund for the $900 I was charged for the wrong dates. Expedia said they wanted to refund me, at least for 2 of the 3 nights, but the hotel would not refund me at all. They were so rude to me and so unreasonable. I had nowhere to stay and was out almost a thousand dollars. Do not stay here and don't use Expedia either. Thanks for ruining my trip to Costa Rica. This hotel is HORRIBLE!
