review_title: Five star amenities and service, four star price value.
review_text:
Check In: The front desk staff was exceptional. They were always professional and immediately ready to help with whatever we needed. From the welcome drink of orange and passion juice that was waiting for us as we walked in, to the friendly greeting by name every time we walked through the lobby, they were great. We also asked to extend our stay by one night despite the hotel being fully booked. They let us know the moment that there was a cancellation and adjusted other checkins so that we wouldn't have to switch rooms. A small thing, but a very accommodating thing.
Room Pluses: The room was small but well laid out. The quality of the bedding was superb, which is 80% of everything about a room; a good night's rest makes the toughest day easy, whereas a bad night's sleep makes the smallest frustrations seem huge.
Wifi was fast and reliable, water was drinkable from the tap (no worry about getting sick from using tap water while brushing teeth,) bathroom was very nicely retrofitted with white tile, quiet closing toilet lids and clog-free shower heads with ready hot water and abundant pressure. Both rarities in even the better hotels in C.R. due to high mineral content in the water.
Room Negatives: There were some glaring deficiencies for a room costing $400/night which included electrical outlets which were very difficult to find as one had to move a bed away from the wall to reach them, the lack of a full length mirror, the lack of a proper fridge for cold beverages, limited closet/storage space and blackout curtains that didn't close completely. Our phone didn't work when we checked in although it was replaced the next day. Instructions on how to use the TV's aren't given but should be, as the sets need to be switched on manually before the remote controls for the satellite TV will work.
Our room was also one of the oldest ones, meaning walls that weren't worth the price. Once the guests in the rooms above us and next to us awoke on our first morning at 6am, we had no choice but to be awake as well as we could clearly hear the walking, talking about breakfast orders etc.
Room Service: The kitchen doesn't have a dedicated room service runner, so service requires taking a waiter away from the restaurant. When the restaurant is busy, this can take nearly half an hour for cake and coffee. We ordered meals, snacks and drinks a total of 6 times, everything arrived lukewarm or cold. Room service is good for deserts and cold drinks, but not for anything warm other than sandwiches. Another suggestion is to avoid the nachos and anything else that is not based on French or Italian cuisine, as every such menu item that we tried fell far short of the excellence and passion that the more classically inspired menu items displayed.
Restaurant Pluses: The restaurant is the shining star of this hotel. There are very few Continental Cuisine inspired restaurants in Costa Rica that can compare to it, in fact it could compete favourably in major European and American markets. The wait staff are extremely personable and quick. I was extremely impressed with how quickly and seamlessly they covered for each other, bussing each others' tables, answering questions and taking drink orders on their way to and from the kitchen etc. At times they were so fluid that we weren't entirely certain which waiter was actually ours.
The menu is sufficiently deep that you won't feel limited even over a four or five night stay. My greatest challenge was to not order too much at every meal, as I was very impressed with the menu and knew that I wouldn't have enough meals at the hotel to try them all! :-) Despite my best efforts I still left the restaurant uncomfortably full after every meal because I insisted upon having three or four course meals every time!
The chef does an incredible job of sourcing perfect produce and other ingredients of great quality. (The one exception seemed to be poorly aged beef.) The presentation is flawless but not overly busy, preparations were always perfectly done to order every time and plate times were consistently less than ten minutes even with a full restaurant.
This is a PROFESSIONAL chef who runs his kitchen like a ballet. My last meal during this stay was a breakfast that included Eggs Benedict with black truffle, (the chef added extra truffle for me,) which was so good that I ordered extra bread in order to consume every ounce of the heavenly mix of sauce and perfect egg yolks. It was the best breakfast that I've had in a year.
Excellent, passionate and knowledgeable Somalier. Thank you for the tour of the cellar!
Restaurant Minuses: While I intend to eat here literally every time that I visit San Jose in the future, it wasn't perfect. I strongly recommend that you avoid dishes which have been added to extend the coverage/reach of the menu beyond classically inspired Continental cuisine. The passion and skill of the chef is obvious and thoroughly enjoyable when enjoying the duck prosciuto, salad with strawberries or pasta. However the braised lamb with Moroccan inspired spices and couscous was a big disappointment, as was everything else on the menu that wasn't either French or Italian inspired including the “healthy salad.” These dishes were clearly outside of his passion or expertise and were wasted opportunities that could have been spent enjoying other, better dishes.
The waiters need more training in wine service and need to be much quicker bringing things like salt, pepper, hot sauce or anything else that you ask for. (For some reason these things are not normally on the table and take several minutes to bring from the kitchen, allowing your food to get cold while you wait.) They also need training on how to prioritize. I once asked for more coffee as well as an order of bacon. The bacon took five minutes, during which I went without coffee even though it was sitting five feet away. Very strangely, the breakfast waiters also refused to leave a flask of coffee at the table, requiring me to ask them to fill two cups at a time. This was needlessly annoying and complicated and cluttered up the table for no reason.
Still, this is now one of my favourite restaurants in C.R.
Bar: There are no good things to say about the bar. Nearly $80 including taxes and service fees for two double vodka martinis is a high price to pay in any establishment and these were poorly made. After our first sticker shock at dinner we avoided cocktails before dinner and digestives afterward, (myself and my partner,) stuck to wine and reduced our dinner bills by nearly $200. The bar needs serious revision and extensive training and re-work.
Amenities: Excellent, lots of attention to detail . Common areas are in need of refreshing and updating as they're a bit worn, but that is because the hotel is operating at capacity. Which is an incredibly good sign of quality.
Maintenance Problems: Phone not working, weird calls from maintenance at 7am, 7:15 and 7:26 about the phone which we couldn't answer because despite being able to ring, the phone didn't work in the first place! Also a VERY bizarre call came one morning while we were still sleeping from house keeping asking if we were ready for them, waking us up again. Even though we had the Do Not Disturb sign hanging on our door. It was surreal and very annoying.
Summary: All in all this is definitely an hotel where we'd stay again in a pinch, as the location is excellent and the service fantastic. The rooms are both good and bad and could be partially improved without too much cost, but will never be really worth the price point being charged. They are closer to a $200 value in our experience as professional travelers and hospitality company owners ourselves. The staff are exceptionally gracious, quick and hardworking. The bar is to be avoided.
The restaurant is utterly fantastic!

review_title: Elegant hotel priding itself on service
review_text:
My wife and I spent three nights at this hotel before starting a tour. An elegant if somewhat rambling property as one would expect of a former residence located within walking distance of main attractions and shops. Reception was friendly and efficient and the Manager took the time to introduce himself. Our bedroom was a deluxe patio, sparsely but adequately furnished. WIFI was good and the bathroom was well equipped and had a large shower.
Breakfast selection was adequate but the two dinners that we ate were excellent.
Service throughout the hotel was very good indeed.

review_title: old world luxury in a busy metropolis
review_text: Within easy walking distance of "downtown" yet in a relatively peaceful location in noisy, polluted capital city. This is a converted Victorian mansion providing comfortable bedrooms free from traffic noise provided you are not in the rooms facing the busy road. Superb breakfast. Reputed to have the best restaurant in the city but we did not eat dinner as still groaning from a late lunch elsewhere. Staff at front desk very helpful and friendly and all speak excellent English. Delicious coffee available from at least 5am in reception lounge for early risers. Strongly recommended.

review_text: We stayed here for just one night at the beginning of our Costa Rican holiday. Lovely room off a small courtyard, good sized bed and bathroom. Loved the quirky decoration of this old Victorian building. Ate a simple dinner in the restaurant as we were very tired from a 12 hour flight, very tasty & good wine choice. Breakfast was à la carte in the large airy courtyard, good choices and great coffee. Spent some time on the small terrace in the morning but didn't use the jacuzzi. Friendly, helpful staff made our brief stay here even more pleasurable.

review_title: The Gorgeous Grano melds Contemporary and Classical Charm
review_text:
It's been a while since I stayed here with girlfriends, for a night on either end of a trip to Tamarindo but the Grano makes a lasting impression!
If you love the idea of staying in a modern and comfortable, yet romantic hotel that could have been the location for a 40s movie set in the tropics, this is your place. The rooftop deck is charming and the monstrously large, potted plants, on pillars, at the ends of corridors will amaze you gardeners.
My room had a tiny, private, walled garden which, because of the quirks of the mansion, was only to look at out the window and not to sit in. It had a zen like fountain that I could hear in bed, and a killer, luxury bathroom with every amenity one could want.
Outside the hotel is the hustle and bustle of SJ, inside, it is quiet and a world away from the city. The location is not the best but the hotel is a world unto itself with no need to go out, if you're only there for an overnight.
The restaurant was romantic with wonderful food and the hotel staff were impeccable in their old world, professionalism and kindness, from curbside to tableside. It's the only place I'd stay, if I were to go back to San Jose.

review_title: Wonderful traditional hotel in San Jose
review_text: Stayed her for one night before flying out of Cista Rica but could have stayed longer. Beautifully designed and furnished hotel with jacuzzi and gift shop on site. Room with it's on seating in a conservatory with fountain. Very novel. For longer stay the wardrobe is small but everything else is lovely. Large bathroom with all you need supplied. Excellent restaurant with amazing service and food. Lifts for the travellers with walking difficulties. Good as this is a smaller hotel. 39 rooms. Loved the decor and would recommend for a stay in San Jose. Walking distance of all sites.

review_text: This beautiful boutique hotel was our first night's stay in Costa Rica. It didn't look like much from the street with its ordinary urban neighborhood, but inside, we were welcomed with lush garden areas and a lovely room. This hotel is part of a consortium of small boutique hotels dedicated to being luxuriously green. The manager went out of his way to provide service to us and went over and above by personally going to the local Hard Rock Cafe for one from our group to get a pin for him when he knew we didn't have time to go ourselves. The restaurant is absolutely stunning and the food exceptional. This was a great start to our vacation.

review_title: A real oasis in an ugly capital city
review_text:
Formerly a grand private residence, this hotel has small but well-furnished bedrooms on corridors between open courtyards, one of which is part of the grand and beautifully furnished restaurant, where we ate the best meal of our stay in Costa Rica. The hotel has a colonial feel with old photos and 19th century artefacts, and made a pleasant change from more modern hotels in our package.
The hotel is used heavily for one-night stays by people arriving in or leaving the country, as it is reasonably close to the airport, but it would be a good base for some of the scenic attractions near San Jose. It's just a pity that the capital city itself is so horrible: we took a walk from the hotel to the old town and found nothing of any aesthetic or historical interest except the old National Theatre building, which had by that time closed for visits.

review_title: An Oasis in the middle of San Jose
review_text:
I spent a night in the Grano de Oro as a getaway vacation with my girlfriends and had a fabulous time in this beautiful boutique hotel. The staff was very friendly and efficient and offered us refreshing cool drinks upon arrival. We were early and our room was not ready yet so we left our bags at reception and had breakfast in the hotel restaurant.
The hotel itself is a refurbished tropical Victorian home with walls lined with black and white historical photographs of Costa Rica at the turn of the century. The restaurant which is worth a visit in itself has a lovely outdoor courtyard where we ate breakfast and dinner during our stay.
The rooms are spacious and the bedding is heavenly. Top quality bedding and the beds are not too hard, not too soft. I had a really good nights sleep there. The room has ample closet space, good internet connection in the room, a table and chairs , lots of light but with blinds to keep the room dark if you want to sleep in. Top quality bathroom products as well.
I booked a spa treatment and the spa specialist came to get me in tmy room to escort me to the spa. I had the "reborn" treamtment which was a facial with a mini massage and felt great afterwards.
The restaurant was delicious and I noticed that many clients seemed to come just for dinner so make a reservation even if you are a hotel guest.

review_title: Lovely old boutique hotel outside San Jose
review_text:
The hotel itself is a delightful conversion from a huge Victorian mansion. If you have
trouble with steps, or even seeing steps, this hotel is not for you. Everywhere you
go there are 3 steps up or two steps down....
Delightful outside eating area in the centre courtyard where we ate breakfast and
dinner.
Our main disappointment was our bedroom. This was by no means a cheap hotel,
and we were given a small room with only one window overlooking an inner courtyard.
Almost no light penetrated the room. The decor and furnishings did not match the quality of the rest of the hotel, the lighting was inadequate, and the room was very
uninviting.

review_title: What a place to spend your first or last night
review_text:
We stayed here on our last night. The taxi driver told us it was the best restaurant in town as we had been quizzing him where to eat. The front of house told us the same so it must be right ( it was). Wow what a beautiful hotel. Old style Spanish hacienda with lots of internal courtyards with more greenery than the rain forest, beautiful public rooms. A barman who could mix the bets cocktails ever and a truly stunning restaurant. The wines as usual for CR very expensive due to tax and poor quality unless you could get a mortgage. Wifi throughout. review_text:
This is a beautiful hotel, within walking distance of the city centre, but blissfully quiet and comfortable. In an old colonial building with bedrooms set around greenery filled courtyards with fountains--really lovely. We stayed here at the beginning and end of our Costa Rican holiday, so experienced two rooms. They were very different, but both elegantly furnished, tastefully decorated, with excellent beds and lighting. The bathrooms were not huge, but had good baths and powerful showers. It was all spotlessly clean, and having free nibbles and non-alcoholic drinks from the minibar is a nice touch.
Check in and out was easy, with charming reception staff who spoke perfect English. The welcome passion fruit drink was much appreciated
Breakfast starts at 7, and is cooked to order. It was delicious, as was the evening dinner
Highly recommended

review_text:
We stayed 3 nights at the start of a lengthy trip to Costa Rica, the Grano de Oro is probably the best address in San Jose, far enough away from the busy city centre but not too far to walk to the main attractions such as they are.
Our "superior" room was at the back of the hotel in the rear "rainforest courtyard". The rooms are dotted round the hotel and are all unique so this is unlike staying in a standard fare city centre hotel.
A medium sized room (no. 21) with polished wood flooring, white and yellow walls, ornate moulded ceilings, air conditioning and a ceiling fan. The mini bar is stocked with free goodies and the bathroom is simple but functional with a comfortable bath.
Staff are all very friendly and willing to help. Breakfasts were very good from an a la carte menu and dinner (we dined here two nights) was excellent with an ward winning wine list too. This is certainly the best address to eat in San Jose.
Highly recommended.

review_title: Nicely converted and characterful Victorian mansion - SO pretty at Christmas
review_text:
We only stayed in this boutique-style hotel here for one night, but on the breakfast alone I wished we'd had longer. Things we loved were:
1. The breakfast - I had the pancakes with roasted bananas and caramelised macadamia nuts. Wow (see photo). People we coming up to me saying they wished they'd gone for that. Delicious and so big! Nice fresh fruit and warm fresh bread. My bloke had the huevos rancheros for his cooked breakfast, which was really good too.
2. The Christmas decorations - so many lovely touches. Each and every room had a Christmas stocking hung on the door, and there were tasteful trees and other decorations. It's often hard to feel Christmassy far from home, but this place nailed it. A real sense of fun.
3. The elegant furnishing and surroundings - you could dine in an open air courtyard under umbrellas, or inside. The lounges were sumptuous and very characterful. There was a lovely interior garden, and you'd stumble across a stone fountain in a corridor. Even our Deluxe room had a small garden area with a water feature.
4. The staff - absolutely charming. Such nice people. Made us smile many times.
5. Our room (no 38) was lovely, and the bed really comfortable. Despite being in the heart of the city, it was quiet too.
This was a perfect place to relax and unwind after a long flight. We felt very spoiled.

review_title: Beautiful Hotel, Delicious Restaurant, and the Best Staff
review_text:
This boutique hotel is so beautiful. The room was clean and the little patio attached to the room was wonderful. We ate at the elegant hotel restaurant 3 times out of our 2 day stay, each time ordering all three courses and multiple drinks. I had the french fizz cocktail and the mojito (which rivaled the best from the states and south america).
Not only did the beauty of the hotel and the quality of the food impress me, but the service was wonderful as well. There was a gentleman (manager maybe) at the restaurant, Alvaro, that helped me find my 2 year old son's yellow tractor that he left behind...I could hear the whole restaurant team on their walky talkies communicating to find it. That was just the kind of service that made me want to take the time to write this review. Kudos to you, Alvaro, and the rest of the Hotel Grano De Oro owners and staff. We will definitely be back!

review_text:
Sadly we only stayed one night here before heading across the the peninsula.
The staff here has incredible attention to detail. This isn't our first time in Costa Rica, and service can be a bit.... slow in some parts.
Not so here! I know gratuity is included, but we gladly tipped 20% on top! We both spent a lot of time in Costa Rica, that's where we met! So we know how expensive it can be for ticos, and how hard it is the find and train a staff here.
Kudos to the management team! The staff is warm and inviting, their English is great even though we both speak spanish, we never needed to use it.
Some parts of Costa Rica can be shady, more so in the small towns than San Jose. It can be harder to find good service and the staff can be greedy, again, not so here. Warm and genuine.
Pros: excellent service!
Great food
Cons: it's in San Jose :(

We spend one night at Grano de Oro, after arriving in Costa Rica.
This hotel with a lot of character must be one of the best in San José
We had a standard room, but the standard at Grano de Oro is very high, so this room met our expectances by far. Nice dining room, with tables in an enclosed garden. Fine dining and fine wines.
Staff very friendly and helpful.
If you stay in San José, don’t book a room in one of the international mastodons,
Book a room in Grano de Oro, it is boutique, customer friendly and offers you a great stay

The secon night we have been given a room at ground floor, and even if they said they upgraded us, the room was smaller and the balcony was darker and open air.
The hotel structure is very nice, and also has a small terrace with jacuzzi!
Some suggestions on how to improve: larger twin beds, giving the possibility to hosts to turn on heating when it is 15 degrees ouside.

review_text:
Loved our room, number 24. Comfortable bed, shower over bath 😟, good storage for clothes and quiet. We drank cocktails at the bar, they were great. We ate breakfast both mornings in the restaurant. The first morning we waited 3/4 hour for it to arrive with service that could only be described as brusque. Husbands Pico was lovely, my rancheros tasted great but waaaay to much quest and the presentation was awful. Loved the fresh juices. Breakfast was faster the next morning and I had the pico!
We also ate at the restaurant both nights. Patchy service again. Husband had rabbit which he pronounced delicious. I had the chicken which had a lovely taste but dry. Second night husband went for the rabbit again nad this time it was mushy. I had the duck and it was superb! So was the tart tartin.
Not a place to come for reliably efficient service but beautiful environment and some food to please. We would come back.

review_text: My husband and I spent 3 nights at the boutique Hotel Grano de Oro. Everything was beautifully done, clean and comfortable with all the little details attended to. Upon arrival we were greeted with a delicious glass of tropical juice. With a garden and jacuzzis, there are lovely places to relax in a big city. A mini bar was stocked with a variety of beverages and snacks, all of which were complimentary except the alcohol. Palmier cookies were left for a sweet bite before bed or to have with your morning coffee. The staff are friendly, helpful and knowledgeable. We did not have a car so the hotel was well-situated for our needs. In one direction we were one mile from La Sabana Park and the National Soccer Stadium, and in the other direction we were two miles from downtown, the pedestrian area of Avenida Central, shops, museums, restaurants and near neighborhoods of historical homes. We ate our last dinner at the restaurant at the hotel. While it is expensive, it was worth the splurge. The menu was varied, and the food was delicious and well–presented. My husband had the chateaubriand and loved it. I enjoyed the lamb shank and couscous. While the dinner was great, the dessert was amazing. The Merengue Crema de Amaretto was to die for. Stay here…you won’t be disappointed.

review_text: This was the best hotel stay I've ever had, anywhere -- and I've stayed at several Ritzes and other places that charge more than $500 a night. As soon as the luggage is out of the taxi, it disappears up to the lobby. When you step up to the desk, Pedro pulls out two flutefuls of local fruit juice. And it keeps on getting better from there. Whatever you need, whatever you want, SUPER service with a smile. Gorgeous facilities, comfy rooms, clean and constantly overloaded with extras, extras, and more extras. And they upgraded us instantly, without my asking, too! If you ever come to Costa Rica, this is the place . . . and even if you're not planning on visiting San Jose, this hotel makes it worth a trip. Ridiculously perfect!

review_title: Poor service in a beautiful Hotel
review_text:
I will not return to this Hotel at least until I am convinced that service has really improved.
The reception is a disaster. You called it, no answer. When it answers it hang up the phone.
My luggage arrived on the 2nd day of my stay as it was missed by Copa, and it was forgot at the reception notwithstanding I asked. It was when we confronted them with the receipt that it admitted, oh we forgot.
The wifi is a disaster. A problem each day.
As for the rooms my business partners complained and were changed. My room was a normal room which I just needed. Beds are comfortable.
The restaurant is a must. Great breakfast in a beautiful setting.
A lot to improve to be called a Hotel and not a B&B and more to be in the No. 1 spot of this prestigious site.

review_text: I booked this hotel in celebration of my boyfriend and I's anniversary.... the staff was very very kind, but for how much I spent (more than twice as much as many incredible places in Costa Rica) I was certainly underwhelmed. It's old Victorian charm might appeal to some but we felt like we had left Costa Rica! We got an upgrade to a deluxe room which was quite average. Again, such kind staff, and if you want to drop tons of money on a place that feels safe and colonial, this is your spot.... but I wouldn't go back even at a lower rate. I had a great omelette for breakfast but my Boyfriends huevos rancheros were almost inedibly heavy and rich and saucy.... a bit bummed about it all... but great location!

The value is great...not a cheap eat by any means..but worthy of a special occasion. Don't miss the small gift shop too!

review_text:
We spent a few days in the southern part of Costa Rica and decided to stay over two nights in San Jose since our flight was out very early in the morning on a Monday. I had booked this long before and almost had forgotten why I had booked it.
This hotel comes with the feel of the ritz, but the quaint aspect of a boutique hotel. I know that it was called boutique, but they really do this up and make sure that you are tended to every step of the way, which honestly is what you want from any hotel you stay at.
Rooms were spacious, the shower was nice and hot, and the beds were very comfortable. We ate at the hotel restaurant and let me tell you, that was some good bits right there. The food was delicious!!
Right when we got there we asked about massages and they signed us up for an hour and a half apiece and just when I thought I didnt need anything like that, it was exactly what we needed. Made the flight home so much more relaxing.
Only downturn I would say for the whole experience was breakfast. I was told that the fruit plate came with the breakfast, but was sadly disappointed in the selection and the amount. I love fruit and we got a small dish of it to my dismay (even after the waiter pointed out we didnt need to pay for it because Costa Rica is the land of fruit). Well if it is, then FRUIT it up!!
All in all I would recommend this hotel to anyone who asked.

review_text:
House like property is fully restored. The mix of traditional and a splash of modern flare make the property an enjoyable place to hang out. The greeting from the front desk staff was welcoming. The corridors were twisting as the hallways opened up to fountains or gardens as they lead to the rooms.
The room had lovely hardwood floors, modern fixtures and was immaculate. The modern bathroom was bright and the water pressure and temperature were delightful. This room had an attached patio with a round table with chairs under the shade of an umbrella. This patio area was complete with a wall mounted fountain for a relaxing atmosphere. As a special bonus all the items in the minibar were complementary except the alcohol. I cannot say enough about the staff of the property as they did everything to make our stay very comfortable. The hotel has a restaurant with a bar and it is highly recommended to eat and have a drink.

review_title: Step back to the elegance of the early 1900's in San Jose!
review_text:
Charm, character and elegance abound in this Victorian era hotel. This small boutique type hotel, with 17 or so unique rooms located in San Jose, will throw you back in time to the days of the sugar can plantations and Victorian Costa Rica.
My room was the most exquisite gem of a room, with an attached solarium including a little fountain, orchids and tropical plants. I have never seen anything like it, With a single queen sized bed, it would be a romantic room for two. The dark hardwood floors extended through the bathroom, which was home to an enormous soaking tub. The entire space was immaculate, and tastefully decorated. Linens were luxurious and the mattress divine!
Rooms are located on the second and third floors, and circle around an outdoor eating area. The view from the hall way to the terrace below is very european, although the Costa Rican gift for landscaping and plantings is evident.
The restaurant was simply fabulous. The food was amazing, I highly recommend the Sea Bass, or perhaps, the Salmon Nicoise. Do not skip dessert. Creme brulee rivals the competition in Charleston, SC and the coffee cream pie was worth the flight. I am going to review the restaurant separately, as it clearly warrants its own amazing review.
I would be remiss if I did not compliment the staff. Clearly, they can read minds! Gracious, warm and welcoming are the first words that come to mind. From the fresh juice at check in, to the little tasting treats at meals, the details were consistently spectacular. I was directed to the hotel after a flight cancellation, and think that my overnight stay was one of the highlights of my trip to Costa Rica. Imagine the inconvenience of a cancelled flight resulting in a most amazing experience!

review_title: Exquisite boutique hotel with incredible service and food
review_text: WE LOVED GRANO DE ORO!!! The staff warmly welcomed us upon arrival; although we arrived quite early, they checked us in and gave us a complimentary room upgrade! The room was beautifully appointed with gleaming hardwood floors, a sitting area, a comfortable bed with nice linens, and a complimentary mini bar (snacks and non-alcoholic beverages). YES! I said COMPLIMENTARY! Our room was off a small courtyard with gardens and lots of privacy. We had dinner in the Grano de ORO restaurant; the service was on point; the food was spectacular. Some may say it's pricey or expensive; it was worth every penny. 5-star dining at its best! Our breakfast at the same restaurant was also complimentary and again delicious. I highly recommend a stay here; you won't regret it!! Next time we want to splurge and get the king suite!

review_title: Wonderful old hotel with exceptional service!
review_text: We landed in San Jose and this was our first destination and overnight. We were greeted with friendly faces and a glass of fresh juice at check in. It really put is in a great mood after a long day of airports and travel. The staff was helpful and the rooms were very charming. The gift shop supports local artisans and had beautiful offerings. The staff was incredibly helpful, friendly, and proud of the country and especially the hotel. They went above and beyond to make us feel welcome. We had a phenomonal dinner at the restaurant, and an engaged, funny waiter. The dinner truly was absolutely delicious. We didn't get a chance to try the jacuzzis in the hotel, but wished we had the time. One of the rooms had a cute veranda with a fountain and beautiful bathroom. The showers were great too! We were sad to only have one night in the comfortable beds. The ceiling fans cooled off the rooms. We loved hearing the history of how the hotel came to be and enjoyed seeing old photographs of the hotel and the area in the entry hallway. An incredible breakfast was a fantastic way to start the morning and set off on our Costa Rican adventure. We can't say enough good things about this quaint hotel.

review_title: Loved this hotel and the staff!
review_text: I recently went back to San Jose to complete some dental work. I chose Grano de Oro because of its close proximity to my dentist. Upon my arrival I immediately felt at home in this former luxury tropical mansion turned hotel. I booked the standard room (which is very nice), but was upgraded to the deluxe patio room which was extremely pleasant with its own private garden and fountain. I was very impressed with the wood floors, tasteful decor, and cleanliness of the room and outdoor patio. The bed was also very comfortable with luxury linens. The staff was very friendly and the food in the restaurant superb! Having breakfast in the open air courtyard reminded me of sitting at a cafe in Europe. Should I go back to San Jose, I will stay again at this lovely hotel.

review_title: First and last time I stayed here
review_text:
I wasn't familiar with San Jose and wanted to stay in a well located hotel where we could go walking to restaurants, cafes, clubs, etc. based on the reviews I booked this hotel. However, if someone reads this review, and has the same interest I did, please don't stay here. Location is terrible. I think a hotel in Escazu is way better.
Pros:
- I can't think of one... Oh, maybe the patio at the room was nice.
Cons:
- The shuttlel from the hotel takes forever to arrive. It is not complementary.
- Hotel is waaaay overpriced
- The hotel lacks maintenance. The carpets are stained, and the whole place needs a renovation.
- The recommendations the front desk staff gave us where the bad one and the worse one...
- Location: there is literally nothing around the hotel. The Avenida Colon, is a crowed, not pretty and uninteresting one, that will take you after 30 minutes walking to the Church and Museum. But I rather stay at another hotel and take a taxi to the mUseum. No cafes, no restaurants, no shops, nada, nada. You will be trapped at Grano de Oro restaurant which is as bad as the hotel.

review_text:
This hotel is so beautiful. It truly feels like an oasis in the city. Grano de Oro has an old plantation feel with lush, tropical greenery and fountains in the courtyards.The hotel is pristinely clean and the decor is simple and beautiful.
I enjoyed the touches of fresh juice upon arrival and the fact that beverages and snacks in the room (with the exception of alcohol) were gratis!
The beds are comfortable and the bathrooms quite large with soaking style tub which can be difficult to find in hotels. Great water pressure and abundant hot water. There is also a jacuzzi on site, but we did not take advantage of this trip.
Walter and David at the front desk/concierge were quite nice and helpful to us during our stay.
This is definitely a gringo hotel experience, which was a pretty nice introduction to what we are planning to be a more rustic/Tico style vacation.
Highly recommended!!!

review_title: Nice rooms, elegant restaurant, great food
review_text:
We were met by the hotel shuttle, straight off a flight from London and were glad we’d chosen to use the shuttle as it was spacious and cool, and we were in it for a long time because the late afternoon traffic was terrible!
The room was comfortable, much as you’d expect from a boutique hotel of this type. The hotel staff were extremely friendly, from the front desk, to the waiters, though to housekeeping. We were made to feel welcomed to the hotel and to Costa Rica.
We ate in the restaurant two evenings and while it isn’t cheap, it is a very elegant room and the cooking is good. It isn’t a typical tourist restaurant: we noticed that it was used by lots of local business people and had quite a dressed-up crowd of couples on the Friday evening.
You can walk to the city centre, though you may prefer to hop into a taxi: they’re cheap and plentiful. We liked San Jose more than we were expecting to: it’s definitely a ‘real’ city – not a tourist town – and is not especially picturesque, but the museums and galleries are interesting. We especially liked the Gold Museum.
If we were back in San Jose we’d definitely make the same choice again.

review_title: Perfect start to my first visit to Costa Rica
review_text: This was a very pleasant surprise within what is an otherwise rather ordinary-looking part of San Jose. Everything about the hotel is tasteful and atmospheric, and that includes the lobby area, the elegant restaurant & bar, and the stylish guest rooms themselves. I received an enthusiastic welcome on arrival, and all staff who helped and spoke to me had clearly mastered the ideal blend of warmth & professionalism. My only regret was the fact that I was only here for one night, and with a pick-up of 06.30 am it was a rather early checkout. Don't think I could have experienced a better introduction to the country

review_text:
My wife and I stayed only two days in Grano de Oro, one day at the beginning of our trip and one day at the end of our trip. We were very impressed with the hotel, the staff was very pleasant, warm and welcoming.
The first room in which we stayed was very comfortable with a/c, free WiFi and cable TV. We later went up to the roof terrace and enjoyed the jacuzzi.
On our second stay we were upgraded to the garden suite which was bigger with access to a small garden equipped with table, chairs and a sun umbrella. A small green corner if we had enough with our luxurious room. The bathroom had a Jacuzzi which unfortunately we did not take advantage of.
The hotel restaurant is amazing. The food is delicious and the kitchen is run by a French or French schooled chef. The decor is colonial with dark wood beams that gives the place an old class sophisticated atmosphere. Try the red snapper incased in salt and the pie Grano de Oro for desert, it's amazing.
Definitely recommended
Pura Vida

review_text: This delightful small hotel in an unassuming neighborhood in San Jose is just a short walking distance from the shopping district, museums and sports arena. The staff is friendly, professional and bilingual (they even suffered my poor attempts at Spanish). The initial room we were assigned was quite pleasant but we had a small problem with it and the management immediately moved us to another room that turned out to be an upgrade to what we had booked (at no additional charge!). Very nicely done! The best part is the lovely restaurant, bar and courtyard. Check out this restaurant even if you aren't staying at the hotel (but call ahead for a reservation as they fill up fast). Service is impeccable and the food wonderful. We sat in the courtyard under an umbrella (against the possibility of a stray shower) after a drink at the bar inside (there are two sides to the bar, one inside and one out). They have a nice selection of local microbrews as well as the usual local cocktails and liquors.

review_text:
This was a planned celebratory trip for my two nieces college graduation. We bookended our coastal visit with our stay at Hotel Grano de Oro. We could not have been more pleased!! We fell in love with this carefully restored mansion, the beautiful greenery & landscaping, the interior courtyards, and the top notch professional & endearing staff. On our final stay, we upgraded to the king garden suite which was a real treat. It's worth the splurge!
Their restaurant is on premises and is superior for every meal, including room service.
Our only complaint was that we couldn't stay longer! For anyone flying into San Jose, we would MOST HIGHLY recommend a stay and a meal at Hotel Grano de Oro.
They truly provide 5 star service and amenities!

review_title: Best hotel in central San José
review_text:
Hotel Grano de Oro is a charming hotel in old colonial style. The hotel is one of the best hotels in central San José. It’s located a 10 minute walk from central avenue where “all” the main attractions are located.
There is not much to see or do in San José. Many of the guide books tells you to spend as little time as possible in San Jose, after staying there for two days we completely agree. We have travelled a lot, we usually find most places we visit interesting and appealing in their own way but that was hard in San José. I wouldn’t recommend people wasting their time visiting San José. There are too many other beautiful places in Costa Rica to visit. The best thing about San José was this hotel.
Our room was spacious and tastefully decorated. The room had a little private patio with a table and two chairs where we enjoyed a drink in the evenings. The bed was comfortable and batroom was equipped with a bathtub.
The hotel has a well-developed sustainability program with recycling, ecological cotton in bedsheets and towels, sustainability certified products etc.
The restaurant at the hotel is a French restaurant and it’s consider to be one of the best restaurants in San José. The restaurant serves a good a la carte breakfast.

review_text:
Spent one night here on arrival from London.
The courtyard rooms were off a small garden. Pleasant enough if a trifle basic but we were not in them long enough to worry about views etc. Clean and comfortable. I'm sure there are better in the main building and for a bigger price.
We enjoyed a nice dinner in the hotel restaurant. Smart, diligent and courteous waiting staff. The food was pretty good and reasonably priced at just over $100 for four including drinks.
Breakfast the next morning was a leisurely affair due to a big table getting in just ahead of us and a bunch of fellow travellers getting up even earlier than we did with some jet leg I guess. No problem though as the quality of the food and the lovely ambiance of the dining room made up for the wait.

review_text:
The Grano de Oro is a lovely hotel with a great personality - certainly not part of a chain; which is great. A variety of rooms and different layouts with courtyard areas. Small roof terrace with two jacuzzis and a restaurant on site.
Staff are friendly and helpful and will readily advise on what to do or see. Not located in the trendiest part of town but various places to eat nearby and within walking distance of the Mercado.
The restaurant has its own TA listing, but presumably covers the good hotel room service. Breakfast is a la Carte and not included - this is fine in principle but as this adds time it's not easy to have a quick breakfast if you have an early start.

review_title: Brilliant place to stay in San Jose
review_text: Most holiday information tells you to spend as little time in San Jose, capital of Costa Rica, as possible. If you stay somewhere like Grano de Oro, however, that isn't the case. Welcoming atmosphere, hot tubs on a roof garden, inner courtyard with tiled walls for breakfast and meals, and a good place to start off for walking into the city centre and places like Teatro Nacional and the Gold Museum. The building is a warren of corridors, some going through outdoor courtyards with fountains, to get to your rooms, which are thoroughly comfortable.

review_title: An oasis of good food and wine in an otherwise drab city!
review_text: We stayed three nights in the Grano de Oro, loved the hotel, the staff and most of all the restaurant! Lovely quaint rooms, ours opened on a small inner garden, fountain and well-maintained plants. After a day in San Jose, it was just great to get back to the hotel and have a cocktail in the spectacular restaurant; yet another beautiful inner garden with stained glass and interesting paintings by local artists. The hotel arranged our transportation from the airport; the staff was friendly and helpful, what more could we ask for?

review_text:
My wife and family (three children, ages 20, 26 and 28) returned to Costa Rica for two weeks for a second time to explore the country and visit with other friends who were also visiting. We used the Hotel Grano de Oro as a base, staying one night on arrival from the United States, staying again for one night a week later to greet the other arriving families, and a third time, for two days at the end to do a little exploring of San Jose before returning to the US. We picked Grano de Oro after enjoying it on our first visit six years earlier.
First the good news, and it almost entirely good new. The hotel is constructed from colonial Victorian mansions and has the very cool vibe of both modernity and turn-of-the-century colonial luxury. Every room bright and a little different. Spacious rooms and big beautiful white tile baths. Incredibly helpful and friendly staff. They helped us arrange dinner for 17 in the restaurant (more on that), held our excess luggage when we went out to the other parts of Costa Rica, handled all of the many transfers from and to the airport, etc. Couldn't be nicer or more professional. And the restaurant is one of the finest I've ever eaten in. Supposedly the best in Costa Rica, and I believe it without question. All this in a hotel at what I consider very modest prices, compared to the rest of the world.
Now the bad new, and there's very little. This is not a big, family resort with pools and the like. If you want the Hilton in Maui this isn't it. Realize that the hotel is smack in the middle of mostly uninteresting old San Jose. You'll wonder where you are when the cab pulls up to drop you off. Don't be dismayed. First, because the moment you set foot in the place you'll be delighted, and second, because if you give San Jose a day or two to explore you won't be disappointed. Now it's true that a day or two is all San Jose warrants, and Costa Rica has much else to entice outside the capital, but stay more than one night. Fact is, that if Grano de Oro was in any other city with attractions, you'd stay a month.

review_title: Gracious, Quaint Hotel With Excellent Restaurant
review_text: My husband, two teenage sons and I stayed here for four nights on the last leg of a two week tour through Costa Rica. The hotel room was the CLEANEST room I had ever stayed in. We have stayed in many a five star luxury hotel in places all around the world and this room topped them all in cleanliness. The rooms are spacious, well appointed and quiet. The front desk was very attentive if we needed anything and the restaurant was wonderful for breakfast and dinner. We were welcomed with fresh juice at check-in and plates of fresh fruit and goodies when we entered the room. Our second day we came back to find a lovely note from the manager with a bag of jams and salsas. On our last night we came back to find vouchers for free alcoholic and non alcoholic drinks at their beautiful restaurant bar. All in all a wonderful experience

review_title: Old World Style with a Modern Touch
review_text: We needed to stay one night in San Jose before flying home, and this property was recommended in lieu of a Hampton Inn. We LOVED it, from the service to the linens to the restaurant and bar, and the location. We booked a suite, our party was one couple and a single, and we had all the privacy but shared a bath. We walked several blocks to the central market, but cab service is also available. Short cab ride to the airport. We wish we could have stayed another day or two.

review_title: Lovely old hotel with excellent bar and restaurant

review_text:
My wife and I spent two weeks in Costa Rica at the end of May. The last two nights in the Hotel Grano de Oro in which we had stayed on our only other visit to Costa Rica 15 years ago.
Our stay, and the hotel, we just as wonderful as in our memory. The on premises restaurant is even better than before and has been relocated and enlarged since our last visit.
During the reservation process the General Manager, Marcos Montoya, got personally involved and arranged for us to stay in the room immediately next door to the one in which we had stayed last time. He would have seen to it that we got the exact same room had we wanted to, but we opted for a higher category room.
The room was immaculate and well appointed with a small but very private patio. It seemed to us that even though the room was immediately next to the other room in which we had stayed and backed onto the same street, the room was quieter. I'm convinced that they have replaced windows with double or triple pane but did not verify.
Arriving by car on a drizzly day, we really appreciated the valets with umbrellas on our arrival and were able to borrow umbrellas for our walks in the area.
We'll return on our next visit to Costa RIca which will hopefully be in far less than 15 years.
Only negative is that the traffic seems to have gotten two to three times worse than in 2000.

review_text: Wonderful staff, very clean facility and location is quiet and secure. Loved the quirky corridors which connect the several historic buildings which comprise the hotel. The prices in the hotel gift shop are good.

review_text:
My wife and I only spend one night in the Grano de Oro, but it lived up to its reputation. The suite was well prepared when we arrived, complete with a congratulatory note regarding our wedding. Room 31 offers a wonderful view of the city right from the jacuzzi and is private in that you have no neighboring rooms attached. The hotel decor is luxurious and the staff was always very helpful when needed. The hotel restaurant is five star quality, with the option to sit in a romantic courtyard or in an old world style restaurant setting.
I would definitely stay there should we visit San Jose again.

review_title: Above average charm below average service!
review_text:
Our trip started with a mix up regarding a transfer from the airport. We ended up just getting a taxi. The staff seemed in no hurry to step away from their desk to greet us. Not very warm or helpful. Our beefs: the free coffee in the lobby stops at 7:30..silly when you consider the price you pay. There is a little gift shop that is run by the front desk and is rarely open. It seems very unorganized. Our lunch was very good although it set us back $104 dollars with no alcohol and, again, coffee refills were not free! (we are in the Mecca of coffee..just pour it freely!)
If we would have stopped at this resort first then we wouldn't have been this underwhelmed but coming from Nayara Arenal the customer service at the Grano de Oro was lacking.

review_title: Charming hotel full of character in a bustling city
review_text:

review_text: Only stayed the one night after a tour through Costa Rica. Wanted to get a little bit away from downtown. Arrived early. This hotel is a beautiful example of an old colonial estate. The house is built around a couple of small courtyards. It just reeks of charm. Beautiful wood and glass work everywhere. The front desk said we did not have to wait until check in and that we received an upgrade. First up, the bed is the best I have ever slept in. The room was beautifully decorated, without being overdone. The basics were there. Airco worked, the was bathroom spotless and well appointed, and after a couple of weeks of poor internet, the wifi here worked perfectly. What a relief. In hindsight, I wish we had booked dinner at the restaurant, supposedly one of the best in SJ. So much character to the place. Only down side, missed any cafes of shops in the area. Would certainly go back though.

review_text:
Located a 20- minute walk from downtown, this is one of the most serviceminded hotels we've stayed at. Front desk is quick and efficient, we were upgraded and sent mail wishing us welcome before arriving.
Parking is free, and should you need transport to the airport it will be arranged for 30 Usdollars and take around half an hour.
The restaurant is one of San Jose's finest, and serves international fare with local twist.
The beds are very comfy and the rooms spacious and spread out through this previously private home.
A nice touch is that tapwater is filtered and thus drinkable

review_title: Perfect end to our journey through Costa Rica
review_text:
After all the tents and tree houses and lodges we stayed in during our tour this was a welcome touch of luxury. Beautiful hotel with old world charme and modern amenities. Small courtyards with fountains and plants and rooms grouped around them. We had booked a standard room but were upgraded and even given a fruit platter (either because it is low season or because they knew we were on our holiday trip to celebrate our 25th wedding anniversary). Room had wooden floor and access to small tripcal courtyard. Bathroom and tub and lovely smelling lotions and potions. We had dinner and various coffees in the restaurant and bar area and the food is amazing. Staff very friendly and welcoming (everbody also spoke fluent English and soem even German).
Walk to town centre in 15 min. Parking is secure and just next door.

review_text:
My wife and I stayed in this hotel on the first night of our honeymoon. After a days worth of travelling from London via Miami this hotel was a short trip from the airport which was ideal. On arrival we were warmly welcomed by the staff and served a refreshing drink and cold towel, they also knew it was our Honeymoon so had upgraded us from our standard room which was a nice surprise.
We left the hotel early the next day as the main reason for choosing it was its convenient location.
All in all, we didn't stay long enough to really enjoy the hotel but the decor of the hotel is worth a visit on its own! We did have a look around the hotel at the facilities and can say that the rooftop jacuzzi's looked great, and the bar and restaurant was very posh (maybe too posh for us middle class British folk)
Overall, would recommend staying in this hotel for a short time if like us you are in transit to another part of Costa Rica. Enjoy!

review_text: Our flight arrived in San Jose around supper time, so we splurged and stayed in the Vista De Oro Suite before heading out for the rain forest the next morning. It was a very romantic setting in a very charming hotel. I don’t know the whole story, but they have done a great job converting a grand old estate into a beautifully detailed and comfortable hotel with a tropical ambiance. The courtyard restaurant was excellent. Sometimes restaurants in Latin America try to emulate a European style and fall short—but this was the real deal and a very good French restaurant in a tropical setting. The wine list was deep with great European and South American choices. If you have business to do in San Jose, or need a place to stay before or after a flight, or just want to see the city for a few days, this is a great place to stay. The same good French restaurant served us a wonderful Tico breakfast with gallo pinto and fresh fruit the next morning, which got our next day’s journey off to a perfect start.

review_text:
Beautiful hotel. We were tired & starving when we arrived so we just dined at the restaurant. The room we were assigned to is in the second floor. After staying at Nayara, the room seemed so minuscule. But it was just right for our last night in Costa Rica before heading back to the US. They serve this really wonderful truffle that I wanted to order & take home to the US. I inquired if they would sell me some in a box but instead they gave me complimentary 6 pieces. They don't make a lot & they serve it at the restaurant.
The hotel is a good walk around San Jose & not too far to the airport. We enjoyed our last night in Costa Rica & appreciate the hospitality. Stayed June 2015.

review_text: This is a beautiful property, I loved the Victorian details throughout the hotel alongside the modern touches, particularly in the well appointed room with a very modern bathroom but with a Victorian light fixture. It really was charming! The room was large and the beds were so comfortable, it was such a welcoming, warm place to come after staying in some very rustic jungle accommodation the previous nights. The staff was wonderful and really made us feel welcome. The restaurant and courtyard was gorgeous. The hot tub deck was small but cute and quiet with comfortable lounge chairs, we read for an hour out there and felt like we were in a nice quiet little spot in an otherwise very busy city. Staying here was a treat for a milestone birthday but I would stay here again if in San Jose!

review_title: #1 Hotel! What a great place to stay!
review_text: My wife and I come to Costa Rica every year for the last 10 years. We stay in a neighborhood in Playa Bejuco, south of Jaco, with friends from the states. One couple lives there year round. We never spend any time in San Jose. It's always fly in, go to Bejuco, stay, fly home. We didn't want to be rushed on the day of our flight so we decided to try out Hotel Grano de Oro. I'm so glad we did! The hotel and staff are 5 Star. What a warm welcome! The restaurant and bar are amazing as well. What a wonderful stay in a beautiful city! I'll stay nowhere else while visiting San Jose in the future.

review_text: Clasic Hotel near downtown San Jose. The Hotel is built in a house from the 19th Century, which was adapted to be a Hotel. Rooms are not very large but nice and comfortable. I stayed in one with a small patio with a fountain and was very nice. Service is great, people is very friendly and helpfull. Its walking distance from downtown, and to the Sabana Park.The restaurant is beautiful, food is awesome, and service is great. If you want to stay near downtown this is the best choice, however I have to say that downtown San Jose was not such a nice experience. Not many things to do, crowded, and not very clean. Going in the opposite direction Sabana Park is much nicer. Costa Rica as a Country is beautiful, green all over, safe, and people very kind and nice.

review_text:
We decided to stay for two nights in San Jose after arriving from the US to get acclimated and this hotel was prefect for that purpose. We look to stay in small unique hotels and this hotel was definitely that with its historic feel and dark wood ambieance.
We had a deluxe patio room which was on the second floor in the older section of the hotel. The room had extra high ceilings and dark wood floors and trim. There was a patio off the room in the back. The patio was actually a bit unnecessary-it was a small patio designed to feel like a garden that was totally enclosed with a skylight on top but since it was very hot when we visited, we relaxed in the room with the A/C going.
The hotel appears to be a bunch of different building which are connected with a maze of hallways which lead to rooms facing open air courtyard gardens.
We ate breakfast and dinner in the hotel restaurant which was very elegant and also had an open air courtyard where we had our breakfasts. The food was good and so was the service. San Jose is a gritty city and the hotel is about a half hour walk to the center of the city where the main museums and the historic theater are located.

review_text: The hotel is lovely but we had bugs in both of our rooms. We picked this hotel because of other ratings and because it looked like the nicest hotel in San Jose. The lobby and staff were great but the rooms have bugs. We checked into our garden room and quickly began seeing little black bugs flying around. After getting several bites I called the front desk and they were great, upgraded us to a garden suite. Their intentions were good and the room was lovely but there was a large roach in the bathtub!! I was unable to sleep because I was so creeped out. They need to have screens put on the windows or the staff should not leave the windows open. I do not expect bugs in a hotel of this quality and this price.

We were only staying for one night whilst transiting to Tortuguero. We had a very qiuiet room with nearby access to the roof terrace where a couple of hot tubs relaxed some very stiff joints and muscles.
Our room had everything we required, safe, coffee, WIfi, shower etc.Tv if we wanted it.
The hotel decor is super, Lots of plants, pictures and old photos of San Jose.
The restaurant and bar is exceptional. A beautiful use of local timbers.
The menu varied and local produce figures strongly. A wonderful meal.
I would say that prices are similar to London.

review_title: Beautiful Rooms, Not So Great Location
review_text:
We stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro for one night on our way out of Costa Rica. We were looking for a luxurious hotel and restaurant for our last night and found it at this hotel.
The Hotel: A beautiful hotel and restaurant! We received a welcome drink when we arrived, and were told about the various services the hotel provides. We were also informed that we were upgraded to a Garden Suite upon arrival, so that was a nice surprise. There's a restaurant and a gift shop with a little something for everyone. Surprisingly, the hotel is not in the best part of town. We walked to the ATM and noticed that all hotels had armed security guards in front of them, and a lot of homes had barbed wire atop their fences surrounding the home. While the hotel is safe (it has security), the area is not one to venture too far out. There is a jacuzzi terrace, but it's not much to keep you entertained for long.
The Room: Our room, number 9, was a garden suite and was extremely luxurious and well appointed. The bed was super comfortable and the sitting area and patio were nice touches. The tub is large enough for a bath. WiFi was fairly good, although a little slow at times it was able to keep up with Face Time as needed. Mini bar and coffee maker in the room. If you can splurge for the garden suite, I highly recommend it!
The Restaurant: We read that we should dress nicely for dinner, but at lunch as well (we appeared to be under-dressed). Lunch was good, we had the beef tenderloin sandwich. For dinner we had steak and the red snapper, which were good but not the best we have had. Beautiful restaurant, though.
Overall: The hotel is too nice to pass up due to the area. I do recommend this hotel, but only if you plan to stay overnight only and not for more than a day or so.

The staff was friendly and attentive.

review_text:
We were a family group of 6 and had reserved 2 rooms at the end of our holiday in Costa Rica. One of our rooms was upgraded from the Deluxe 2 Beds to a lovely Family Suite with 2 bedrooms! Our other room was a Superior Room. Both were decorated beautifully and the beds were very comfortable. We were greeted by friendly and extremely helpful staff at the reception desk. They helped book a tour for us to La Paz Waterfall Gardens and also printed off our boarding passes for our flights. The front desk kindly phoned our previous hotel as we had forgot to return an ornate room key. We were instructed to leave the key with them and someone would come pick it up when they came to town. That took the stress out of trying to mail it back ourselves!! We made good use of the (very hot!) rooftop hot tubs and loungers.
The Restaurante Grano de Oro was fine dining at its best and seating was full, so reservations are recommended! We were given a complimentary creamy soup with scallops bits in it. Everything we ordered was done to perfection and delicious! The breakfast was also great! Thank you for a memorable stay and welcoming us with such warmth!

review_title: Classy hotel with excellent customer service restaurant
review_text: This is where we started our vacation to Costa Rica. It got our vacation off to a wonderful start. Unfortunately we did not spend much time here because we got in late, and had to hit the road in the morning, but the interaction we did have was great. The staff was very polite and helpful, even though we got in around midnight. They had made reservations for us at their restaurant, but since we did not make it in time, they had a plate of fruit in our room waiting for us! We had a delicious breakfast in the morning with very good coffee and fruit smoothies. This is definitely a great place to stay if you are in the San Jose area.

review_text:
California to Costa Rica....
When researching flights to get in and out of Costa Rica, you will find that available flight times, price and convenience don't always go together, especially if you are traveling outside of the city San Jose. Therefore, you will require possible before, and after stays in San Jose, prior to catching a morning flight out.. With that being said:
Took the Red Eye out of California Wednesday night, cheaper and you arrive in San Jose at around 9:00 am the following day. We chose the Hotel Grano de San Jose to stay on our arrival portion.. WOW!!! what a great Hotel..
I had called them on making the reservation to see if we could get at least one of our three reserved rooms available on arrival, seeing as we just flew all night, and would possibly be needing food, and a little nap.. Technically, check-in is at 3:00 pm.. Paublo, made it happen!! when we arrived, we immediately were treated like VIP, and were greeted with a cold refreshing beverage in the lobby, and escorted to our rooms, and the rooms were wonderful. The beds were big, and so comfortable, and included all in room amenities you could ever require.
After changing clothes, we went to the Hotel restaurant, for an absolutely delicious breakfast. We had pre-scheduled appointments for a massage at their spa, so decided to hang out by their quaint terrace Hot Tubs, and just relax and enjoy the amazing hospitality that this Hotel offers.
Later, we decided to yet again go down to the Hotel Bar and Restaurant for cocktails, then appetizers, then Dinner...which was all so delicious, we just stayed and enjoyed..
When we booked this Hotel, the idea was to walk around town and enjoy San Jose before catching a flight out to Manual Antonio the next, but much to our surprise...We never found a reason to leave this Hotel..... It was absolutely perfect!!
Thank You Paublo, and all your staff, including the Spa and Restaurant for such a fantastic start to our unforgettable trip to Costa Rica..
Just on a side note, the Hotel while not far in distance from the Airport, does have some traffic getting to and from the Airport. Give yourself plenty of travel time. Paublo can help you with your transfer, and ensure your transfers go smooth.

review_title: A TRULY SPLENDID PLACE TO STAY IN SAN JOSE
review_text: We chose this hotel because it was reputed to be lovely and quiet, and both are absolutely true. It is about 2/3 mile from the city center, an easy walk, but avoids all of the hubbub of being in that area. The hotel itself is an inspired architectural feat of building a beautiful hotel within an old hacienda, preserving some interior patio spaces so that all rooms feel as though there is an outdoors close by. The rooms are nice, large, clean, and with good beds. The staff is absolutely the best you can imagine, fluent in English, kind and utterly helpful in every way. There is one of the finest restaurants in San Jose within, and a lovely gift shop as well. On the roof are two Jacuzzi tubs, and a fine massage therapist is available on short notice for brief stopovers between other destinations in Costa Rica. We came and went there three times, the staff remembered us and gave us the same room and put our friends next door, which we thought was unusually thoughtful. The food truly was amazing and we kept coming back for more of it. This is a hotel which we will use if we ever return to lovely Costa Rica.

review_text: This hotel was perfect for our stay in San Jose. We were only there 2 days before jetting off to the first stop on this jungle adventure ride but it seems like the nicest place around. While the hotel is lovely, the area is nothing special and I thought it was odd that the rooms don't have a double bed option. Just a full size in each, which is fine but as some non-couple pairs we likely would have requested it if he option was available. The dinner at the restaurant was delicious and the staff are so friendly/helpful. Food was great and breakfast was even better! There are no screens on the Windows but also haven't seen a mosquitos. The AC works great to keep bugs away and me to stay cool! Safes in the room and hot tubs on the roof. Would stay here agin if on the way somewhere but doesn't seem like a destination.

review_text: We have just visited for a night and had a great stay. The hotel has a colonial feel to it - quiet, well laid out and great to wander around in. The staff were welcoming and helpful (though we had to wait for 15 mins for our room to be ready despite sending 2 emails to say we would be arriving at 3pm). We had a Garden Room which was wonderful - wood paneling, great bathroom, space to relax in and small outside space that was perfect for a bit of fresh air. It's not close to be center (about a mile away before you get to the incredible hustle and bustle of San Jose) but it's an interesting walk! This was a lovely oasis in a busy city.

review_text: After a 21 hour journey from the UK it was very pleasant to stay in the Grano de Oro for a couple of nights.The hotel is "colonial" in style with nice rooms and shady passageways. Our room (deluxe double) was comfortable and clean with a good bathroom. The main restaurant was both in an open courtyard but you could also sit inside if you wanted too. The internet service was excellent (FOC) though you did need a password to log on. This was the only place in Costa Rica where we did need a password. Staff were helpful and courteous at all times.

review_title: Amazing place to stay in San Jose as your starting/ending point
review_text: Hotel is amazing and upscale. Restaurant is great. We used it as the first night stay and last night stay in costa Rica since its only 15km from the airport. we had a rental car and drove around the country the rest of our time. This place was so upscale and nice. Food at the restaurant was awesome, you don't even need to leave the place. they exchange dollars for colones also, so you don't even need to go to a bank. If you have a rental car, they have a private, gated in lot so your car is safe. I would highly recommend this place to anybody that needs to stay in San Jose. Top notch all the way. Staff is so friendly also.

review_title: An Experience not just a Hotel
review_text:
This is by far the best hotel option in San Jose, Costa Rica. It is a lovely hotel with history and elegance. There is no other hotel like this one in Costa Rica. The combination between the classic elements and the new modern design is just stunning. Even the outside area of the hotel, you just know right there, you have entered a great unique property. Customer service is over the top at Grano de Oro, the welcome cocktail was delicious and colorful. At our room, they had some fresh delicious tropical fruits waiting for us. What a nice gift. Perfectly placed on our cute little table in our room.
The rooms are just neat. Really, they are just neat and perfectly arranged for every guest to have a great time. I mean really, the rooms are just cozy, elegant, super comfortable beds, nice amenities. We just love sleeping in Grano de Oro. We took our time to enjoy the nice deck with jacuzzis. It is a great area to relax, enjoy the weather in Costa Rica, it was nice beautiful evening/ night weather. We had some wine as well there. What a treat. One of the highlights of the hotel is the restaurant, it is for sure the best one in the capital. Nobody can´t deny this part. It is amazing, over the top experience. The pejibaje soup it is worth trying. It´s just rich in flavor. You won't find anything like this anywhere else. Please, ask for the pejibaye soup. And the plate of cheeses is amazing as well. Very unique selection. The snock is to die for. A very fine selection for sure. Not to mention how adorable the scenary is. I just adored the restaurant. You can spend hours in there. It is magnificent. Eggs benedict in the morning are a must for breakfast. The best I´ve ever had in my life. There are many hotels in San Jose, but there is only one like Grano de Oro. This is a hotel for those looking to enjoy their stay in the best way possible, really! You just can´t go wrong with Grano de Oro hotel. This is hotel without an elevator, it is hotel with history, ambiance, romance, it is place that makes you feel comfortable and welcome like any other hotel.
Just over the top experience!

review_title: A jewel in an otherwise unremarkable town
review_text:
A great hotel. The room was first rate (we had #9, what used to be the library, apparently), reception was prompt and helpful with excellent English. We got there early and snagged parking right beside the hotel which was supervised by two guards 24 hours a day. Very convenient and very safe.
The restaurant was excellent, with a good range of choices and obviously also a popular place for locals. Prices were a bit on the high side, but nothing out of the ordinary for a very classy hotel.
A small boutique hotel, very popular, the only minor, but very understandable inconvenience as that the noon checkout time was rigidly adhered to - we had a 6 pm flight out so we were very early!
San Jose the town, however is itself an unremarkable commercial city with little to redeem it. If you need to stay somewhere, then this hotel is the place to be.

review_title: Cozy room in a charming building; good choice for a layover in San Jose
review_text:
I stayed here, traveling with husband and young son, for one night en route to the Nicoya Peninsula. We arrived very late on a Friday night and left at checkout time the next day. We enjoyed a tasty breakfast in the beautiful dining room, and the staff were helpful in accommodating our late arrival. They had some food and beverages that i had pre-ordered waiting for us in our room.
The hotel has an ingenious design, with most rooms facing an inner courtyard area, a good idea as the surrounding streets are fairly drab. A consequence of this design, however, is that rooms are somewhat dark and windows face into the corridors so you are more likely to hear noise from guests passing by than in a more typical hotel.
Our room was well-appointed, if somewhat small, with 2 very comfortable queen beds. The hotel is located near SJ's fruit and vegetable market. We appreciated the opportunity to stock up on fresh local produce on our way to our rental house in Nicoya.
The restaurant is beautiful. I would highly recommend eating at least one meal there if you are staying in the hotel.

review_text:
We stayed here twice on our trip. The front desk service is nice, with a fruit drink at arrival. The hotel was decorated for Christmas - very pretty. The rooms are nice, although on the smaller side (we had standard rooms). All hallways open to the outside, which we didn't realize in our second room. It turned out the window was open but we were using some A/C, and we heard noise from the hallway. it looks like a nice, inn hallway - no idea it was open air! Wish they would have mentioned that when we called about the noise.
Linens were very nice. The beds were on the hard side.
In being in the city, we did not walk around outside the hotel. Instead, we stayed in for dinner and breakfasts at the onsite restaurant, which is very high end. Dinner is expensive; breakfast reasonable. Both worth it.

review_text: The 'Golden Bean' - referring to the coffee bean which made so many Costa Ricans rich - has around 40 rooms, but you'd never know. It feels like a family home, exquisitely furnished and well maintained. Our standard room was one of four in a courtyard of lush tropical plants. It was comfortable and cool, with a large double bed. Toiletries were sparse, but there was a bath to sloth one's aching feet after a day trudging round the capital. Meals are taken in a charming courtyard, with very good food and lovely service. Check in was first class, and they will store your bags for you if you're going out before or after check in/check out. Breakfast was excellent, and included in our room rate. The house is located about 20 minutes walk from the centre of town, with the last 10 minutes being along a pedestrianised avenue. The city is rather a dump, like a giant Poundland. In daytime it felt sort of safe, but one carefully guarded one's possessions from a constant stream (on a busy Saturday afternoon) of some fairly sinister looking characters. We took dinner at the hotel, which was superb, and frequented by many locals. We visited the very interesting and well-designed Jade Museum, but ran out of time to try the Gold Museum. The much-touted major public buildings aren't up to much. Taxis are easily found in downtown - red and white - and will efficiently take you home for $5 (agree the rate in advance). Grano de Oro is not a luxury hotel, but top class and it's probably better to stay slightly out of the noisy and dilapidated town centre.

review_text: We arrived late at San Jose after very arduous multi sector flights. This hotel was a true gem. We thoroughly enjoyed our room, the staff were extremely friendly and helpful and, well the dining room, that was something to just sit back and soak up the ambience before even ordering anything. The meals were very well presented and tasted every bit as good. We had also had booked for the following day and we were really pleased that we had as the hotel had a very cosy and comfortable feel to it. Outside the hotel it is just 'the city streets of San Jose' but within this sanctum we felt as if we were in our own 'cocooned special place' giving us a very comfortable and content feeling.
