review_title: Good, but not as great as guidebook said it would be
review_text: Feel is historic, colonial period which keeps it from being a generic hotel. Stayed two separate nights spread over one week. They kept a bag for me while I traveled. And did not charge me until I checked out the second time. All of this was handled by a very adept and friendly front desk staff. First night in room 7 was cool. Nice big room, very clean, big bathroom. Since the room had no window they had created an enclosed balcony with glass ceiling, complete with plants and a water feature. See picture. Really cool. Second night in room 125 was a let down. Room was pretty generic with very few, easy to reach, power outlets. I did not care for the restaurant - too slow, stuffy, and the food was mediocre at best. I will send a detailed review of that separately.

review_text:
We stayed at this hotel at the beginning of our trip to Costa Rica for two nights. We took a pre-arranged cab ride from the airport.
The hotel is beautiful and felt true to their culture (not a typical american transplant). We didn't eat at the restaurant because it was so expensive.
After checking in, we were escorted to our room which was down a hallway then in an open air court. There was a beautiful water fountain in the middle of the court.
We entered the room, on the bottom floor, and we had a lovely patio with two chairs and a small table where we enjoyed our breakfast.
One of the nights, we ventured out into the city and ate at a local restaurant. The restaurant, who's name I can't recall, reminded me of a Jonny Rockets. The waiter did not speak English nor was the menu available in English. I know a little Spanish and we were able to order what I hoped was a chicken dish and milk shakes. The food was really good, though I'm still not entirely sure what we ate.
The second night we ate at Restaurante Mirador Tiquicia, which is a mountain top restaurant that overlooks San Jose. It's a buffet with a show. Food was good, but typical of Costa Rican cuisine (rice, beans, plantains, etc.).
After we left the hotel to move to the next city, I realized I left my hair straightener at the hotel. The hotel packaged and mailed it back to my house in PA and charged my credit card at my request (cheaper than buying a new one). Great customer service.
Oh, and free wi-fi.

review_title: Stunning Hotel in the Centre of San Jose
review_text:
This was our first hotel at the start of our honeymoon in Costa Rica and wow! It's just elegant and stylish and contemporary from the moment you walk in, with a huge, spacious, glass.-fronted reception area. It is a converted Victorian-style townhouse / mansion, with spacious modern rooms and an excellent restaurant, serving highly-rated food (reservations recommended!). The decor as you walk around is fantastic, with open courtyards with fountains (i.e just outside your room!) to sweeping stairs and bookcases. There was also a roof terrace with loungers and jacuzzis although we didn't get the chance to try this due to the weather.
The staff were also exceedingly helpful, which helped to make this a truly great experience. They arranged airport transfers, called ahead to book a taxi in spanish at our next destination, pointed us in the right direction for buying rubber boots (I know, random, but we were going to the jungle next!) and best of all gave us a free upgrade due to our honeymoon. What more could we ask for?!
The only downside for me was that breakfast was not included in the price for our room and I felt it was a bit expensive. But then again, the centre of San Jose is only 15 minutes away on foot so it would be easy enough to go somewhere local and cheaper, should this be an issue.

The hotels restaurant is excellent; great food, great atmosphere and an awesome wine list. This hotel has everything you need in house ... don't go out and wonder around this city ..
Although it's not a good area, that would not deter me from staying at the Hotel Grano de Oro when passing through San Jose again.

review_text: We booked three nights at Grano De Oro, where we started our tour of Costa Rica. We arrived on sep, 7th late evening quite exhausted from USA on a connection flight from Europe (door to door 22h). A warm welcome from the hotel staff a refreshing drink offered and a few minutes after we were already "singing under the shower" and finally sleeping, as on the next day we had a planned tour to Braulio Carrillo's national park. At Grano de Oro we settled for three days in a very cosy and reasonable sized patio room, without windows but which opens on a private garden with fountain (see enclosed photos for reference). The hotel is indeed an elegant sanctuary to shelter from the busy San Jose town (as a side note San Jose at 06:30 AM is as busy already as many european cities typically are at 10:00 AM). The center of San Jose can easily be reached in 20 - 25 min walking down Paseo Colon (notice that it is unsafe to walk around at night, tough). Breakfast is served à la carte at the restaurant, portions are generous and the colonial setting (both in the open internal courtyard or inside), is beautiful and really elegant. We had dinner at the restaurant on day 2 and enjoyed it. Cuisine is a merge between Costa Rican tropical and European, the atmosphere is elegant, service is good, staff kind, friendly and mostly attentive. On day 3 we ventured to dine a few blocks away at restaurant Machu Picchu which serves peruvian dishes, definitively worth a try. PS: as I forgot to bring a European/US-style power adaptor for shaver and camera I was able to buy one for 2 USD at the hotel front desk. During our stay we took advantage of the hotel's laundry which offers daily clean/dry service at very reasonable rates. PPS: make sure to find some time to rest in the hot jacuzzi on the roof terrace!

review_text:
My wife and I stayed here on the last night of our trip. The hotel was nice and the restaurant was very good, but overall we weren't impressed. Our room wasn't ready when we got there so they switched us to another. Would have been fine, but we saw our original room and it looked much bigger then where we ended up. Also, we were there on a Sunday and apparently the spa is closed on Sundays, which nobody ever mentioned. They were nice enough to give us the name of another hotel with a spa, but it was inconvenient to have to take a cab there and back.
Overall it wasn't a terrible experience, and I might stay here again for a night if I'm in San Jose, but I'd probably see what else was out there first.

review_text:
Stayed here for two nights early September. Had arranged airport transfer, that was perfect, and the arrival was a wonderful experience, welcome drinks, smiling faces, beautiful property. We had a suite (#9) which was just delightful, with a private small garden in the back, with a table and chairs, very charming, very quiet, very private. We had dinner at the hotel restaurant (which I normally try to avoid) due to the reviews, and we were not disappointed, the courtyard dinner was just wonderful, I just can't find anything negative to comment on.
Location is good, we walked to the Nuestra Tierra Restaurant / Museo de Oro Precolombino / Calle Central area, be aware that it is a good 30 / 40 minute walk, and can be intimidating at times if you are not used to Latin America. Absolutely not recommended to walk around after dark however.
Breakfast was also very nice, no buffet available, has to be ordered a la carte, but savoury and plentiful.
Definitely the place to stay downtown, I agree.

review_title: The place to stay when in San Jose!
review_text:
We really enjoyed our stay at Hotel Grano de Oro.
A 'boutique hotel', just a 15 minutes walk from city center, with probably the best restaurant in town, nice rooms (our had even a small private garden....), a very efficient and professional staff, and an extremely pleasant 'jacuzzi' space on the roof.
Free wi-fi, of course.
We received a free upgrade, on our second night at the hotel.
Forget big hotel chains, which are all the same in NY, Rome or Beijing...this is definitely the place to stay, when in San Jose.

review_text:
We stayed here for one night in the Vista De Oro Suite. The room still seemed to have most of the charming features of the original master bedroom that was once a part of an old mansion, which we loved. We enjoyed the views from this room as it overlooked the city as well as 3 volcanoes in the distance. The bed was comfortable and the room was large. The bathroom was a little small, but it suited our needs as we were only there for one night. The jacuzzi tub was large and had views of the city too.
As we were checking into the hotel, they gave my husband and I each a champagne glass of fruit juice which was a nice touch. The people at the front desk were very welcoming and helpful. The bell hop took our luggage to our room and told us a little history of the hotel which we enjoyed. I think because we booked this hotel through a deal with trip adviser, we received a gift from the hotel, which was a nice touch - bag of coffee, coffee mug, post card, and a handwritten note addressed to us thanking us for staying at the hotel (they scored big points with us by giving us a handwritten note).
We ate at the restaurant at the hotel for dinner. The food was good and we liked our table where we sat inside and looked out of the open window into the pretty courtyard.

review_text:
We stayed here three nights in a standard room for $140. It was great, the price was good, service was amazing. The room was very clean and well taken care of. The staff were extremely helpful and the place had extra amenities like computers for guest use. They even stored our bags for us free of charge while we were in the jungle for a week. The water from the tap is good to drink (important and money saving).
The restaurant was good. We had heard so many reviews saying it was amazing so maybe our expectations were too high (my husband also worked in fine dining for years), the food was good and presentation beautiful but I didn't think it was necessarily, "out of this world". This being said, I do still recommend that you eat there, it is very good, just not the best I have ever had good, like I have heard others say.
Overall: if you are going to San Jose, this is the place to stay without a doubt. So happy we found this place and look forward to returning one day.

review_title: Top boutique hotel in San Jose, CR
review_text: This is a superb boutique hotel with very few faults. The building is beautiful both inside and out. When we arrived late in the evening, the reception check-in guy was not in uniform: he had a zipped up sweater which was unprofessional given all other staff we saw during our stay were in uniform. The room was not huge but very adequate with a lovely open air but private garden courtyard. We actually kept the door open all night with ceiling fans running which was lovely. The room was spotless and also had 'green' features such as recycling bins, etc. The shampoo, soap, etc is in a dispenser on the wall in the shower. I understand the whole recycling thing and support not using unnecessary plastic but perhaps the dispenser could be nicer reflecting the rest of the aesthetic features of the hotel. Breakfast was superb with an a la carte menu, fresh juice and great coffee (of course!!). We also had dinner in the hotel restaurant which is rated one of the best restaurants in San Jose. It was amazing - beautifully executed, top quality ingredients and great service. The only criticism is that the waiter evidently did not know a lot about the wine list and should have sent over the sommelier (and we should have asked). The sommelier did later take us down to the wine cellar and showed us around the highly rated wine cellar. A great night - and we just had to go upstairs to bed! The city centre is about 10-15 minutes walk away and we had an enjoyable time taking a guided tour of the Grand Theatre (beautiful), exploring the Central Market (fun!) and visiting the Gold Museum (excellent and informative). Back at the hotel, we had a jacuzzi one afternoon which was really nice. The temperature had dropped so getting into a warm jacuzzi was really great but not sure that I would want to get in when it is really hot and humid. Perhaps they could get a small cool plunge pool. In any case, this hotel was amazing and I would highly recommend it! Stay at Hotel Grano de Oro if you can!

review_title: Great Service at a Beautiful Boutique Hotel
review_text:
We stayed here for just one night prior to being picked up to head to tortuguero the next day. The staff was extremely friendly, upgraded our room due to our honeymoon, and gave us a quick run down of the facilities.
The room we were upgraded to had a beautiful bathroom and our own little backyard area with a fountain. It rained for the entire time we were there so unfortunately we didn't get to use the two hot tubs on the second floor.
We didn't venture out of the hotel because we got there so late. From what I could see during the taxi ride over from the airport (which cost about $25) San Jose is not a city in the American sense but if there is a downtown area it did not appear to be near the hotel.

review_text:
It was so nice to arrive at the Hotel Grano de Oro after 10 days in the jungle and a day of white water rafting. We had our share of insects and bugs, especially at our last hotel in the La Fortuna area. The grounds were so beautiful with folliage everywhere you walk in the courtyards. Although we were near the city center, it seemed we were in the middle of the jungle, but a clean, luxurious jungle. The interior of the hotel was equally charming and exquisitely decorated. After many days together, 2 of our boys were fighting and didn't want to share beds. The hotel happily provided us with a rollaway bed, free of charge and had it set up within 10 minutes of requesting it.
We ate dinner at the restaurant which was expensive, but delicious. It was pricey for a family of 8, but worth the experience and convenience, especially since it was our last night in Costa Rica. The next time we come to Costa Rica, I will definitely make sure we stay longer at the Hotel Grano de Oro.

review_text:
This is a beautiful and peaceful hotel in a residential area of San Jose. Relatively close to the airport and downtown attractions.
Excellent customer service! All of the staff were very professional, friendly and always willing to help out. We actually stayed here twice during our recent visit to Costa Rica. It was very helpful to be able to leave some of our luggage at the hotel while we went to other areas of Costa Rica for a few days.
Rooms - beautifully decorated, cozy, impeccably clean and very quiet. The room also had a safe which was a plus for storing valuables.
Rooftop jacuzzi - nice and relaxing
Restaurant - gorgeous!! especially the open patio area. Plus the food was outstanding! Don't miss this dining experience.
Wifi - free and always had a good connection
Kudos for their conservation and green efforts! Keep up the good work.

review_text:
The Grano de Oro is an elegantly appointed and quite charming small hotel located in the heart of San Jose. I have stayed there on four occasions. The rooms are tastefully done and many of them have attached gardens containing a functioning fountain. There is no ceiling over the garden, in effect it acts as your window. The garden and room are separated by a glass door and wall. If the sound of running water is not your cup of tea you need only flip a switch to turn the fountain off. The resulting silence is only broken by muted traffic noise. The restaurant and bar are beautifully appointed and the service is excellent. Presentation at breakfast, lunch and dinner is done in a professional and stealth-like manner. Nothing is hurried but one is not left waiting either. It’s a very enjoyable experience.
The lobby is visually pleasing. Walking from there through the maze of hallways and staircases to one’s room is reminiscent of being in a very large mansion.
The old airport, now a park with a soccer stadium at one end, is only a few blocks away. Lots of stores and fast food places line the avenue to the park. It is a busy street with lots of people waiting for buses or walking with purpose. I had no trouble walking around the area during the day. Travel time to the airport is about 30 minutes by cab.

review_text: We spent one night here and had a fantastic experience. Hotel staff greeted us out front and signaled ahead to the check in staff. We were greeted with fresh wash cloths and juice on check in. Excellent service, wonderful room with a very comfortable bed. We had a ground floor room off the fountain courtyard. We loved the charm, but we also loved how close the hotel was to the center of town. We enjoyed walking down the Avenida Central to the mercado. Had dinner in the restaurant. Our server was a bit stiff/quiet at first, but eventually opened up and we had a fabulous experience. The brulee cheese appetizer was simply scrumptious. We had a great night of sleep after soaking in the roof top jacuzzis before bed. I wish we'd stayed here again on our last night returning to San Jose. We just loved the boutique feel of the hotel and the friendly, welcoming staff.

review_text: Probably a 20/30 minute drive from the airport to town. We only had one night at the hotel and once we got there it was so nice that we decided not to go out and to make the most of the hotel instead. We had lunch there as the dinning area is beautiful, they have a great menu, and the meals were delicious. Our room looked out onto a small garden so you don't feel like you're in the city at all. We had to leave early so didn't get to experience their breakfast but the coffee station was up and running with takeaway mugs. If we return to Costa Rica, I would certaintly stay there again.

review_text:
check in was a breeze lovely smiles and a cool drink. The room was excellent, beautiful bathroom and wonderful court yard with a bubbling fountain.
The staff were courteous and professional.
We booked for the restaurant in the hotel and was expecting something special as we have travelled from NZ and had read many reviews.
Alas we were given a table in the courtyard with an oversized umbrella covering our table. We asked if the wait staff could remove the umbrella and we were told it was there in case it rained.
We eventually got it moved and saw above a lovely starry night.
The food was top marks delicious.
Our only problem was the moment we had finished our first course it was whisked away and replaced with our next course, so we had no time to sit back and relax and digest our first course.
The wait staff seemed to want us out of there as soon as possible and for a restaurant of high esteem, I had to ask for cracked pepper. I know I am being picky, but when you pay high prices you expect Grano service.
Again wonderful hotel will stay again and again
cheers

review_title: A wonderful little oasis in San Jose
review_text:
We stayed 2 nights with our family. The city of San Jose is very nice, but there is very little to do and it feels a little unsafe after dark. I think the government could spend a little time cleaning up the public areas in the city and making it a little more tourist friendly.
The hotel on the other hand is first class. Wonderful service and fine dining at a reasonable price. The open air part of the restaurant was a
little oasis in the city!

review_text: We stayed here one night before leaving. Room was very clean, bed was super comfy. Did not like the location of our room though. Right outside the roof top Jacuzzi. Ate at the restaurant. Don't waste your time. This is supposed to be known for great service and food, we did not have great service, or food. Waiter was so rushed with us. I even mentioned to him, I feel like you are in a hurry. He took silverware off the table and we weren't even done using. I was extremely disappointed in the service. The food was not all that. Stuff came out cold and undercooked. Water glasses left emptied- total shame. This could be something. They need bus boys to help clear tables. Venture out down town to eat, I'm sure the service/food would better.

review_text: We stayed one night in this hotel before leaving Costo Rica in order to get a taste of the capital city. The hotel was a perfect choice based on location, service, comfort, and food. The staff were wonderful in planing our afternoon walk to the gold museum and to the park where the World Cup was being show on a monster TV screen to 10,000 people. We could not have planned our visit better. We saw the country so engaged in the World Cup. Most people in the city wore red shirts supporting the team. Before we left the next day, the van driver from the hotel took us into the city to buy team shirts for our grandchildren. This was not an easy task but he was very helpful and patient. The food in the restaurant was delicious. Our waiter for dinner was not very friendly or attentive which was the only negative experience during our stay. All the other staff were outstanding. The gift shop has beautiful locally made crafts. Our room was perfect, comfortable, quiet and in pristine condition. As was the bathroom. This was a great place to end out ten days in Costa Rica.

review_text: My family and I stayed one night at the Hotel Grano De Oro prior to leaving for the airport the following morning. I wish we would have stayed longer. The rooms are simple, yet luxurious with all the amenities required. Our rooms opened up to a garden atrium. Stunning! The staff is so very attentive and accommodating. The restaurant is very elegant and all of the meals are absolutely delicious. If traveling through or staying in San Jose, I definitely recommend a stay at the Hotel Grano de Oro. There are five other boutique hotels that are in partnership with Hotel Grano throughout Costa Rica. If I return to Costa Rica, I would love to stay at one of these boutique hotels.

review_title: Perfect hotel in central San Jose
review_text:
This hotel was absolutely fantastic.! We stayed in the hotel for 11 days and had nothing but perfect service from the time of arrival. When we arrived at the hotel we were greeted with a fresh glass of fruit juice, smiles and perfect service.
The entire staff at this hotel are exceptional. From the room service, to the bell men, to the concierge, to the front desk, to the maid service. I'm not sure who trained the staff but they should offer their services to other hotels as well.
The restaurant food was exceptional. Even if you don't stay here at the Gran de Oro stop by and eat at their restaurant. It's the best food we had during our time here in Costa Rica.
I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone that wants to stay in San Jose and travel to visit other daily destinations.

review_text:
This was the first hotel we stayed at as a part of our honeymoon in May 2014. This was a great hotel in downtown San Jose. You might think that it would be loud and hear a lot of car traffic considering it's location to a major road but inside the room you do not hear it. Our room was very clean and the perfect size. The staff were very helpful in setting up excursions or just trying to get around the city. They will also hold your bags if you have overnight excursions but plan to return to the hotel.

review_title: Liked it so much we added a night
review_text:
We booked a room on both bookends of our trip, on the recommendations of two friends, as we flew in and out of San Jose. I am so glad we listened to them!
What a gorgeous entrance to the hotel. We were greeted warmly outside, and were given assistance carrying our bags into the lobby, and eventually to our room. The front desk personnel are great, and we were given a delicious juice in a champagne flute. Nice touch! The personnel speak English very well, but I chose to speak in Spanish to practice up a bit since we were in a Spanish speaking country.
The room was fantastic! We had the garden view room for our first night as the deluxe patio room was not available. It was a great room, large, big bathroom and very comfortable. The view of the garden was very nice and we slept with the windows open, and it was so quiet.
Where we stayed on the Caribbean side of Costa Rica once we left San Jose could not even compare to the Hotel Grano de Oro, and we longed to be back every night. We decided to leave our place in Puerto Viejo one day early and head back to San Jose so we could finish our trip by once again staying in a grand hotel.
This time, the deluxe patio room was available, and it was even better than the garden room. Loved the private patio with bubbling fountain, very large room, and huge bathroom.
The food is excellent! We had 1 breakfast, and 3 dinners over the course of our stays. Service is very good, and the ambience is very relaxing. We sat out on the patio for all of our meals, even once while it was raining.
Some of the amenities in the rooms:
Great wifi
Shampoo, conditioner and body gel provided
In room coffee/ tea
Flat screen TV
Mini bar
Safe
Very comfortable beds

review_text: The accommodations were excellent! The beds were soft, the room was clean, and the staff attentive. The ambiance of the corridors was inviting and quaint. We ate at the restaurant for dinner and they had our reservation down for the wrong night. They scrambled and seated us, but not in the courtyard as we had requested, so we were disappointed with our location in the dining room. The food was okay, but I thought it could have been seasoned better. We also lost our server midway through our dinner with no explanation. I guess he got ill, but the replacement was just as attentive. We arrived on a Saturday and left the next day, so it is hard to say what the neighborhood was like during the work week, but we did walk to the Gold Museum and ate lunch out and felt safe in going to and from which was quite a bit away.

Excellent drink menu as well, and they even offer a few local craft beers, a rarity in the city, as well as the country.

review_text: We stayed here on our first and last night of our Costa Rican trip. Wonderful, fabulous, beautiful. We were greeted by handsome and charming David upon our arrival and served a wonderfully cold pineapple cocktail. Our room (same room on first night and last night), was spacious, elegantly furnished and had an outdoor patio with plants and a fountain. The restaurant and bar was one of the best. Enjoyed drinks on the patio outside of dining room and then dinner both nights and breakfast was sooooo good! This hotel has a great staff both in the hotel and in the restaurant. The wait staff was very efficient when informed we needed breakfast quickly because we had an early departure time. All in all, I would recommend this hotel highly if you like to be treated like royalty.

review_title: A great place in a so-so city.
review_text: Hotel Grano de Oro is a wonderful oasis in a so-so city. It's a small hotel, with elegant rooms, attentive staff and very pleasant gardens. The hotel restaurant is first class and offers a beautiful setting for cocktails or dinner. It's located in an area that's thought to be safe if not particularly scenic. The art museum and the largest park are a 5-8 minute walk, and major government buildings are a short cab ride away. San Jose doesn't have much to offer a visitor except for a few nice museums, an active pedestrian mall and some pretty parks.Mostly it's crowded and rundown, and some parts are known to be dangerous. The lack of addresses is (sort of) charming in rural parts of CR, but not so when you are trying to find your way downtown. Most of the better hotels are out by the airport or near Escazu-- out of the way of anything downtown, but also not near anything interesting. So if you are staying in town this is an excellent choice.

The hotel is a 20 minute drive from the airport, so it was very convenient.

review_text: We stayed at this hotel for one night before leaving Costa Rica. The hotel is an old house and is very cool. The rooms are mostly spread out across different halls and courtyards. Since it was our honeymoon, they upgraded our room to a king room for free. The room was very comfortable and clean. The staff was very friendly and spoke great English. We ate dinner and breakfast at the hotel restaurant, which was also very cool with an open courtyard. The food was very good and the creme brule was awesome. San Jose was a busy crowded city so this hotel is far enough away from the hustle and bustle of the downtown area but close enough that we walked home from downtown.

review_text: What a classy place. We expected our last night in Costa Rica to be no more than a Holiday Inn (not that their bad) sleep over for our next day departure home. Were we surprised when we arrived. The hotel reminded me of some of the hotels in Charleston SC but with nuances that gave it that extra feeling of luxury and class. The whole place was quaint starting with the beautiful clean rooms, to the many corridors that took you into various nooks and crannies, to the patio restaurant eating areas. We loved it all. The staff was professional and extremely courteous. You'll love it. If there is a weak point it is that it is surrounded by older almost run down buildings which certainly detracted from the over all ambience. But still well worth the stay.

review_title: Charming, beautiful, great service- great way to start your vacation
review_text: We stayed here just one night to kick off a 10 day trip to Costa Rica, so we didnt stay long, but I was very impressed in under 12 hours. We got in late, the staff was waiting for us and helped us with our kids, bags, etc. I am mobility impaired and even though they are a small hotel they went out of their way to help me. We had a beautiful room in a tiny garden and got room service very late at night b/c we got in so late. The hotel is incredibly charming and pretty. If we go back to San Jose would stay here.

review_title: Perfect Beginning/End of Travel in Costa Rica
review_text: We stayed the first and last night of our trip to Costa Rica the end of April/beginning of May. We had a deluxe patio room the first night and the Garden Suite the last night. Both rooms are exceptional-clean, comfortable and beautiful. The staff are attentive and helpful. Ate dinner both nights at the restaurant and breakfast one morning. The service is wonderful, food is delicious and price is reasonable for the quality. Took a cab to the National Museum, ate a local restaurant suggested by staff and walked back from there to the hotel through the Central Market. San Jose is like any other large city in the world. With common sense, it is perfectly safe. Having lived in a neighborhood in San Jose for a summer in college, the hotel's neighborhood is no different or less safe than any other community in the area.

review_text: I kept coming back to this hotel as part of my holiday in costa rica. The staff were super friendly and helpful. Rooms were lovely, fresh and clean. Breakfast was delicious. I used room service as the restaurant looked a little too formal for an evening meal when I was on my own. The menu had a good variety and was delicious. I had a massage in their spa which was super relaxing after the long flight to costa rica. Sadly it was fully booked on each of my return trips so it might be worth trying to book in advance. All my rooms were well sized. My only criticism was that guests seem to be awake very early for activities and transfers. Despite the signs in the corridors there was little respect for other guests need for peace and quiet as they left the hotel in the early hours.

review_text:
After having spent considerable time online searching for a good hotel we decided that this was possibly the best in San Jose. Luckily we were not disappointed.
The hotel is located near the city centre, within a walking distance of 20 minutes. It did not look like other and better hotels are close to the centre. Besides, the city itself does not offers much in terms of points of interest.
On the plus side: the whole hotel grounds and our room were spotlessly clean; our room was on the internal courtyard and it had nice wooden floor and a white bathroom with new appliances. Personnel is helpful and courteous. Being a boutique hotel with only 40 rooms, gives the hotel a lot of character.
It has a couple of jacuzzis on a top level terrace, but no pool. We also ordered breakfast and dinner room service and both were very good.
On the minus side: the room was a bit dark and lacking storage space. The bed was also small and a bit uncomfortable for tall people. A pool would be nice, but I guess there is not enough space for it.

review_title: great hotel for business, couples & quite families
review_text:
I think this hotel is very good for the beginning or the ending of your trip. That's what we did and it was very nice and easy getting from and to the airport.
There is a nice park a short walk away and we we're lucky to come when the Art festival was taking place so there was a nice flea market and shows at the park.
The staff & crew - very nice and accommodating. We didn't needed them much but every interaction with them was very pleasant.
The restaurant staff - excellent service!
the restaurant - VERY GOOD!
We ate there twice dinner and breakfast and everything was very good and tasteful.
The rooms - Very nice. the couples rooms did not have a bathtub but all the rest did and it was very nice to discover they had not only Shampoo & soap but also conditioner which I found very useful.
the stream could have been better but we had hot water all the time.
Very clean!! They cleaned our rooms on a daily basis even when we stayed for 2 nights.
The hotel is one of the best (if not the best) decorated hotels I've ever seen!
It is so pretty and green it makes you feel relaxed just by looking around you.
There is no pool ,however, there are 2 Jacuzzi's side by side in the garden.
I think it was nice if they had a pool but we enjoyed the jacuzzi very much.
The hotel is very quite, Which I fund very much , and that is way I think it is suitable for all type of travellers beside big families with little kids who are looking for attractions.
I will gladly come back to this hotel.

review_title: Rooms are stunning but the restaurant is something else!
review_text: Our agent booked us in here as the last stop on our honeymoon. We saw in the guide books how highly it was rated but it was even better than it suggested! The rooms are great, staff great, and the hot tubs a bonus. But the restaurant is the undoubted highlight. It's been called the best eat in Costa Rica and it would put all but a few places here to shame. Service, drinks, bar, wine cellar, toilets, and , of course, food, we're simply out of this world. The salmon and vanilla was sumptuous! It's not cheap by CR standards but worth the splurge. We've spent more in the UK for lower quality. The only regret was only staying one night!

review_text: We enjoyed the charm and elegance of the Grano de Oro: the classical architecture as well as the murals and artisanal artworks. The hotel is in a residential area, away from the hustle and bustle of central San Jose but close enough so that we were able to walk to and from the hotel. We felt quite safe. We chose a deluxe room overlooking the enclosed garden. It was very quiet, as previous reviewers had noted, though after peeking into some standard rooms while they were being cleaned, we didn't feel that our room merited the extra cost. The restaurant was top notch, with a formal enclosed dining area surrounding tables in a more informal central open courtyard (we preferred the latter). Restaurant staff were very professional and front desk personnel were knowledgeable and helpful. This is a very well run hotel.

review_text:
We stayed at this hotel for 2 days during our holidays in Costa Rica. It is a very charming hotel, very well maintained, clean, classy with a tropical style, our room was lovely and very clean. The staff was extremely friendly and nice. We had breakfast at the hotel restaurant, the service was slightly slow but good, breakfast was delicious and the settings of the restaurant is super nice, with an indoor part and an outdoor part.
The only cons would be that it is not very central, however you can reach the city centre with a 20min walk, which we did not mind.
I would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting San Jose'.

review_title: Good option but service not so warm..
review_text:
This hotel has great history, it´s a very nice option, maybe the best in Costa Rica, but as mentioned before in other reviews, I consider a luxury property when they have not only a nice infrastructure, but also when serve makes you feel they care, and much.
In this case hotel is very well maintained, food is very good but staff is concentrated in administration only, beyond that not much.. I think they should pay attention to this matter as they already have all the rest!!
Patio room environment is so good as it has it`s own fountain! that is so cool.. Room was very clean and room was queen, that was good too.
Hotel restaurant can´t get full very easily as is also an attraction for tourists so make sure to make a reservation and let them clear you are a guest.
There is no SPA or gym at the hotel, only a massage room, just keep that in mind if you like to make exercise.

review_text: I stayed here in March picked this hotel not only based on the TA reviews, but the comments from other travel sources. We arrived around 4 in the afternoon after traveling about 7 hours. We were hot and tired. It was so nice that as soon as we approached the front desk, they brought us glasses of a really nice fruit drink. I don't know what it was, but is was very refreshing. Just what we needed. This hotel really is an oasis in San Jose', a city which is nothing that special. After our one hour walk through the rather loud and unimpressive city, it was really nice to come back to such a lovely hotel. We only stayed one night, but we tried to make the most of it. We bought a few presents for family in their small, but quality gift shop. I'm told all of the items there are purely Costa Rican (unlike so many other gift shops around the country). We had dinner the night we stayed and the food was quite good, but the service was a tad slow (and it was not a weekend night). Our room on the second floor was perfect. I have never seen a garden inside of a hotel room, but we had one here. It was a really nice and unexpected touch. I actually didn't even notice that there was no window in the room till the next morning. This was because there was clear glass that served as the roof of the garden so light and a breeze came through (which is very important to me). The wood in the room itself was a beautiful dark stain and appeared to be a high quality wood. The whole room felt like it was designed by someone who really had a creative touch. I loved the bathroom as well. In the morning, we ate breakfast in the courtyard area. This was really pretty and I loved that part of the bar was in this area. The thought crossed my mind that if I was to have stayed a second night, that it would be so relaxing to have a drink in this bar. It was quite a unique and pretty design. I had never tried mango juice, but did this day and it was fantastic!! I had the banana pancakes and they were wonderful. What a great send off breakfast before our flight. I liked this hotel so much, I am already planning to work it into my next trip to Costa Rica.

review_title: Old-fashioned elegance and charm in a modern world
review_text:
We spent 3 nights in total at this wonderful hotel, 2 when we started our holiday before going to Arenal and Monteverde and the 3rd before flying down to the Osa Peninsular to continue our holiday.
Our rooms were stylish, comfortable and extremely clean with all modern conveniences but still retaining their Spanish origins. The breakfasts were served in an open air courtyard with a fountain playing in the centre. Dinner was served either in the courtyard or in the dining room surrounding it, the service was excellent, very attentive with a wonderful selection on the menus.
I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this hotel to even the most discerning traveller - it's wonderful.
San Jose city itself not worth spending much time in though.

review_title: Beautiful and peaceful place in busy San Jose
review_text: San Jose is a big city but Grano de Oro provided some peace and quiet. Our room for two nights was small but adequate and very clean. It opened up to an interior courtyard which provided light since there were no other windows but we also could hear everyone walking by, even at 5am when they were leaving. We found the staff to be very gracious and friendly, however. We had a lovely dinner in the hotel restaurant which one of our guides told us was the best in town. My duck was prepared perfectly and the wait staff was very attentive. I would recommend this hotel with a couple of cautions. You may want to choose your room ahead of time to avoid noise and to obtain a larger space, especially if you are spending several days in San Jose.

review_text:
My husband and I spent our first and last night in Costa Rica at the Grano de Oro. This refurbished Victorian Mansion has an elegant ambiance especially in the restaurant's courtyard. Our first room was adequate and the water had an odd odor but it was very clean yet on the small side. However, they had provided a lovely fruit plate in the room in celebration of my husband's birthday which was a nice touch. Dinner in the more formal restaurant was excellent and the service was attentive but not smothering.
Our room at the Grano on our last day in Costa Rica was more spacious and the size of the bathroom and the water quality were much improved. We had a seemingly nice lunch in the restaurant, then drinks before having dinner there. Again, it was a lovely experience especially our waiter in the evening who was particularly professional yet friendly. The food at both lunch and dinner was excellent or so we thought. However, several hours after returning to our room my husband became very ill from an obvious food contamination. Being a registered nurse I was able to treat this with medications which are recommended for travelers. After a sleepless night with him being in the bathroom every hour, he was "well enough" to travel. I told the front desk and the restaurant of this experience and only one staff member showed any real concern. The other's at the front desk merely stared as if in fear of being blamed. However, since no other food or water was consumed other than the Grano hours before the illness it was apparent that the culprit was contamination at their restaurant at lunch or dinner.
I would have given this hotel at least a very good rating but after my husband's illness and the hotel less than concerned attitude we would not even recommend it.

review_title: Maybe the best in San Jose, but not very good
review_text: Like a lot of people, we spent the first and last nights of our Costa Rican adventure at Grano de Oro in SJ. It may be the best hotel in SJ, and it is comfortable enough for one night, but it really leaves a lot to be desired. The rooms are OK, and the restaurant is very good, but the service is miserable. They just don't seem to give a darn, perhaps because they have this captive audience of birders and adventure holidayers. And the neighborhood is depressing, ugly and a bit scary.

review_title: Grand Hotel with History and Charm
review_text:
The Hotel Grano de Oro is a charming converted Victorian Mansion. The central courtyard is a great place to while-away-the-hours sipping fine wine and Hors d'oeuvre. The rooms are small but comfortable. The food is good but the service a little lackluster compared to hotels in the same collection (Finca Rosa Blanca and Lapa Rios). The location is fine, but don’t expect to be able to walk to most destinations. San Jose is not conducive to touristy strolls. Taxis are plentiful and cheap so don’t despair.
Overall not a bad place to spend one night in San Jose waiting to catch our international flight home. I would definitely return.

review_text:
We stayed at Grano de Oro for one night at the end of our trip in Costa Rica. The hotel itself is not very big, it is a boutique hotel, but very well appointed. The decor is nicely done in a classic style. We ate at the restaurant for dinner, which was great… I will post a separate review for it. We occupied room 19 with double beds, it was comfortable and located in a courtyard. We do have two things to point out: the bathroom smelled and we suspect that the odor came from the water (although the faucet water is filtered, it could be from the shower or toilet water). The smell was unbearable. Also because the rooms are all so close to each other, when the neighbors woke up at 6am slamming the doors, we could clearly hear them talking. Lastly, the location is not very good. Even though it is central to the city, it is not in a good location. In fact, the hotel being so pretty, it kind of sticks out in the run down neighborhood like a sore thumb. We ventured out to walk around the main areas (20 min walk) to the Gold Museum and the market and got a headache from the crowds and the smell. It definitely was not worth it.
If I had to do it all over it again, I would skip our night at this hotel altogether.

review_title: Nice hotel; not much of a neighborhood
review_text: As previous reviewers have indicated, the Grano de Oro is a fine hotel property. The service is excellent, rooms are nicely appointed and both the garden and hot tub areas are pretty, comfortable and restful. The restaurant, which I will review separately, is world class. If there is a problem with the hotel it is its location in the middle of nothing nice. You can walk a few blocks to a slew of fast food places and the art museum, but otherwise, there is nothing. Going out after dark is not recommended by the hotel staff (or me.) We used the Grano de Oro as a base for touring before we embarked on a cruise at Caldera. This was a mistake; although the tours to various gardens and volcanos were pleasant enough, we spent more time on buses in incredible traffic than we did at the sites. The hotel was efficient in organizing transportation from the airport and to the port at reasonable prices as well as recommending and booking day tours. The hotel seemed to be crowded with people coming and going in all directions and the hotel staff was terrific at getting everyone to the right place on time. I would return to Grano de Oro for one night on the way to/from a cruise port, otherwise, no matter how grand the service is, there's no reason to stay there.

review_title: The Perfect Base in San Jose!
review_text:
The Grano de Oro was our last stop on a two-week trip to Costa Rica. We arrived at the Grano de Oro on March 10th, around 10:30 am, after flying to San Jose from Punta Islita. This was my wife’s first trip to Costa Rica and my fourth. We also stayed at Hotel Manatus, El Silencio Lodge, and the Hotel Punta Islita, all of which I have also reviewed.
We only stayed at the Grano de Oro for one night, but it was so outstanding it deserves its own review! The converted Victorian mansion is just fabulous from top to bottom. There are photos on all the walls in the passageways that were extremely interesting, and I wished for some kind of information about them but nothing was available. They were all taken over the last 100 years or so and showed so much about the development of Costa Rica.
We had booked the special garden suite on the first floor, and it was ready for us upon arrival. The gareden suite was all the we expected. It was spacious, well appointed, clean, and most of all, it felt like home. The bathroom with its huge Jacuzzi was perfect.
We originally planned to venture into town for the afternoon to visit some museums, however we ended up changing our plans and decided to stay in at the hotel. This turned out to be a great decision. We ended up having lunch and dinner, two of our best meals in Costa Rica, at the hotel's restaurant which is world class and as good as any you will find in the world's culinary capitals. Absolutely outstanding!
After experiencing the level of comfort and service at the Grano de Oro, we will absolutely not return to Costa Rica without making it our first and last stop. Bravo Grano de Oro! Thank you so much!
All the best,
Roberto and Juanita

Difficult to talk about this very nice hotel because we checked in late in the evening and checked out very early in the morning the day after! (Twice by the way-:()
This small hotel is probably one of the best of San Jose and all the armosphere breaths this amazing and gorgeous colonial style.
A delicious diner taken in the patio under an umbrella, the restaurant is well known in the city and is a real "place to be" in the center of San jose.
A warm welcome by a staff taking good care of you and despite the location in the center of the city, the hotel is quiet enough.
Our room was fully equiped with all amenities you can expect from this kind of hotel but a little small, anyway we had a good short stay.
Wifi in the main lobby as well as in the bar or in the restaurant.
Terrace on the roof but no time to enjoy the view or the jaccuzi.
We will return if we have the chance to come back in CR!

review_text: We stayed at this hotel for several nights while visiting San Jose prior to a tour. It is a wonderfully renovated old mansion, with fountains and green areas intermixed with the rooms. The sundeck and whirlpool area is a nice place to relax and enjoy the sun. The room was very nice and roomy, as was the bath. The staff is exceptionally friendly and responsive. Although the location is away from the center of the city, it is an easy $4-7 cab ride, depending on which part of the center you want to go to. Sabana park and the Art Museum are within an easy walk and there are a number of nearby restaurants. We would definitely stay here again.

review_text: We first stayed at this wonderful hotel several years ago and loved it so much we vowed to return. Our visit this time was as fabulous, and the remodeling on the main floor increased the ease and flow of the space. We brought our 12-year old granddaughter for her birthday trip and the Grano de Oro started off our exploration of Costa Rica on just the right note. Importantly, this is a "green" hotel and we were impressed with how well the sustainability ethos is integrated into the luxury of the hotel--the best of both worlds. We had a lovely room with hardwood floors and comfortable beds, with a lush garden and fountain to lull us to sleep. Our granddaughter especially loved the rooftop hot tubs, with the surrounding foliage. Everything was clean and well maintained and all staff was helpful and friendly. The restaurant--in new space since we last visited--was elegant and comfortable, with a choice of outdoor seating in the courtyard or indoor dining in the surrounding area. As with the rest of the hotel the staff was attentive, helpful, and engaging. Breakfast was casual and relaxing, with everything from the Tico breakfast to waffles to entice even the pickiest eater. Raves to the coffee and to the hot chocolate. Dinners were excellent, well prepared and beautifully presented, and the wine selection a good range of varieties. We especially enjoyed the salmon, pork, and tilapia dishes which were all done to perfection. We were thrilled to see the same gift shop and proprietor from our last trip; she has a gorgeous array of gifts created by Costa Rican artisans that we hadn't seen elsewhere. Overall our 3 day stay was perfect and we would highly recommend the hotel to anyone--with or without children.

review_text:
It really pains me to leave this review, we stayed at Grano De Oro our last night in Costa Rica and everything was impeccable, well, almost everything.
Service was excellent, the room was beautiful and spotless, dinner in the hotel restaurant was excellent, the hotel is well kept and spotless, though the carpets in the common areas were dirty, I only noticed because it's so out of place with the rest of it and I found it curious. You couldn't ask for more helpful staff and even the little gift shop was great.
So why only two stars? We were put in room #1 which is about 20 feet from the lobby and had a super early flight out of SJO. The room sits on top of some sort of maintenance or janitorial closet I think and there was some noise there, also the big, empty lobby echos up to that particular room until late at night. You can hear every word said, and particularly annoying mos of it was said by staff members shouting at one another. Do I really need to call your front desk staff and ask them to keep it down after 10pm? On top of that you have the stairs along the other wall and people up and down the hall, plus thin walls between the other room. Neither of us slept much, if any.
What good is a beautiful, perfect hotel that you can't get a good nights sleep in?

review_text: This was our first visit to Costa Rica (Nov. 2013). We were so excited about getting into the rain and cloud forests that we weren't really focused on the hotel in San Jose when planning our trip. Thank goodness our travel agent was, however, because this was such a lovely surprise. This is a very quaint, architecturally interesting boutique hotel. We stayed 2 nights in a very comfortable room with a small, private garden area. The bathroom was the type that made you want to take a bath in the tub, which I did that first day! The restaurant (although pricey) was well worth it - nice courtyard, good bar drinks, excellent food and service. We were moving on to other parts of the country and eventually coming back to San Jose at the end of the trip and we were sorry that we did not plan to stay our last night in San Jose at the Grano de Oro, but we will be back!

review_text: On our first stay in Grano de Oro, our flight from Miami was nearly 3 hours late and, as a result we only had a very short night in a beautiful and comfortable room in the old part of the hotel. We did not even have time for breakfast before we left in the morning. The room had its own private garden and water feature and the large old-fashioned bathroom was a delight. We returned to the hotel at the end of our stay in Costa Rica when we had more time to enjoy the hotel. We were not allocated a room in the old part of the hotel on this occasion but our room was still excellent, with a pretty small garden and water feature, although perhaps with a little less character than the first room. We had dinner and breakfast in the elegant courtyard restaurant. The food was very good but the service initially was slow and we had to gee-up the waiter. The concierge was very helpful in directing us to a very simple local restaurant for lunch and he was very particular about our taking the appropriate care (no jewellery etc) when walking in San Jose. We have already recommended this hotel to our friends and would stay there again ourselves. Given the nature of the hotel: originally a Victorian Villa, there is no room for a swimming pool etc. Thank you to Imagine Latin America and their excellent local agent: San Germain Tours for arranging this hotel for us.

review_title: Wonderful Boutique Hotel with an Excellent Restaurant
review_text:
We spent two nights at this lovely small hotel in the heart of San Jose, Costa Rica. The desk staff was warm, welcoming and helpful. They gave us a complimentary upgrade to a superior room from the standard room we had reserved. It was spacious and well furnished. The mattress was comfortable, the bed linens were first-rate. The bathroom had a large bath tub, nice amenities and soft towels. The room had two nice chairs and a table as well as a desk. The complimentary breakfast had several excellent choices; the food and service were excellent.
We ate dinner in the hotel restaurant twice because it was so good! The chef concentrates on French food and incorporates traditional Central American foods into his recipes. Everything was delicious and the ambiance could not be beat.
I highly recommend a stay at this wonderful old-world hotel.

review_text: My partner and I stayed here for one night at the end of our week trip in Costa Rica in March 2013. It was a fantastic way to end our vacation. The hotel is small and feels like a boutique hotel. I was impressed with the furnishings in our room and bathroom, and the restaurant, with its outdoor courtyard, is charming. A few other reviewers commented on the hotel's location. When we first arrived I thought the location seemed a little odd and out of the way. But after spending a little time in San Jose, I think the location is excellent. The neighborhood feels quiet and safe and the central part of town is only a 15/20 minute walk, or a very short cab ride away. It's within easy walking distance of a fairly large and nice park as well as a handful of restaurants and convenience stores. If you're staying in San Jose before or after your trip, I recommend staying here rather than near the airport. While the city doesn't have a tremendous amount to offer in terms of tourist attractions, it's worth checking out and you can't go wrong with this hotel. (It is also easy to get to/from the airport if you have a rental car.)

review_title: Excellent is not a good enough description!
review_text:
We stayed 2 nights at the beginning of our vacation and one night at the end. What can I say?This hotel is fantastic, like something out of a film of bygone times. The rooms are spacious, peaceful and quiet. The staff are so helpful and professional but what amazed us the most was the food. The food quality is outstanding, presentation, service,atmosphere in the dining room, everything was unbelievable. Also, the price was extremely reasonable, if this had been in the UK it would have been 100 times the cost for probably not the same quality. I would just like to mention the waiter that served our table who was called Hugo. This man is professional, polite and a credit to the hotel.
On check out the following day we had an early start for our flight back to the UK. We requested a breakfast box and expected a few sandwiches in a box .No, not this hotel,,we had 2 huge boxes packed with juice,croissants,yogurts,jams etc!!!
Highly recommended and really hope one day we will return to this special hotel.

review_text:
Stayed 2 nights at the beginning and 1 night at the end of our CR trip at this medium sized boutique hotel in a beautifully restored colonial building.
First stay was excellent. Quiet downstair room with all amenities in a lovely garden. Extremely helpful receptionists, jacuzzi on rooftop, within walking distance to the few sights of San Jose.
Dining room with roofed patio is overwhelming, but if your table for dinner is in the patio it´s that dark you´ll need a torch for reading the menu (ask for it- the waiter is prepared for this)
Restaurant is not bad, but overrated, especially the winelist overpriced and parts of staff are underachievers. There are definitely better restaurants in town, e.g. La Esquina de Buenos Aires.
Second stay was not excellent at all as they gave us an indeed beautifully furnished, but extremely noisy room on first floor. As windows were far away from any kind of noise prevention we could listen to heavy traffic till about midnight and again from about 4:00 a.m.- what a night :-(
All things considered this is quite a recommended place to stay, but take care which room you get. Restaurant is only recommended if you just want to spend an evening in colonial atmosphere ;-)

review_text:
We stayed here just one night when we first arrived in San Jose. While we were happy to leave the city early the next day, we were sorry to leave the hotel.
Our room was lovely, with its own little courtyard garden complete with fountain. The staff were friendly and helpful.
We usually avoid hotel restaurants, but after walking to the pedestrian center of San Jose in the afternoon, we decided we didn't need to go back at night- so ate at the hotel. Good decision! The restaurant was excellent- food, service and ambiance.

review_text: We stayed 2 nights here when we first arrived in Costa Rica and again one night before flying home. It's not situated in a particularly good area but from what we've seen of St Jose haven't seen another area that could be any better. The Grano de Oro has the feeling of being a relaxing ,comfortable place with a slight air of faded grandeur. We were happy with the standard room when we were first here , and when we returned found we had been upgraded to a more spacious room. Very nice with comfortable beds and fine cotton bedding. We left some luggage with the hotel while we were travelling in Costa Rica which was very convenient ,they also found a cardigan that I had left behind in the restaurant and that was waiting for me too carefully folded and wrapped. Very thoughtful. Food is very good in the restaurant and the courtyard lovely for breakfast and lunch on a sunny day. The staff are great especially reception, very friendly and helpful.

review_text: My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Grano de Oro on our last night in Costa Rica. The hotel is so beautiful and we had such a great room, that we wish we could have enjoyed it more. Unfortunately, the travel agent who booked the hotel for me didn't include the hotel's address in our itinerary and I didn't catch it until the last minute. We wasted a few hours driving around in rush hour traffic in dicey areas of San Jose in a vain attempt to happen upon the hotel. We finally backtracked to an area that had a Marriott and an Outback restaurant so that we could access wifi to find the hotel address (no cell service so utilizing our GPS was out of the question). Upon arrival, we were greeted with a complimentary cocktail (much needed) and a pleasant check-in. I booked the garden suite (Room #9), which was very spacious and included a big jacuzzi tub and a private garden to relax in. We had dinner in the hotel restaurant: great atmosphere, wonderful food and the service was pleasant and relaxed. I recommend the black bean soup and the Corvina Cardamomo. The desserts looked tasty, but we had no room left after eating very well for two weeks. This is a great hotel to treat yourself to if you need a place to stay for an early morning flight out of San Jose. One final tip: the route to the airport is very easy from the hotel and about 30 minutes away (ask reception for a map). However, there is little to no signage for the rental car returns (Thrifty was our rental agency - no signs announcing the rental car office whatsoever). You'll find the rental car return for a number of agencies directly across the street from the airport right next to the Fiesta Casino. Take the exit for the Fiesta Casino (on your right) and you'll be fine. Now I'm off to learn some Spanish for my future trips to Costa Rica.

review_title: Colonial-era comfort, too close to downtown
review_text:
Almost everyone who visits Costa Rica has to spend a night in San Jose. Our travel agency put us in this very attractive, renovated mansion. The central courtyard, surrounded by the formal restaurant, is a nice place for breakfast-which was included with our particular rate. One reason we stayed in town was that we asked to visit the huge gardens at the Hotel Bougainvillea, and the private orchid garden of Ileana Teran (accent marks omitted.)
Our room, #23, was off the small fountain courtyard and had a tiny terrace surrounded by a privacy screen. Although the room was attractively furnished and had a large tub/shower bathroom, it was relatively small and the huge King bed was due for replacement. The room had a very modern split-ductless-unit air conditioner, but we didn't need it. We were not disappointed, but the level of luxury didn't quite live up to the price.
As you exit the lobby at night, you pass a sign with an international graphic for "Please be quiet!". I wish every American hotel had one of these on each floor at night! What a good idea. We didn't find the jacuzzis on the small, screened roof that attractive, but they could well appeal to other people.
As other reviewers note, there is little reason to stay downtown if you don't have museum (we missed the Gold Museum, alas), theater, or business duties. If you're being picked up for a jungle-sort of daytrip, stay outside the rush-hour traffic zone, not here. You might even get to sleep later. We noticed that this hotel is part of several groups, including the Cayuga Collection and Small Distinctive Hotels of C.R., which might be a way to screen other places for a rough level of quality. We later stayed at another, very fine, Cayuga hotel, Lapa Rios.
We found all of the staff to be friendly and helpful, including in the dining room. The dinner was elaborately Continental, and satisfactory ($70 for two with one round of drinks and service charge) , but not the equal of a big American luxury hotel. Breakfast was very pleasant. There is a wheelchair lift at the street, and an elevator in the building.

review_title: A special hotel in San Jose
review_text: My wife and I stayed here on our first and second night in Costa Rica after travelling from the UK and arriving late in the evening. This place was an oasis of quiet, calm and luxury in San Jose. Lovely decor, attentive staff and a fantastic restaurant. Hot tubs on the roof and an open and airy feel to the whole place. Not the cheapest in town but definitely recommended if you have had a long journey or have been roughing it in the jungle for a few days and are in need of some luxury!!

review_title: Lovely hotel let down by surroundings
review_text: We decided to spend our last night in Costa Rica in San Jose. The hotel is fantastic with lots of character and wonderful staff at reception (restaurant staff not quite as good see below). However, San Jose has very little to offer and the hotel is located in a unattractive area with nothing else to offer. However it is not far from the centre which also has little going for it. We did visit a few of the historic building left in the city and visited the museum which was interesting as it gave us some insight into the original indigenous population. Some fantastic gold artefacts. We ate at the hotel in the evening (had lunch at the old Theatre which was pleasant) and the food was OK but not the fine dining it purports to be. Almost there but too many silly little mistakes and the waiters could take a lesson in how to be pleasant. If you are looking for a night in San Jose the hotel is definitely worth considering and our room was wonderful but they could do a bit better.

review_text: Full of character and beautifully decorated. Stayed 2 separate nights, one at the beginning and the other at the end of our trip. We ate in the restaurant on our last night - an elegant evening of fine dining. A perfect way to start and end our holiday.

review_title: Excellent way to start and end a Costa Rica expedition
review_text: We stayed our first night and last night at the Grano de Oro. What a very nice and superb way to start and end a unique and memorable vacation. My wife and I were delighted all the way: very nice room and unique set-up with small garden and waterfall IN the room, excellent food and very attentionate staff. We felt welcomed and cared for. Imagine how important your first night and last night expriences are to set the tone of a unique vacation. Thanks a lot.

review_text:
This beautiful Victorian building has such old worldly charm but with all modern amenities required for the perfect stay.
It is set a short walk away from the bustling centre of San Jose on a quiet side street. Check in was efficient and quick although as with all Costa Rican hotels we visited you are given a welcome drink while standing filling out paperwork the minute you arrive. Not at all relaxing especially after 18 hours in transit.
We had room 17 which was lovely and had everything required for our two night stay. It was very private and hidden by lush planting in the courtyard. Toiletries were generic but ok, bed was lovely with comfy pillows. Widescreen tv if you need it, two ceiling fans, quiet air con and opening windows so plenty of ways to adjust the temperature.
The hotel is quirky with small courtyards and internal gardens, a small sun terrace with tropical planting and two small jacuzzis. You can eat inside or out in the beautiful central courtyard. Dinner was superb as was the good choice of al a carte breakfast. Again like most hotels here food is very expensive but at least here it was superb. The staff are very formal but very efficient.
If you come to San Jose this hotel is a must on all fronts.

review_text:
We stayed two nights at Grano de Oro at the start and end of a rafting trip in the rainforest. The hotel service was great. They knew we were coming back and so offered to store our extra luggage before we asked. We needed to find an ATM and were given a map to a very secure location within 4 blocks. I loved the ambience of the restaurant and our meals were good. The first night we had the chateaubriand and the cardamom sea bass - both amazing.
Our tour company described this as being close to the main touring areas of San Jose, which I wouldn't agree with. During the day it may be OK, but we were warned to be very careful walking around in the evening.

review_text:
We stayed two nights here, once at the start and once at the end of our holiday over Xmas & New Years 2013/14.
Not quite central, more a residential kind of neighbourhood just to the east of centre, the Grano de Oro is a beautiful colonial style boutique hotel with very good levels of service (though not excellent/5* [more on that later]), very comfy beds, surprisingly quiet rooms, and a fabulous restaurant (if a little pricey) with a delightful courtyard setting for breakfast.
Our first night we were in rooms 14 and 15 (queen bed in each), ground floor near reception and a little susceptible to lobby noise (though not late), which were modest and adequate if unimpressive. Second night we were in room 19 which was delightful, highly recommended, with two queen beds and zero noise problems and a lot more charm being situated off another quaint courtyard.
There is no pool, not even a small one, which was disappointing, but two decent hot-tubs partly make up for this.
Regarding service, our flights home were cancelled and the like of 5* service showed when we asked the hotel for help. We had to do all the chasing and make all the phonecalls ourselves, for which we were charged (albeit at a concessionary rate - $32 of calls granted to us for $10). Compare this to the Mandarin Oriental in Singapore where we had a similar problem and the hotel staff treated us like royalty and did all the hard work for us, greatly reducing the stress element.
Overall very good, 100% recommend and will be my hotel of choice whenever back in San Jose.

Make sure to book if eating in the restaurant on Friday or Saturday nights as it is very popular .

This is a lovely, quaint hotel with charm and comfort. We stayed here our first night in Costa Rica, before heading out to our first official destination in the morning. The area outside the hotel didn't look to safe and since we arrived just before sunset, we just stayed in our room and just relaxed before dinner.

Staff was friendly and welcoming.

review_title: Lovely oasis in downtown San Jose
review_text:
We stayed here for two nights at the beginning of our two weeks in CR. The property and rooms are beautiful in an old victorian style and the staff is very friendly and welcoming. There are also two fantastic jacuzzis on the private hotel patio that provided a great way to unwind from our day of traveling. Although the hotel property is completely safe, the staff will advise you to utilize taxis if you are venturing out at night. We did a lot of walking around San Jose in the 36 hours we were there, and although we didn't see anything any worse than any other city, having just arrived in country, we took their advice after dark.
The rooms are averaged sized and very clean and our was situated in a picturesque courtyard. The beds are comfortable enough, and there are a realistic amount of outlets in reasonable places. There is an in-room safe.
There is a great little diner/soda shop a very short cab ride away that is open until about 3am and a good place for a tasty bite if you arrive on a later flight.
If you're looking to arrange your airport transfers, or transportation to your next town or accommodations, the hotel staff is happy to assist you, however, you'll want to check with your next hotel as well and see who will be more reasonably priced.
Lastly, and I will end all of my CR reviews with this note: *You will be charged a 13% tax and should factor that into your budget from the very beginning.* As long as you keep that in mind, your bills will never surprise you.
Overall, a great little hotel, worth the price. I would stay here again and recommend it to friends.

review_text:
We stayed at Grano de Oro in November 2012. As many other reviewers mentioned, we stayed in the hotel for only one night when we flew into San Jose. The hotel itself was beautiful. The dark wood and décor in the room was gorgeous. The staff was very friendly and welcoming. We were handed fresh juice the moment we walked in. We enjoyed fresh made fruit cocktails in the open air beautiful court yard. The bartender was great in helping us navigate and pick some of the well-known and popular cocktails in Costa Rica. We dined in the restaurant and had high expectations given many travel books say the restaurant is one of the best in San Jose. We would have to agree with their recommendation of the restaurant. The food was spectacular. The only negative is that it is an area where they recommended we not walk around; however this seems to be common in San Jose and not only limited to this hotel.
Overall, we would definitely use this hotel as a stop when coming into Costa Rica again though we would not stay much longer than a night as many a travel book will tell you because there isn’t much to do or see in San Jose.

review_text:
I'll preface this review in saying this was my first trip out of the US, and I traveled solo?!! Prior to arrival in San Jose, I contacted the Hotel Grano de Oro in San Jose, booked my stay (based on the many many positive Tripadvisor reviews) and I couldn't be happier with my decision. It was just a one night stay. The communication from the hotel staff prior to my arrival was excellent. I inquired about "things to do" when I arrived in San Jose, and they went out of their way trying to help me find a coffee plantation tour, and suggested other "popular" things to do, as an alternative. They also arranged for ground transportation, which I would HIGHLY recommend, as "navigating": through customs/immigration was a bit challenging. It was so comforting to exit the airport and see my transportation awaiting with a sign that had my name on it! Perfect!!
The courtyard off the lobby was perfect to enjoy an afternoon libation. Had breakfast there, and it was also nice.. not incredible, but very good.
The room was comfortable, and the staff was extremely pleasant.. offering restaurant suggestions. The room was just what I needed for one night.. comfortable beds.. clean (spotless) accomodations.. and so pretty decorated with Xmas "holiday flare!"
If I ever needed to stay in San Jose, I wouldn't think twice about staying at Hotel Grono de Oro, and you shouldn't either!

review_title: Excellent Hotel--Great Choice for Proximity to Estadio Nacional
review_text:
This is simply an excellent hotel, which I strongly recommend as an alternative to chain business hotels on the western side of San Jose. Some friends and I used this hotel as a home base in September for the US-Costa Rica World Cup qualifier. The hotel is an easy walk to the large urban park (La Sabana) where the new Estadio Nacional is located. The area around the hotel itself is not particularly scenic, but the hotel is a beautifully renovated old building with character. At midday, you will see local elites out for business lunches--not just tourists moving on to the beaches. Downstairs from the restaurant are interesting black-and-white photographs of old San Jose. Wonderful ambience.
The restaurant and bar are situated around an open courtyard, like many older Central American hotels. We ate both breakfast and dinner there, and they were very good. The restaurant is elegant and has a beautiful, old-fashioned bar with knowledgeable bartenders. In general, the staff were friendly and helpful.
This is the only hotel I have stayed in in San Jose, but frankly, I cannot imagine staying somewhere else, whether for a business trip, a stopover on the way to the coast, or a soccer game. This is a well conceived and executed boutique hotel.

review_text:
Like many other travellers we used this hotel as our first night stop after flying into San Jose. It is only 20 minutes from the airport so perfectly located. I had booked our hire car from the airport so it was frustrating to see that there are many companies just round the corner from the hotel which would have been a much better option!
We picked a garden courtyard suite which was another mistake as it gets dark pretty early so we couldn’t use the outside space and we were off fairly promptly in the morning so pointless really. I found the decor a bit oppressive - lots of dark wood and very traditional.
The restaurant was great. Lovely fine dining experience and clearly popular with locals enjoying special dinners. Beware if you are light eaters though the portions are huge.
A great option for one night arriving or departing from SJ. Not sure I would want to stay any longer.

review_text:
We were just looking for a place to spend the first night in Costa Rica before moving on. A quick trip to Trip Advisor brought us to the Hotel Grano de Oro in San Jose. It was an absolute gem. The staff was fantastic. It is not in the city center, but that's a small price to pay for the luxury of this hotel. Between a long day of travel and convenience of the hotel restaurant, we chose to eat there. The food was absolutely top notch! We were told the next day by our driver that it was considered one of the top restaurants in Costa Rica. I had no trouble at all believing it. There was a little sticker shock with the dinner bill from the restaurant but it wasn't what you'd think. The bill comes with gratuity included and was in Colons as well as Dollars. When it looked like the bill was 60000 dollars, I was headed for a heart attack. When it turned out to be under $120 with tip included, my cardiac problems were minimized.
Would I go back again? You betcha!
