review_text: I have to tell you. I never ever take the time to write reviews of any Hotel, however I was inclined to write one now. My wife and I just returned from an 8 night trip to Costa Rica. I hated Costa Rica as it is an overpriced over rated country and would rather spend my money in Hawaii or some other Caribbean Island, however the only bright spot of our entire vacation was our layover in this wonderful Hotel Grano de Oro. I must say that I have stayed in some of the finest hotels in the world, Four Seasons, Ritz Carlton, St.Regis, etc. Our stay at this little hotel was up to par with some of those larger hotel chains. Although Costa Rica as a whole was disappointing, this Hotel was the best part of my trip. The service, the rooms, the staff, and the food was incredible. We stayed two nights when we first arrived and another night on Christmas Eve. The restaurant was excellent and we thoroughly enjoyed a dinner with the family. I want to thank everyone at this Hotel for making our stay as pleasant as it could be. Please don't change anything as you are a perfect Hotel. For those planning on going to Puerto Viejo, Cahuita, or any other part of the Caribbean side of Costa Rica....DON'T! That area is full of crooks looking to screw you out of your money and it is a drug infested crap hole. The only bright spot of our trip was this great Hotel. So thank you for making my vacation half way decent while we stayed at your Hotel.

review_text: We capped off a weeklong trip to Costa Rica with a one-night stay here before flying out the next morning. Our travel agent had tried to put us up in a Holiday Inn, but my high-end daughter searched the internet and found this place which cost only a tiny amount more. All the places we stayed previously were supposed to be superlative but weren't. This place really was a Holy Cow! experience. It was aboslutely gorgeous, the food was incredible and the service even more so. I was beginning to despair about nice hotels in a third world country (actuallly Costa Rica seemed second world, if there is such a thing.) The hotel surroundings weren't especially gorgeous, bu they weren't bad to walk around and I am very nervous in cities. There was no city noise in the hotel, the beds were super-comfortable and the entire experience was an absolute delight and huge sigh of relief. Thank you Grano de Oro!

review_text:
We had one night to kill in San Jose, at the end of our Costa Rican vacation. The Hotel Grano de Oro was the perfect hotel for this purpose. The rooms are clean and luxurious (perhaps the beds are a bit too soft, but they ARE luxurious). The staff is friendly and helpful, the food at the restaurant is absolutely delicious, the hotel facility is beautiful and well-appointed. Everything was decorated up for Christmas, and it was beautiful! We also really enjoyed the beautiful music coming from the next-door convent (?), orphanage (?)..... while they held their religious services Saturday night.
The only downside to this hotel is its location. It is close to downtown San Jose, which, it turns out, has very little to offer to the tourist. It is truly the downtown of a large city, where the shops are mostly discount shoes and clothing, aimed at residents of the inner city. We spent a morning walking around, hoping to find some last minute souvenirs. We had been directed to the downtown area, but truly found nothing. We did eventually find an artisan craft area at the far end of town. It is telling that two different hotel front desk people warned us to be careful while walking around. One told us that the area is safe, as long is there is daylight. The other told my daughter that she should remove her little necklace and earrings before going out.
The Grano de Oro itself is fantastic! It definitely rates 5 stars, if it could be picked up and moved to an better location.

review_text: We stayed here just for one night before traveling on to our main resort in CR, and I wish we could have stayed longer. Walkable to the main areas of SJ, which was nice. The gift shop was even great! The restaurant is supposed to be one of the best in the city so we had our dinner there and it was superb. I had a great Duck and my mom had a lovely steak dish. I just could not imagine staying in a better place. It's a shame that the city of SJ has so little to offer otherwise or we would stay here every time we came to CR!

review_text:
Beware, and know what you are reserving before it's too late. Hotel Grano de Oro is located within walking distance of downtown San Jose.... but its is a long walk in a very questionable area. If you are looking to feel safe or comfortable walk.... think again. Our first morning as we were leaving I was stopped by the doorman and asked where we were going. When I said downtown I was told to remove my little gold necklace. Seriously?? I have traveled the world and have never had to worry about a thin gold necklace. Just to be clear, although downtown San Jose is a "one time" must visit, it is on the rough side, a huge fist fight broke out right in front of us - not a comfortable experience!
OK, back to Grano de Oro, for the price point, you can do much, much better. We reserved the family suite as my husband I were traveling with two of our adult children. We got two double beds and one twin, and one bathroom. Personally, I don't define a double bed and a shared bathroom as vacation! Also note, there is no breakfast included making it even a worse value.
Lastly, before you reserve, note the cancellation policy - they are not willing to make any changes! They didn't care that we were unhappy. I think Hotel Grano de Oro has survived on its restaurant. We made a strategic decision not to eat in their there as we didn't want to hand them any more money. I'm sure it's very good, so my strong suggestion would be to skip the hotel (you will do much better anywhere else) and rather just go for a meal and check out the restaurant.

review_text: My husband, oldest son and I recently traveled to San Jose, Costa Rica to visit another son who is traveling abroad for a semester. We stayed at the Hotel Grano de Oro in San Jose' and it was PERFECT! The room was large and spotless. The bathroom had all that we needed. The bedding and the linens were just right. The decor of the lobby, the restaurant and the hotel was just beautiful, yet very relaxing! But, the thing that made the hotel so wonderful was the staff. We were there for 7 days and spent a lot of time at the hotel as it rained all day, every day for the entire trip. Thank goodness all the staff spoke very good English as we don't speak any Spanish. The staff was kind, helpful and just plain old fun. This hotel is truly an oasis in the middle of a developing country/city. I would definitely stay at the Hotel Grano de Oro again AND highly recommend it to anyone who is thinking of traveling there. One minor point however, don't expect to walk to anything. Anything and everything is either a taxi ride or bus ride away. That said, don't let that deter you from staying at this hotel. The staff totally took care of us in all aspects of getting to and from the hotel. The restaurant in the hotel is not to be missed. Everytime we ate there we just wanted to come back for more. This includes breakfast, lunch and dinner. The decor of the restaurant was just gorgeous, the food was exquisite, the presentation of all the food was extremely creative and the service was awesome. I would have loved this restaurant just as much if it were in London, Paris or Rome!

review_text:
We stayed in this beautiful, historic hotel on the final night of our vacation. What a perfect way to end a wonderful Costa Rica holiday. When we checked in, the friendly hotel staff had upgraded us from a standard to a supreme suite. The room was large, clean and the bed was comfortable. We had dinner in the restaurant on site; an excellent meal. The presentation of the dishes was magnificent.
After dinner, we used the lobby computer and checked into our flight and printed our boarding passes for our early morning flight. The front desk booked a private transport to Juan Santa Maria Intl Airport ($25) and offered a wake-up call.
I would highly recommend this hotel staying in San Jose.

review_title: Like a trip back in time to an era of elegance, class and sophistication.
review_text: This was our third visit to Costs Rica but our first to San Jose. Regrettably, unlike so much of this beautiful and wonderful country - my favourite in all the world - the capital city has little to offer. Nevertheless, I would always be happy to start and end my trips there in the future and to return to this simply lovely hotel, which is one of the best I have stayed at anywhere. It is beautifully presented, the rooms are immaculate (with the most comfortable beds ever!) and the staff friendly, helpful and efficient. The restaurant is sheer elegance and sophistication, and makes the dining experience a real pleasure. The food is also extremely good - certainly no more expensive than good hotel restaurants in Panama City, Lima or Cusco. Whilst it is tempting to keep such a gem to oneself, i would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting San Jose, and I wouldn't want to stay anywhere else in the city.

review_text: What an incredible hotel. This beautifully appointed hotel is a blast from the past and has been kept in pristine condition. The bar, restaurant, and rooms - we stayed in 10 for a couple nights at the beginning of our trip, and stayed in suite 9 at the end of our trip - are a must see for any visitors to Costa Rica. The wood paneling, carved woods, garden areas, and sitting rooms are cosy and comfortable. The staff made our trip less stressful and did everything they could to make us happy. This hotel truly exceeds the 5 stars that are given to many hotels we've stayed in. We will definitely stay, eat and drink here when traveling back through Costa Rica.

review_title: Good option for business travellers too
review_text:
I regularly stay at this hotel, as I need to visit San Jose on a monthly basis. Being a boutique hotel has it's advantages and disadvantages, of course. The rooms vary from one to the other, and you don't accumulate points in a loyalty program. But then again, loyalty programs are meant to replicate the kind of service that small hotels like this one can provide.
The daytime staff are very friendly, and remember you from one stay to the next. I usually get the same room every time I visit, and once, accompanied by my wife, I got a free upgrade to a grand suite.
It is true that the difference in friendliness between daytime and nighttime staff is surprising, and there is street noise to contend with. To that I would add that the table and chairs in the rooms are not the most comfortable for working.
On the other hand, the location is very good if your business takes you downtown, and the hotel is near the Sabana Grande park, which is a good option for exercising.
A highlight is the restaurant, which is well known in San José in it's own right.
Overall, a hotel worth becoming a regular at.

review_title: Loved the hotel, the architechure, atmosphere, food, ....
review_text:
An old mansion turned into hotel, Hotel Grano do Oro is an excellent place to stay, It is charming and peaceful (it was great that you were in a very nice hotel without long hall ways, large halls, elevators, ....) Very tastefully decorated. We stayed there for 3 night. The restaurant was excellent: the food was great, the atmosphere was very formal, but the waiters were so warm and friendly and would do everything to make you happy. It is beautiful, with gorgeous stained glasses, a large courtyard in the middle. Definitely go there if you are in San Jose.
One other thing: they have a nice gift shop.

review_text:
We arrived at this beautiful hotel directly from the airport and were upgraded from a Standard room to a Superior room free of charge. The room was lovely and the bed was the most comfortable and the shower had the most pressure of all of our hotels in Costa Rica. We didn't get a chance to use the rooftop hot tub as we were only here one night, but the view from the roof was pretty neat.
At check in they provided us with a city map and once we settled in, we decided to explore downtown San Jose a bit. Since it looked rainy, the hotel provided an umbrella for us to take just in case. We ended up needing it on our way back!
The hotel provided a laptop with free internet access so we could email our family and let them know we had arrived safely. The only thing I wish they would have offered was a free phone to call internationally, as my parents don't have internet and we had to wait until we got to our next hotel to call and let them know we had made it.
We ended up eating dinner here and the food was good, but not great, and a little overpriced in my opinion. However, the tres leches cake was the best that we had in all of Costa Rica. Amazing!!! We also had breakfast here in the morning in the courtyard and my mango creme french toast was wonderful. The best breakfast of our trip! My husband's omlete was good he said, but nothing special like my french toast!
Overall we had a great stay and left with fond memories of San Jose and the Grano de Oro.

review_title: A classically beautiful hotel with great service
review_text: Ten years ago, on my first trip to Costa Rica, I noticed a beautiful old house being renovated as we were driving to the airport. I asked the driver and he said it was being made into a boutique hotel. I made a mental note that if I returned, that would be where we would stay. Voila! This last June, we had a wonderful return trip to visit relatives and spent our first (and only ) night at the Grano de Oro. Dining in the exquisite restaurant, my husband remarked that this was a super way to start the trip! We loved everything about the place: service was friendly and excellent; our room was upgraded and we were able to have a room opening to a lovely garden patio. Whenever I emailed with a question, they responded quickly. Indeed, it was a great way to start the trip.

review_text: Staying here was the only thing that made our visit to San Jose worthwhile. The hotel and rooms are beautiful. The hot tubs on the roof make a beautiful respite from what is a hectic and dirty city. Despite being outside, they were surprisingly quiet. The staff are incredibly friendly and helpful, and they gave us detailed directions to our next stop as well as great recommendations on local restaurants. The parking area has a locked gate, and there is security outside the hotel at all times. We were able to walk to the main part of the city from the hotel, although it may be a bit far for some people. However, cabs are readily available. Also, the restaurant easily had the best food we ate in Costa Rica. It had a beautiful setting with very professional and formal waitstaff. It was so good that we ate dinner and breakfast there even though we stayed only one night. For such a nice restaurant, it was surprisingly affordable, too. Overall, we were underwhelmed by the city, but our stay at the hotel made it worth it.

review_title: Elegant Impeccalbe Emaculate - Oasis in San Jose
review_text:
We stayed at this beautiful hidden gem a few nights ago and had to jump on Trip Advisor to agree with all the positive things that have been written about it. The rooms, staff, food, atmosphere were all exceptional. We would highly recommend this hotel.
One thing that we thought should be mentioned is that it seems a good idea to take a taxi to anywhere else you want to go in the area. We were not totally comfortable walking around the area. When we asked the people there they agreed that taxi was our best bet. On that note, keep an eye on your taxi driver as they continually tried to take us long ways to our destinations, and even once told us we had arrived at a place that wasn't really where we had asked to go. We think it was a scam to take us to one of their friends businesses.
Otherwise, enjoy the Grano de Oro. It is an oasis in San Jose.

review_title: Absolutely amazing - WAY beyond our expectations - STAY HERE!!!
review_text:
The Hotel Grano de Oro was our first stop in Costa Rica - it is about a 20 minute drive from the International airport depending on traffic.
The Hotel is an oasis near the center of the city. It is quiet, restful and very luxurious.
I cannot say enough about the high level of customer service of the staff. The restaurant staff is also top notch and go out of their way to recommend, suggest and just plain help! The food in the Hotel restaurant is also excellent and reasonably priced!!
Overall, I would not skip the chance to stay at the Hotel Grano de Oro while you are in Costa Rica. You will not regret this decision!

review_text: We stayed at this hotel twice during our 12 days in Costa Rica, once in the middle of our trip and once at the tail end. The rooms are very clean and comfortable, the internet access is fast and reliable, and it's very quite considering it's so close to the big city. This is the best way to end your trip to Costa Rica-clean, reliable, efficent, and professional.

review_text: I can't say enough great things about Grano de Oro. It is a real treasure. The hotel is in downtown San Jose, by Paseo Colon, so it is centrally located for shopping and tourist attractions and so forth. The rooms are just lovely, cozy and comfortable (there is even piped in music via the phone that you can leave on or turn off). The staff is great- service here is really a priority. Gift shop is very cute, colorful. Amazing flower arrangements and art throughout the hotel and in room. Somesimes fresh fruit arrangements upon arrival. But my favorite part by far, and I have stayed at this hotel many times, is the restaurant. It is so elegant, the food is great, menu has lots of choices, service is wonderful and the best part? The Grano de Oro pie. A chocolate expresso mousse confection that is totally irresistible. We love this hotel- if you stay in San Jose, stay here, you will have a wonderful experience. And don't forget to have the pie.

review_text: We stayed here for the first two nights of our honeymoon. After a hectic few weeks organising our wedding and a long journey to Costa Rica, we could not have asked for a better start to out holiday. Our room was tastefully decorated and spacious, overlooking the courtyard dining area. Breakfast was fantastic, especially the fresh smoothies and coffee. The area surrounding the hotel does not have much to offer, we only ventured out to the main shopping area to grab a few last minute holiday supplies and spent the rest of our time relaxing at the hotel, reading and enjoying the rooftop terrace & jacuzzi. The dining room is quite formal but dinner was simply delicious - highly recommended.

review_title: Glamorous hotel near the centre of San Jose
review_text: Stayed here for our honeymoon, on our two nights in San Jose and absolutely LOVED it! It's a beautiful hotel, we stayed in a room by a patio which was quiet, clean and well catered. review_title: We'd Stop in San Jose just to Come Back to This Hotel
review_text: The ambience, service, and helpfulness/friendliness of the staff (from the front desk, bellhops, waiters) combine to make this one our new favorite hotels. The hotel is set up beautifully with a mix of modern and historic farchitecture. The restaurant is incredible and worth visiting even if you're not staying at the hotel. At the airport, we overheard a gentleman telling another couple to "try the duck" at this restaurant. I did and would second that opinion. I don't know when I've had a better meal. The hotel is somewhat remote (20 to 30 minute walk) from the busy market areas, which turns out to be an advantage. It's quiet and peaceful. Highly recommended.

review_text:
We stayed 2 nights at Grano de Oro after arriving in Costa Rica at the start of a fortnight holiday. We travelled with 3 children 14,12 and 11 and we stayed in a family room.
the hotel is located in a bit of a 'run down' area off the Via Coleon, it is on a quiet street. we walked into the centre of S.J. and we felt quite safe.
The Grano de Oro is a quality hotel, with lovely rooms, great public spaces and a fantastic restaurant, it is a delightful place to stay, and the staff were very welcoming with us and our children.
If you want more than somewhere just to 'rest your head' then try it!

review_title: A great hotel, we are so glad we stayed here
review_text: We stayed at this hotel for one night and had a free afternoon to explore San Jose. The hotel was an oasis in an otherwise uninspiring city. We went for a short walk around and then headed straight back to the hotel to enjoy our lovely, unique room. We booked a standard room via Expedia, but it was more luxurious than standard and even had an outdoor, covered patio with a fountain! We ate at the hotel restaurant in the evening to avoid going out in the city after dark, but actually the restarant was great. It was very grand, but we felt comfortable in the smartest clothes that we had brought with us (not very smart) and our flip flops! It was not the cheapest meal, but I would recommend it. We were very pleased with our choice.

review_title: Relaxed oasis in the middle of San Jose chaos.
review_text:
This is a review of Hotel Grano de Oro in San Jose, Costa Rica.
We stayed here because it was one of the few selections available on a travel gift certificate that was awarded by our employer. It is an expensive place to stay, but if you can afford it, it is well worth it! The entire staff was always extremely polite and helpful, but really stayed out of the way otherwise. The hotel is not large, so its quiet and not busy. It is apparently a converted mansion so theres lots of different rooms, neat twisty hallways and tropical courtyards. Though this doesn't have a swimming pool, the sun deck and Jacuzzis were great. The location is great - even though its in a strange neighborhood, its actually walking distance to the major park (with soccer stadium) and also the downtown pedestrian mall. I really liked that this hotel does NOT feel like an "American chain" hotel though it has all the luxuries and amenities.
A great bonus is the restaurant in the hotel - one of the best in San Jose and certainly as good as the nicest restaurants I frequent in New York City.

review_text: I love this hotel. I have been staying here off and on for 12 years. And they have really up’ed their game. It is a totally civilized way to start or end a jungle adventure. I usually stay here when I get in late or have to leave early as most of my trips are to the coast. The rooms are incredible. Pretty perfect in fact. Great beds, linens, marble bathrooms, etc. The restaurant is very elegant. Great food, huge selection and impeccable service. Sometimes they get a little to involved in executing their service and forget there is a customer there, but you can’t be completely on all the time. A low beginning room rate makes this an option for almost any budget. I typically get the lowest price, which is a great room. Last couple of times they upgraded us and wow. Nice. They don’t have a pool, so if that is really important this may not be a good option. The hotel is in an “up and coming” area of San Jose. When you go here, you pretty much stay in the hotel as there really isn’t much to walk to. Again, I love this hotel.

review_text: We had just returned from a 12 day tour of Costa Rica staying at places like Arenal Nayara and Los Altos Resort and Spa. The standard room at Grano de Oro was just perfect... a wonderful combination of glamour and hominess. review_title: Lovely hotel, not sure about the neighborhood
review_text: We stayed here just one night after arriving from the US and left very early the next morning to fly to the Osa peninsula so we didn't get to see as much of the hotel or its surrounds as we would have liked. The room was wonderful - reminiscent of a caribbean plantation house. Beautifully furnished - and with the comfy beds we needed after a long day's travel. We didn't eat in the restaurant but we did go in there for a drink and it looked lovely - partly undercover and partly in an open courtyard full of plants. The hotel had another palnt-filled courtyard that was very nice and which some of the rooms opened on to. We left before breakfast was served and didn't get to go outside, except as we arrived and left in taxis. The neighborhood doesn't look very inviting and it doesn't seem to be easy walking distance to the downtown area and attractions (but I could be wrong about that). All in all - a lovely, relaxing, very well-kept-up hotel. It was rather expensive though - nearly twice as much as the downtown Gran Hotel we stayed in on our way back through San Jose

review_title: An excellent exception in San jose
review_text:
It is extremely difficult to find a quality accommodation in San Jose. Since the capital is often just a stepping stone to other destinations in the country, many hotels are run down or simply just not nice.
Grano de Oro is an exception in this bleak landscape : the setting is simply great, the rooms are big and very nice, the restaurant is very good, and the staff does everything they can to make guests welcome and assist them.
Furthermore, the interior courtyard is a wonderful and soothing place to spend some time.
I've stayed here 3 times in the past month, and would definitely come back here next time I'm in Costa Rica

review_title: Beautifully Appointed in the heart of the City
review_text: We needed a stop before heading to the airport, so we settled on the Hotel Grano De Oro based on the other reviews of the hotel. I'm glad we did. The room was very comfortable and well appointed. We even had our own private courtyard with water fountain. It was very elegant. The breakfast in the morning was the best we had by far on our trip. The food was gourmet and the wait staff was extremely nice. Our waiter went out of his way to tell us how in Costa Rica you only have to pay an additional tip of food service if you feel that it was well deserved. They automatically charge a 10% service fee on the bill. Our nature is to tip 20% back in the states, so we did tip 10% additionally. But we both agreed that it was nice of waiter. I guess he thought we had just arrived in Costa Rica! I would highly recommend this hotel. It's great as a stopover or a full stay as well in Costa Rica. Keep in mind it is about 15minutes to the airport from there. Not a huge deal. But if you have a really early flight you may want to consider staying near the hotel. I also recommend venturing outside the hotel. A 10-15 minute walk to the shopping area is worth it to check out the central market. It's the local market where folks sell fruits, vegetables, meats, and more. It's very authentic as it's not geared towards tourists but local individuals. It was fun walking around, I felt like I was on an episode of Anthony Bourdain!

review_title: The nicest hotel in all of Costa Rica
review_text: If you are an American, you will feel very much at home in this modern, clean, safe former Victorian mansion converted into a charming boutique hotel. There is a lovely courtyard with stained glass and outdoor dining. The grounds have actually several landscaped & well manicured courtyards. The perfect combination of modern and classic, familiar and exotic. The restaurant is very expensive, but the nicest you will find in all of Costa Rica. Even by American standards, this hotel and restaurant are both 5 stars. We didn't much care for San Jose, but you are only a few blocks (or a few dollar cab ride) away from the downtown area or "Cultural Square" which is of course worth checking out if you're in the area. I've been told not to walk around this neighborhood at night. The beautiful building and lush landscaping stick out like a sore thumb in this neighborhood. The front desk staff was fluent in English and incredibly helpful and friendly. Nice gift shop with local art work. The hot tubs on the roof are fantastic and make you feel like you're far away from the dirty city. There is a safe in the room, air conditioning and hot water. You can drink the water here, as there is a filter on campus and there is literature about their filtration process, if you are hesitant. Small hotel - probably about 10 rooms altogether. The elevator only gets you to several of the rooms, some of the rooms require stairs. All the comforts from home. If in the area again, this would be my first choice.

review_title: Historic hotel with class - maybe San Jose's only one with reliably good service
review_text:
This is truly a little gem. It is a little hotel, formerly a mansion owned by a coffee baron, near but not too near the heart of San Jose. I have been in many a hotel in and around San Jose, and throughout the country of Costa Rica. This happens to be the hotel with the best, and in fact one of the only, gourmet restaurants in Costa Rica. If you are looking for a great restaurant with something above the level of fastfood, chains, or that of the Tico diners (called "sodas") food, in other words a more refined cuisine, in San Jose, it is very hit or miss. You might try Macchu Picchu for Peruvian cuisine (pretty good), or Cafe Mundo for various, mostly Italian fare (but a bit hit or miss itself), but if you want something reliably good, and fine, then you have very few choices in Costa Rica.
This is THE restaurant in San Jose, if you want a real restaurant with a fine wine list, and a creative menu with food like you could get in a real restaurant, with a real chef, in a major city in the United States. It is the place if you have a romantic dinner date or any other important occasion requiring a food for discriminating palates.
As for the hotel, it is also the ONLY hotel in San Jose, or even throughout the country, among the many, many in which I have stayed which purport to be 3 to 5 star hotels, where the service was what you would expect - the workers all seem to know what they are doing, want to work, and understand their job is to serve their customers. Most of the hotels throughout the country are overrun with Tico service which is the pits - lazy, even hostile workers who resent their relatively rich foreign guests and sometimes do not hide that fact at all, who have a blase, at best, attitude, and bring down the level of their hotels from what would be 3 or 4 or 5 star hotels (based on the physical features, the amenities, etc.) to a 2 or 2 1/2 star hotel, merely based on their abysmal service and related idiotic management.
If you want perhaps the only hotel in San Jose with great service, in an interesting, museum piece-like hotel (with art inside telling the story of this former home of a coffee millionnaire), with a cute rooftop jacuzzi, and a great restaurant, probably the very best in town, this is your place.

review_text:
We stayed at Grano de Oro for a single night before catching an early flight home the next morning. The hotel provided a restful sleep in a small but beautifully furnished room with comfortable linens (and the first bathtub I had seen in two weeks)! Staff were excellent and ready to assist with anything.
The restaurant is lovely, with a little open-air courtyard and attentive waiters. However the menu is pricey ($100 US for two people) and features top-end dishes that it can't deliver on. We had steak and pasta with pate as a starter, and none of these were interpreted with much skill. Head down for a drink and enjoy the surroundings, but eat elsewhere.

review_title: Pleasant hotel with overpriced and pretentious restaurant
review_text: San Jose isn't much of a tourist destination, but this is a fine place to stay if you want to spend time there. Reviewers who describe the public areas and the rooms as charming are correct. The hotel is 45 minutes from the airport, however. If you are spending just one night before catching a morning flight, the chain hotels nearby are probably a better and certainly much cheaper choice. The restaurant here is very handsome and well appointed, but is also disorganized and, given the New York-level prices, disappointing.

There is virtually nothing to see in town, especially in comparison to the rest of Costa Rica, which is remarkable.

review_text:

The restaurant, again with patio, is one of the best town.
So if you have to visit San Jose, stay here!

review_title: great hotel in a not so great city
review_text: My wife and I didn't want to spend any time in San Jose, but we didn't have much choice as our flight timings didn't allow us to make a same day transfer out of the city. Our travel agent, Highline Travel.com, arranged for our entire costa rica trip including transfers. (I'm going to post more reviews of the other hotels we stayed at). They were right in suggesting this hotel. The rooms were clean and warmly decorated and the showers were good. The hot tub and hotel restaurant meant that we didn't even have to wander around San Jose (which is not very safe) for the few hours we were there. If you are going to be in the city, this is definitely the place to be.

review_text: Didn't expect much of this hotel as it was just a stopover before heading out to Arenal. We were very pleasantly surprised by comfort, luxury, service and amazing food. We spent a Sun. in San Jose and this is a perfect location to step out into the world of the local city dweller. We wandered the shopping district for hours on Sunday and people watched a great deal of the day. We bought great food from a vendor, listened to a street musician, watched a local sports fair, ate at a restaurant tipica, and ended our day on the rooftop deck in the hot tub alone! Followed by a great dinner and breakfast al fresco, we had a marvelous experience. BTW, we stayed in Room 19 which was very roomy and comfortable. The only drawback is that we could hear our neighbors showering and closing their door. Not a big deal.

review_text:

The dining room is so elegant. The food and service topnotch...French chef.
It is a rare treat.

review_text:
My husband and I stayed here when we arrived in Costa Rica and on our final night, for when we were flying out of San Jose. I would recommend this hotel. It is most certainly a 5* but is very good value. The rooms are nice and clean with a good shower.
The breakfast is extra, but very nice and the restaurant is lovely. We had dinner on the final night and it was excellent and very good value for money (you need to book.)
Other tips: we didn't bother going into San Jose itself. We were told there are much nicer places to visit in Costa Rica, so don't bother if you are short of time. We met some people who had been to San Jose, who said that there wasn't much there.
We also hired a 4x4 to get around. It was expensive but money well spent. It made the holiday a lot less stressful and cut journey's down by 50% compared to getting public transport.

review_title: Nice Oasis in the middle of San Jose
review_text: My boyfriend and I stayed here the night before we left Costa Rica. The building is a sight for sore eyes after driving through San Jose. The staff was very friendly and the building is quite unique. It reminded us of an old homestead from New Orleans. The rooms were spotless and looked well kept up. Each room is unique within in the building. We went to dinner at the hotel restaurant and were pleased. The food wasn't outstanding, but it was very good, and very reasonably priced. Again, the decor was beautiful. Highly recommend staying here the last night of your trip if you have an early flight out of San Jose airport the next morning.

review_title: A great boutique hotel to end our CR vacation
review_text: We stayed for two nights Jan. 1 and 2 before flying back to the US. The staff was friendly and helpful during all interactions. The location is only a few blocks from several car rental offices, an easy walk back to the hotel. The front desk knew which restaurants were open on the holiday weekend and guided us accordingly. Breakfast was not included but quite reasonable at ~$10 each including coffee and fresh juice. Our room was decorated warmly and was in perfect condition. We asked for a courtyard room but the hotel was full - ask for one upon booking or at check-in. We soaked in the rooftop hot tubs after walking most of downtown, a nice interlude before going out for dinner. Most of the other guests were like us - zip-off pants and hiking shoes, though most appeared more fresh than us! We have stayed at luxury hotels all over Asia and this hotel was just a nice as any of them. Highly recommended!

review_text:
My husband and I stayed at Grano de Oro Dec 22 thru Dec 26. Needless to say, when booking a Christmas reservation, we really wanted something special. Our stay was fabulous. Friendlieness began at the front desk and was carried on by staff throughout
this beautiful small hotel. Our suite was absolutely perfect, impeccably clean, fresh everyday and a minor maintenance issue attended to immediately. Our dining experiences could not have been improved upon. While the service may be viewed as 'leisurely,' we took advantage of the opportunity to spend time talking and visiting. The wine list is excellent and food presentations whether breakfast or dinner are done with care. If you're lucky, you'll have Walter as your waiter...a fine example of superior service.
For this type is small luxury hotel, there is nothing finer in San Jose.

review_title: Wonderful start to our Costa Rica vacation
review_text: My husband and I spent the first night of our 11 day trip to Costa Rica at the Hotel Grano de Oro. What a delight and fantastic introduction to this beautiful country. From the moment that we checked in, we were greeted and treated with such friendliness and hospitality. The hotel is visually stunning and the lobby, grounds and restaurant were beautifully and tastefully decorated for Christmas. We were given an upgrade for our room which was an unexpected surprise. The restaurant was excellent ! The dinner menu was fairly extensive with plenty of choices, interesting and creative preparations and a pretty good wine list too! We got into a conversation with one of the restaurant's hosts after dinner while taking pictures and what a pleasant exchange we had! Thank you Alvaro for a totally wonderful experience! If spending any time in San Jose, you will not be disappointed staying at Hotel Grano de Oro!

review_text:
We arrived late in the evening on a rainy and chilly night. The greating by the parking attendant set the tone for our two night stay, firiendly, cordial and sincere. We felt immediately welcome.
The Reception Staff were gracious and accomodating (we had way too much luggage) and offered to help without our having to ask. I have to say I did not expect this level of service for the price.
Our room was not large but had a private terrace, a lovely spot with a babbling fountain (which we could turn off if the babling got to be too much, a very nice touch!). Mornings were spectacular with beautiful light and balmy weather, picture a perfect srping day. The only thing i wished that were inlcuded would be a coffee maker in the room, and at least a continental breakfast for that matter.
The room was very clean, the bed was comfortably firm and the fan was more than enough to make the room comfortable. There was a bit of noise from the hallway but most city dwellers would not notice.
They did a very nice job of retrofitting an old mansion into a hotel, the lobby is a little on the grand side, but not overwhelming. The holiday decor was festive and traditional, fitting in beautifully with the architecture. The Xmas music as a little too much, maybe a mix would be easier to digest.
One of the best meals ever had in Costa Rica was at the hotel restaurant: the duck breast was perfectly accompanied and presented beautifully (simple and lovely, no extraneous decoration, it was quite sophisticated), the wine list was very good, and the desserts sublime. The waiter was very nice and happy to help, but he could have been a little more informed, perhaps he was new.
Overall, I am a big fan of Grano de Oro and would recommend it to anyone staying in San Jose. I did not see the basic rooms, but the upgrades are defintely worth it.

review_text: I LOVED Hotel Grano de Oro! We had heard awful things about San Jose and how we should not spend any time there during our time in Costa Rica. Since our flight arrived at 530pm and did not feel safe driving to Arenal at night, we needed to stay in San Jose our first night on our Costa Rican adventure. I heard about this hotel in my Costa Rica for Dummies book which claimed it was the "Best of the Best." When I looked on the website, the hotel looked quaint and elegant. The price of a standard room was very reasonable and I was told their restaurant was excellent so I booked it. After our long flight to San Jose, we wanted to spend as little time in the car as possible... turns out Hotel Grano de Oro was only 20 minutes away from the airport which was perfect! I was so excited to pull up to our hotel. It was so much nicer than what I had expected. It was so beautiful and very elegant. The best part was, it was decorated for Christmas which made it very "home-like." The staff was very nice and accommodating. We stayed in room 13 which was a standard room; fine for just one night. The room was adorable. A bit on the smaller size but it was very cozy and extremely clean. We did not have much of a view from our room, but i wasn’t really expecting any sort of view so it was fine. We ate at their restaurant for dinner which was very nice. The food was great, and reasonable in price. It is the alcohol that is a bit pricey. Since it was our first night in Costa Rica we were unsure of the exchange rate. My boyfriend ordered a glass of wine that ended up costing $60. Opps. It was phenomenal wine, but a bit on the more expensive side. We were told they have amazing desserts at the hotel so we tried what would be a "mud pie." OMG, it was the best slice of pie I had ever had. No lie, it was amazing. I could have eaten the entire pie if I had the stomach for it. For breakfast we ate in their outdoor patio/garden which was very nice and pleasant. I had the huevos rancheros which was probably one of the best huevos rancheros I have had. I was very impressed. Overall, I am so glad we stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro. I would def. go back there, but for longer than one night next time. The only downfall was... I used their public computer in their hotel lobby, thinking it would be safe. Turns out someone hacked into my e-mail account and sent SPAM messages to all of my contacts. It might not have been the hotels fault but just a heads up about using their public computer....

review_text:
Staying at Grano de Oro was a wonderful way to end a fabulous trip throught Costa Rica. This hotel is both charming and luxurious, with design that remains true to its history while appealing to a modern sensibility. There is a very nice roof garden with two hottubs -- my only suggestion is that they amp up the water temperature! It was pleasant but could have been hotter.
The restaurant is what truly stands out in my mind. Do not stay at this hotel without having dinner (and make a reservation, the place seems to fill up, especially on weekend nights!). We had a beautiful meal with impeccable service, and great value -- while more expensive than elsewhere in San Jose, compared to the same quality food in our hometown of Toronto, it was a great deal. Room service is also reasonably priced (with no pesky "tray fee" as we often see in Canada/US!).
All in all, I won't stay anywhere BUT Grano de Oro if I ever return to San Jose.

review_title: Great Little Oasis in San Jose
review_text:
Though the city of San Jose isn't much to look at, once you walk through the doors at Grano de Oro you feel like you're in a new place. The rooms were comfortable and clean and the staff was very helpful.
The restaurant was pretty fancy and the food was very good.
There isn't much in the vicinity of the hotel, but the staff gladly arranged transportation anywhere we wanted to go.
Though we only stayed two nights we had a great experience and recommended it to others.

review_text: We only stayed one night during low season, got upgraded to a deluxe room - it was beautiful. Clean, had a private patio with fountain. review_text:
We stayed at the Grano de Oro on our last night in Costa Rica because of its proximity to the airport and because we had read several reviews from different sources and each one raved about how wonderful the hotel is.
The hotel is beautiful and so much more than I expected. The staff we encountered were very friendly and helpful. The room we stayed in was off of a corridor that looked at over the open air courtyard and restaurant. It was spacious, very nicely decorated and exactly what we were looking for before we started our journey home.
For dinner, we took a taxi to Tin Jo which is a Chinese/Pan-Asian restaurant nearby. The food was amazing. We headed back to the hotel restaurant for dessert, which was equally delicious.
The hotel has a cute gift shop located outside the main entrance for any last minute items you might want to pick up.
The only downside to the hotel is that the area it is located in seems a little seedy.

I will be staying at this hotel every trip back to San Jose in the future for sure!

review_text:
Our real destination in Costa Rica was the Manuel Anotnio National Reserve in Quepos. Which was absolutely beautiful. We chose to stay in San Jose the first night of our arrival as well as the night before our departure, this way we could account for any delays in traveling back and forth from Quepos to San Jose, and be able to enjoy the actual travel and areas we were staying in without feeling rushed. We decided that we stay in what we read to be one of the nicest and highest ranking hotels in San Jose, Grano de Oro.
Our first night was pleasant, they upgraded our suite, which we appreciated - and the room and private terrace was very nice. The bathroom and the entire suite was very clean, and overall comfortable. Though I will say it was very, very noisy, and I had a difficult time sleeping from all the street/city sounds. The service was good our first night here, though I did find that the person working reception was not particularly friendly or personable - I chalked it up to being a late night. Though his attitude was the same the next morning. I am not a nit-picker - but I do think it's important to mention these details when you are under the impression that you are paying for a top quality-"four star" resort, because what makes it high quality ARE the tiny details - or else I'd just stay at a Ramada.
Our last night here, which is also our final night in Costa Rica - was a big disappointment. We arrived to be told that the AC was broken, and their form of compensation was to give us an extra fan. So even though they told us that there was another room available, it was not in the same price category we paid, and it would be extra if we wanted that room. Now after our first experience which was relatively pleasant, I was shocked. And again, the same poor service by the concierge, though it was a different person. No compensation whatsover for the inconvenience of the broken AC - not even a complimentary breakfast, which honestly would have been satisfactory considering that breakfast wasn't included in the first place - to me that would show how important our comfort was and how apologetic they were for having to put us through this inconvenience. I am completely disappointed by their poor customer service - in particular because I expected much more from a hotel that is highly rated and full of incredible customer reviews. Especially since we had such an amazing stay at the Gaia Resort in Manuel Antonio where truly exceptional customer service outshone our experience here at Grano de Oro.
My advice - don't bother "splurging" here in San Jose - if San Jose is just an interim to your Costa Rican vacation, pick a cheap hotel that meets your expetations and go all out on your final destination.

Grano de Oro Hotel is an amazing place to stay. Although the location isn't the greatest in San Jose - it certainly is one of the nicest hotels I've ever stayed in - I would definitely recommend it and come back.
The hotel looks like an old victorian home - and had a nice, European feel to it.
The rooms were very clean and the hotel staff were very helpful and friendly. I would also highly recommend eating at the restaurant here, the food was absolutely awesome. We had breakfast, lunch, and dinner here and were impressed with all of them. It rained most of the time we were there, but we were still able to sit outside under cover in the courtyard for our meals.

review_title: Beautiful hotel, but a ways a way from the San Jose Airport
review_text: We chose this hotel after reading the excellent reviews on Trip Advisor. We stayed there on our last night before flying out very early the next morning to the USA. I thought the hotel was a lot closer to the airport, but it was a $20- $25 cab ride! We got to the hotel late, after taking the public bus from Manuel Antonio to the San Jose Airport (we were advised to get off there because the Coke bus station was too dangerous for two women at night). I was disappointed that the hotel wasn't as close to the airport as I thought. The restaurant was very, very nice-- but way too overpriced for what we wanted. there wasn't anything nearby we could go to. If you have an early flight out I'd recommend staying at the Hampton Inn right by the airport-- it is a little cheaper and has a free shuttle to the airport. I stayed there on my way into the country and it was very good.

review_title: Overrated. Excellent for San Jose, but that's because its San Jose...
review_text:
We had a very, very early flight out the next morning (7:30 am) so we stayed at the Grano de Oro so that we would be close to the airport. Initially, we thought we would also like to check out San Jose itself, after spending 5 days in Jaco and 2 days at Arenal. Seriously, don't bother with San Jose, BUT if you need to be close to the airport, I would highly recommend Grano de Oro as a really nice oasis in the middle of a slum-ish city.
As for the hotel itself, its just fine. We got there at about 2:00 and immediately went to lunch at a nice little Soda around the corner which was delicious (Soda Tilapa, or something. Ask the hotel). Not wanting to leave the safe confines of the hotel again, we booked dinner at the hotel at 8:00, and went to our room to relax. There is free internet in all the rooms, which is a plus, but soon we were bored so we went to the roof deck to enjoy the hot tubs. These were really nice. But to be honest, there isn't anything more to do here.
There is a spa, but it is so small that it can only accomodate one person at a time so either you and your partner have to go separately, or no one goes. We went for the latter option. The hotel doesn't have any other entertainment (ie no pool table, ping pong, etc). So we ended up buying a pack of cards in the gift shop and playing cards and drinking in the restaurant for a few hours before dinner time. It was fine. Knowing the surroundings of the hotel though, I would have appreciated some additional in-hotel entertainment.
As for the room, it was fine. We got the standard room, which was a little small but as we were only staying there one night it was good for us. One pet peeve of mine though was that the hotel did not give you your own soap, shampoo, or lotion. Instead, they had gym-style dispensers on the wall of the shower. I mean really? I know this is a way to cut costs, but it just comes off as tacky in a hotel set inside a victorian style mansion.
Lastly, the dinner. Oy. I wonder if people rating this food have ever eaten anywhere else. The food is okay. We ordered the tasting menu ($65/person) and it was certainly nothing to rave about. My dishes were fine, but my partners were pretty close to terrible. The wine list was also extremely overpriced, and it was $7 per small bottle for bottled water. We remarked during dinner that we should have gone back to the Soda.
One extreme possitive, was that the staff was very friendly and overly helpful. Their front desk is staffed 24/7 and they really do everything possible to look after your every need (including pulling your car around front, greeting you with umbrellas at your car, etc).
Overall, it was a fine experience. This hotel I'm sure is 5 star for San Jose, but for real life, it doesn't meet that high of a mark.

review_text:
We stayed at the Grano de Oro due to having an early flight out. What an unbelievable, unexpected treat! The hotel is beautiful and quaint. The surrounding city is sketchy but the hotel is a nice little oasis, we felt completely safe and we loved the charm of the hotel.
You absolutely MUST try the restaurant. It is advertised as one of the best in San Jose and it lives up to its reputation. I'm not one to be overly impressed by food, but the service was impeccable, the dishes were creative and flavorful, and the restaurant, like the hotel it is in, is exquisite.
We tried out the roof top spa/hot tub which was a nice way to relax at the end of our trip. If you are looking for a place to stay the night you arrive or the night before you leave Costa Rica, I'd highly recommend this hotel.

review_text: There is nothing very special about San Jose, the capital of Costa Rica. But the country is a wonderful vacation, and most flights come in to San Jose. If you decide to stay in San Jose for a night or two, as we did (parents and 3 children, ages 22, 20 and 14) in July of 2010, the Grano de Oro is a must stay. Beautiful, elegant and comfortable rooms in a turn of the century environment that will make you think that you have stumbled into the world of Disneyland's jungle cruise. Nice people, and the restaruant in the hotel is the best in Costa Rica, no kidding. Just an alert- the hotel is in a plain uninteresting part of the city, but frankly the whole city is uninteresting. We spent the full day that we had in San Jose at the the Britt coffee plantation, which was great fun. Loved Grano do Oro.

review_title: Mostly very good, but one exception
review_text:
I am going to give this hotel a mixed review. I stayed there before 8 years ago, and loved it. One night, the only room they had available was their most expensive room, the vista de oro suite. It was wonderful. We had a fruit and cheese basket and the room was incredible. This time, i just had to stay there one night again. We stayed in a deluxe (regular) room the first night. The desk area and dining area had all been changed and updated, and were beautiful. I got in early and they accommodated me in the regular deluxe room, which was very comfortable and clean. I bragged to my cousin who i was traveling with about how amazing the big suite was going to be (we were staying in san jose in the middle of the trip). This time, the room wasn't ready (we were dirty and tired, but this room is worth waiting for. HOWEVER, when we finally got upstairs it looked like they hadn't done a thing to this room, except let millions of people troop through it the past 8 years. It was dark and dingy and not kept up at all, with no air conditioning (the rest of the hotel has it). It looks like your 90 year old grandma lived there and was too old and tired to update, change rugs, or polish any furniture. The jacuzzis just below were the same. That area was uncomfortable, old, falling apart plastic jacuzzis. What a disappointment. And expensive to boot. I wish we had just had a regular room, much nicer. They should be ashamed to sell this room at that price with no updating. We had to leave 5 in the morning and the lighting was so old and poor my cousin left her glasses (we couldn't find anything, it was so dark and dingy) and i left a few things i couldn't see in the poor lighting. Don't stay in this room unless it has been renovated.
.

review_title: Gorgeous hotel that rises above it's surroundings
review_text:
We stayed at this gorgeous hotel for one night after arriving at SJO before we left for Arenal/La Fortuna the next morning. Here is a practical review of all of the info that I wanted before I left. Hope this helps everyone!
1. We stayed Room #8, and it was a gorgeous room! It is a a deluxe king room. This room was very spacious as was the bathroom. The bathroom had his and her sinks, beautiful countertops with plenty of space. It also included a large garden tub/shower. The bed was very comfortable, and we had a great night's sleep in our very quiet room.
2. Access to town-You can defintely walk to the main downtown area (Museo del banco, Costa Rica bank, Mama's Place, market area). It was a 10-15 min walk on sidewalks, and we felt fairly safe in the daytime. The hotel will provide you with umbrellas if needed to take on your walk.
3. Exchage of money-The hotel will gladly exchange your dollars for colones for you at the front desk for the going rate we found on the internet.
4. Restaurant-We ate breakfast and dinner there, and both were great! I would highly recommend it.
We loved Hotel Grano de Oro! The staff was very friendly and helpful. They gave us directions and answered our every question.

3. Exchage of money-The hotel will gladly exchange your dollars for colones for you at the front desk for the going rate we found on the internet.
4. Restaurant-We ate breakfast and dinner there, and both were great! I would highly recommend it.

review_text:
We were invited to a beautiful villa for a week in the Central Pacific Region of Costa Rica (Parrita) and needed to stay in San Jose for one night at the end to scope things out before flying home. I had a friend who now lives in Costa Rica and she recommended the Hotel Grano de Oro.
I contacted the hotel and booked two rooms for our last night and Cynthia promptly return our confirmation and attractive rate. We booked the Deluxe King. Leading up to our trip date I read some reviews here and discovered that not all rooms were air conditioned. Something I never considered, but was thrilled to read about. Naturally, I contacted the hotel again via email and Rolando did acknowledge my request and assigned two Air Conditioned rooms to us.
We left Parrita (Central Pacific) via taxi at 8am and got to the hotel after a very long drive at 5pm. We did ask the taxi to detour to POAS VOLCANO and have our BEST LUNCH at Chubascos.
Walking up the front steps of the hotel with water cascading down on either side is an example of the beautiful flowing waters across the landscape of Costa Rica. The Lobby is a contemporary installation connecting the two old buildings which make up the hotel. The staff were warm and welcoming as was the bellman who escorted s to our rooms 7 and 8 and showed us everything.
Room 8 is an Air Conditioned Deluxe King. On first impression, you think: WOW- Elegant.
The room has dark wooden floors throughout (including the bathroom) and a high ceiling. There was a mini-bar, table with two chairs and tv. The King Bed was a welcome comfort after a week of Eco Adventure. The bathroom featured a His and Hers sink and tub.
The Restaurant is located off the lobby and is around the courtyard. It's Elegant Wine and Golden hues add a richness to this space. It was nice to sit and eat a delicious meal while enjoy the evening rain in the courtyard. By morning the rain had passed and this was the area in which we had a most delicious breakfast.
We asked the front desk to arrange a taxi to the airport, knowing what a previous reviewer had written here about a scam. This was efficiently arranged and we had a comfortable air conditioned minivan to take the three of us and a weeks worth of luggage to the airport at noon. It was prepaid at the Front Desk so I felt very safe about the arrangement.
I loved this hotel and felt I could easily live here. I has a very homely feel to it and its staff all make you feel welcome.
Thank you Hotel Grano de Oro for my last impression of Costa Rica (I'll try to forget the 6 hour delayed AA flight that followed this)

review_title: Wonderful Stay at Grano de Oro
review_text:
I made a last minute decision to stay at the Grano de Oro the night before my flight. It was the best decision I could have made!
I called the day before I needed the room and spoke with Marco. I asked him for the prices for each room and then I told him I wanted a room with air conditioning. He informed me that they were in the process of renovating all the rooms to have air conditioning, but only 10 of the rooms had it and that he would upgrade me at no charge to one of the rooms that had ac. I was given a Deluxe King room for the standard price.
Once I got to the hotel, they had someone immediately take my luggage to the room and explain how everything worked in the room. The room was beautiful. I had an amazing view of the mountains, a flat screen tv, dimmer lights and a jacuzzi tub which I took advantage of.
I had dinner in the hotel restaurant and the entire wait staff was accommodating. Based on reviews here, I decided to try the Passion fruit margarita and it did not dissapoint! It was delicious. I also had a salad with macadamia nuts, gorgonzola cheese and blackberries, seabass and the tres leches cake. Everything I had tasted great and breakfast the next morning was just a great.
I also had a last minute need in the middle of the night and they had someone get the items I needed and bring them to my room.
The jacuzzi on the roof top is really nice and I got to relax there for a bit.
I had absolutely no problems with getting a taxi to the airport. I stopped by the front desk in the morning and told them the time I needed to be picked up. They asked if I would like to charge it to the room or pay for it directly. When I came back downstairs the taxi was waiting for me and I made it to the airport on a Monday morning in less than 20 minutes.
The only complaint I could say I have is that I had asked for a wake up call and they did not call. I did set the alarm on my phone just in case, so it wasn't that big of a deal.
I would definitely stay here again. The food and the service are top notch.

review_title: White Light at the End of the Tunnel
review_text:
I've been meaning to write this review for six + months now - I am a student and didn't have time! However, my experience here was so good, that I felt I needed to say something about it.
As many who travel to Costa Rica know, there is not a lot to do in Jan Jose as a tourist. We stayed here twice on our trip and therefore I can say that their service is very consistent. The first night we had traveled from Chicago and were very tired, the hotel staff picked up on this and recommended a massage. The other thing I liked about this hotel is that they recommended several restaurants in the area, despite having one on premise. We chose to stay on premise and were surprised to find the food to be amazing - surprised, because the staff weren't pushy about trying their restaurant.
We had a great relaxing massage AND they didn't try to force us to buy anything from their spa line, or make us feel bad for not wanting to book a second massage - HUGE PLUS IN MY BOOK - I hate when they do this. The one complaint I had was that my husband I could not get a massage at the same time - but it was a minor inconvenience.
The next day our bill was ready when we got downstairs. We happened to mention that we were checking in again in a few days, from the rain forest to our way to the Pacific side of the country. Upon hearing this the concierge mentioned that he would be happy to hold our bill and we could settle it all at once. That was great, because we ended up saving money on the international transactions!
The second time we arrived late, just in time for dinner. We opted to eat our meal at the restaurant, since we were tired and knew the food was going to be great. The following morning we were offered free coffee at their breakfast bar - which we appreciated.
The ambiance is also very pleasing. The hotel is very light and airy. It has a classic, old world feel. The restaurant has an open air courtyard, but there is also indoor seating options - we sat outside the whole time. Really this place just sneaks up on you in the city, the area it is in is nice, but this is just a gorgeous old world building. I believe it was a mansion, which was converted to a hotel. I highly recommend a night here, if you're in San Jose.

review_title: Charming hotel, with a superb restaurant!
review_text:
If you have to stay a night in San Jose if you're traveling to other parts of the country, this is the place. The staff was extremely friendly, the room was comfortable (we had a room with AC and a cute little patio with a fountain), and the restaurant was excellent!
I wouldn't miss the chance to dine at the hotel's restaurant. It was definitely the best meal of our trip. From the cocktails (passionfruit margaritas) to the duck, to the foie gras mashed potatoes , and the lattes at the end of the meal, we thoroughly enjoyed the food and the charming atmosphere of the restaurant.
A definite highlight of our Costa Rica experience.

The next morning they had a packed breakfast for us because our flight was so early. Next time in San Jose I wouldn't stay anywhere else but here.

review_text: My husband and I stayed here for the last night of our vacation. After spending 3 nights without electricity in Manuel Antonio, we arrived quite early (11am) with hopes of an early check-in and hot shower. The professional and accommodating staff allowed us to check in early and upgraded our room. The hotel was beautiful. The rooms were well-appointed and luxurious. review_title: GREAT SERVICE, GREAT RESTAURANT, GREAT LOCATION
review_text: This beautiful European style hotel has become my base when I travel to San Jose. Just completed my fourth stay. Clients love to join us at the restaurant, which is the most beautiful and one of the best in the city, and my girlfriend and I love the room service, which comes directly from the same restaurant. The macadamia encrusted dorado is the best. The last time we stayed, we received a free upgrade to one of the suites with an enclosed Spanish style patio off the bedroom, complete with running fountain and goldfish. The central location two blocks off Paseo Colon is perfect for getting around, and also just a block away from a classic movie theatre that shows foreign (not Hollywood) films. This is a much better and less expensive option to the major chain hotels.

review_title: 4th time at the hotel and will stay there again
review_text:
I have stayed at the hotel 4 different times in 4 different rooms. All of the rooms are nice and they have many TV channels in English, including FoxNews. The have remodeled the hotel since the last time I was there several years ago. It is now an amalgamation of modern and Victorian styles.
The meals are wonderful at the hotel and well worth the prices. If you have never had Guanábana juice (soursop), try it with your breakfast. It is great! The hotel staff is very helpful and cares about their guests.
The hotel is about a 15 minute or so walk to the city-center. The walking is mostly flat and easy.

review_title: Fabulous hotel, great food, charming oasis in dirty city
review_text: We had a wonderful stay for two of our nights. The first night they put us in a non airconditioned room and it was way too hot. Average temperature over 90 degrees in March. They only have 20 AC rooms so make sure to require one when you make a reservation. The standard rooms are small but well appointed. The restaurant is fabulous- the best in San Jose and possibly in Costa Rica. Plan to splurge on a dinner here, you will not be disappointed. This hotel is great if you like boutique hotels, there is a tremendous attention to detail and lots of nice touches, but bring your own computer if you want to get out on the internet. The one available in the lobby tends to be busy.

review_text: On our recent trip to Costa Rica, my husband and I spent our first and last night's at Grano de Oro. On the first, we got an okay room that was located in their small courtyard. The room was stuffy and perfectly fine, but was not what I had expected (I had read quite a bit of the hotel and thought the room would resemble the pictures). Sound also carried really easily around the courtyard, as we could hear someone talking right outside our window. When we returned for our second night's stay, we got a free upgrade to a superior room and it was A LOT nicer. We had air conditioning (we didn't need to use), hardwood floors, a nice bathroom, and a small little garden with a bubbling stream. It was so nice that I was sad to leave it the next morning for the airport. If you're deciding to go, I would go for a superior room, which is not that much more expensive than the standard and is much more comfortable.

review_text: After landing at the airport and picking up our car we headed into San Jose. The traffic was a bit hectic but Grano De Oro is just at the tip of the city so it's easy to get to. Just be careful with the one way streets around the hotel. We parked our car in their gated garage and got to the hotel. As you can see from the pictures the hotel from the outside is beautiful and you wouldn't think you were in SJ. Check in process was simple and we got into our small but very comfortable rooms. We made reservations and had a 5 star dinner. It was pricier than most of other Costa Rican restaurants but none of them were a gourmet restaurant nor French style service. With drinks and food it was a $100 dinner for a couple. Then we checked up the hot tub which was great with good views if you can look over the fence. This was a great start for our 9 day trip in Costa Rica. If you come in late to San Jose or have an early flight out this is the hotel to stay, or for any other reason you want...

review_title: Outstanding! Best option in San Jose!!
review_text: This hotel is extremely elegant and tasteful, and a wonderful place to stay in San Jose. We spent a week traveling Costa Rica and spent our last night here, and it was an extremely memorable and special experience. The rooms are gorgeous, the service is impeccable, and the restaurant cannot be beat!! Dinner was pricey, but reasonable considering the quality and worth every cent.

review_text:
Grano de Oro is THE place to stay in San Jose. It's beautiful, comfortable, and the restaurant is DELICIOUS! Make sure to bring a sweater and something slightly dressy (church dressy, not ball dressy) because Ticos who are at the same restaurant tend to dress up for dinner. My husband and I were beach bumming it in Costa Rica and when we returned to fly out of San Jose we were cold (you're in the mountains and nights get chilly) and felt slightly underdressed.
The restaurant is AMAZING. The food is some of the best in the country. When you fly in and out of CR either stay at Grano de Oro or the surrounding areas- nothing else!

review_title: Elegant end to a family vacation
review_text: We loved Grano de Oro. We didn't love San Jose, but had to stay one night to catch our plane home. Thank goodness we had such a nice hotel to come back to after exploring the city. We did like the Museo de Oro (Pre-Columbian gold museum), but other than that, didn't find a lot to love about San Jose. The hotel is another matter all together. It's removed from the gritty, congested center of the city, and is just lovely. The service is fantastic, and we loved our room, (#19) facing a leafy courtyard. It did seem like some of the other rooms could be noisy, as there was a "silencio" sign outside of one located in a trafficked hallway. The breakfast at the lovely hotel restaurant was the best meal we had all week. If you have to be in San Jose, the Grano de Oro is the place to stay.

review_text:
Great property! I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again. Exceptional service, excellent restaurant, and a peaceful location in a not-quite-so-hospitable town.
There didn't appear to be air conditioning here, but the night was so comfortable, it wasn't needed. The hotel is a bit of a jumble - looking like a mash-up of more than one property. But that really isn't a problem since each little nook and cranny created by the many walkways and alleyways were well appointed with native plants and/or artwork.
Overall, Grano de Oro was a very lovely, very inviting property.

review_text:
The Grano de Oro is a little gem to be found in the unspectacular San Jose. Costa Rica is such a stunning country that this was the perfect place to start a vacation. The hotel is in the west of the city, a $20-25 cab ride from the international airport and about $15-20 from the local airport (Sansa, NatureAir). The actual hotel is beautiful but the surrounding buildings/area are more typical of San Jose - a little urban run down.
The staff are excellent and provided a very warm welcome after a long flight. The main reception area is very nice but the rooms are really a treat. It feels like you are staying at your wealthy friend's country house. You feel immediately at home and relaxed, not like a hotel at all in that way.
What is really remarkable about this hotel is the restaurant. It's simply excellent. It offers some of the best food we had in Costa Rica and compares very favourably with top class restaurants in London, New York etc. The prices are high for Costa Rica but reasonable when you consider the quality. If you stay here, eat here. If you don't stay here, come here to eat! The cocktails are excellent also!
If I return to San Jose, there is nowhere else I would even consider staying. Truly excellent.

review_text: We just left San Jose and stayed at the Grano de Oro on both our first and last nights in Costa Rica. The hotel is fantastic. The decor is very up to date while still maintaining a French Colonial feel to it. The check-in process was quick and easy and they even gave us an upgrade to a nicer room. The prices are very reasonable - the cost for our standard room (which was upgraded) was around $123 a night. Both of our rooms were clean, simply, but elegantly furnished, with updated bathrooms. The best part of the hotel was the restaurant. We ate four meals here and I wish I could take it home with me. Absolutely fantastic food for relatively reasonable prices (compared to the same type of restaurant in the U.S.). This hotel is great. A couple of points - the area around it isn't very nice, but probably no worse than anywhere in San Jose. We just stayed in the hotel, but the neighborhood didn't feel dangerous. Also, be forewarned that there is no A/C in the rooms. They have ceiling fans and it is designed to sleep with the windows open. The temperatures were in the mid/upper 60s at night and it was very comfortable, even with the window closed. I highly recommend the Grano de Oro (and especially the restaurant).

review_title: An elegant oasis in San Jose.
review_text:
We spent 3 nites in this lovely boutique hotel in #10, a Deluxe King room on the second floor. It was attractive and comfortable with large windows overlooking the hotel entrance and front street.
While the entire hotel is loaded with character, the highlight for us was the beautiful dining room with its plant-filled courtyard, interesting artwork, luxurious decor, stained glass windows and sparkling lights. We ate half a dozen meals there and the food was consistently delicious, ranking up with the best we’ve had during our travels to many parts of the globe. An impressive wine list, top-notch service and (for that calibre of dining) reasonable pricing as well.
Staff throughout the hotel were very friendly and helpful. Honest too- a handbag that was left behind in the bar was returned with everything- including money, credit cards, and ID- intact.
What we found truly unfortunate was most of the neighbouring properties are surrounded by high, barbwire-topped walls or heavy iron security fences and we were warned by hotel staff and other locals that it was not safe to walk around outside after dark (5 PM) because there had been a lot of armed robberies in San Jose.
We arranged our private tour of the country and the hotel booking through Costa Rica Expeditions and would recommend them highly. Our CRE guides were excellent at identifying flora, locating elusive fauna and explaining sites and customs of significance. The vehicles were clean and comfortable and the drivers were competent and safety-conscious. ( After observing other local drivers and experiencing some of the muddy, narrow, heavily-rutted roads which wound up and down mountains , we were glad we had decided not to rent a car and drive ourselves. )

review_text:
We chose Hotel Grano de Oro for our 6 day vacation to San Jose, Costa Rica.
Hotel:
We made our reservation directly with the hotel and the process was quick and easy. A week before arrival we were contacted to ask if we wanted to arrange airport to hotel transport for $30. This is actually a good deal because the service is private, safe and clean.
The hotel is actually a gorgeous Victorian house that has been converted into a small hotel. We stayed in room 1 for our visit which is a small, comfortable room located very near the lobby area. The room was relatively quiet, very chic with a nice bathroom. The one drawback is that the bed is small and firm.
The bed seemed too small for comfort. The hotel provides free WiFi and in-room safe (need to ask for the key, and if you lose it it’s a $10 surcharge).
We particularly enjoyed the fresh fruit juices served during breakfast (at no cost). In fact, breakfast was great at this hotel. However, dinner is relatively expensive. Expect to spend $50 or more for two on dinner at the Grano de Oro Restaurant. The hotel is located close to (walking distance) Kentucky Fried Chicken, Quiznos, Pizza Hut and various other chain fast food venues.
The spa services were great and not over-priced. Lara gave my wife a hot stone massage and me a regular massage.
The staff was exceptionally polite and all seemed fluent in English.
Location:
The location was not great but good. It was a long walk from downtown San Jose. However, the Sabana bus runs near by and for ₡150 ($0.27) will drop you off in downtown. You can chose to get off at either the National Theatre or the National Museum. The buses seemed safe and were reliable. The drivers were more than willing to suggest what stop to get off on and would even let us know when we had arrived.
Hotels seem to always recommend taxis. City buses are much cheaper and in this case, can get you anywhere in the city.
Just a block away from the hotel there is a small one screen movie theater – we watched an Oscar nominate foreign film (in Spanish). There is also a theater with play productions, but none were playing while we were there.
San Jose:
San Jose is surprisingly small. This makes it easy to see most of the sites in a few days. Often we were back in our room by nightfall so we are not sure how the city operates at night. However, from what we saw, San Jose is probably enjoyable for day and night activities.
