review_title: Absolutely lovely! A gorgeous hotel and restaurant!
review_text: My husband and I absolutely loved the Grano de Oro. For whatever reason, we were upgraded to a suite and it was one of the most beautiful and charming rooms I've ever had the privilege of staying in. The tile floor and rich woods were unique and elegant. The room had an AMAZING view of San Jose and the surrounding mountains. Our room had a hot tub and we took a long soak and watched the clouds roll in off the mountains. The restaurant is just as beautiful - tastefully decorated with excellent service. We had a GREAT time and it was the perfect end to our trip. HIGHLY recommended.

review_title: Elegant hotel with old world charm
review_text:
This was our first trip to Costa Rica and we stayed in San Jose for 2 nights before heading on to Manuel Antonio. The hotel is an elegant, old victorian home that has been beautifully renovated. I would say that it has the intimate feel of a bed and breakfast with the modern amenities and service you expect of a large hotel. We arrived super early in the morning and our room was not ready so we had a delicious traditional Tico breakfast in the tranquil courtyard surrounded by exquisite stained glass windows. Skip the orange juice and try the fresh passion fruit juice, it was the best I had during our week long stay in Costa Rica. We also had lunch in the restaurant, it was also delicious.
Paseo Colon, which is sort of the main street near the hotel is close by and has shops, restaurants, and colorful characters. Our room was small and clean, very cozy for 2 people. The service was impeccable. Front desk staff are very professional and friendly, you can rely on their guidance. They made restaurant reservations and arranged our day tour to the volcano. We were invited to dinner at a Costa Rican friend's home in Tibas, the hotel arranged for a private driver and had a floral arrangement delivered to the hotel so that we could take it with us for our host. It was truly a stress free, perfect stay at this wonderful hotel.

review_title: Perfect Starting/Finishing Point for Costa Rican Adventure
review_text:
This was stop #1 and stop #6 in our 13 day itinerary throughout Costa Rica and what a great start and finish. This was an Anniversary trip for my wife and I and included stays in San Jose, Tortuguero, La Fortuna (Arenal), Monteverde and Manual Antonio, before returning back to San Jose and our flight back to reality. You can find reviews of all of our stays by clicking on my profile and searching these out. (what a trip!)
I used a local Tour company for all arrangements (hotels and excursions) in advance and for all transportation throughout Costa Rica. “CostaNica Tours” – We were very pleased with their service and drivers. The entire trip went like clockwork – no surprises or disappointments. Highly recommended.
After a long flight in, we were thrilled with the Grano de Oro as the embarking point for our dream trip. This hotel has a ton of character – I’m not sure there would be any 2 rooms alike. Small gardens, walkways, fountains, etc throughout the property. On our first night, we stayed in the “new wing” of the hotel, and as a result, our room had A/C. The climate in San Jose in November (and year round I understand) is moderate, so perhaps not required, though it was nice to be able to block out the city street noises and have a very restful first night. We had a room in the older part of the hotel on our way back through – and while the open windows provided a nice breeze, as mentioned, the early morning noises of trucks, buses, etc., did make it tough to think about sleeping in. The furniture in the rooms has lots of unique character too.
Some of the highlights here: We enjoyed the rooftop hot tubs as nightfall descended, as well as a wonderful meal in the hotel restaurant – amongst our best while in Costa Rica. The service was excellent, and the ambience with the open courtyard served as a great backdrop for our meal. Lots of great local beers to try while in Costa Rica and at the Grano – Imperial is the standard (and good), though I preferred the Bavaria or Pilsen. We had a great breakfast on our last day there and I have to recommend trying the “Hosta Manana” coffee treat served there. Certainly on the decadent side, but a ‘shot glass’ half filled with condensed milk on the bottom and topped off with strong Costa Rican Expresso is both delicious and a great start to the day. (I asked for this elsewhere on our trip and was told the locals call this “Bonbon” – Mmmmmmm!) Internet was available free to guests on a laptop in the lobby which made sending an email or two easy and for checking on flight status, etc as well.
Our flight home on our last day was delayed, so we went for a walk downtown from the hotel to a pedestrian shopping mall maybe a 10 min walk. Great for filling up on souvenirs if required, or lots of sports stores, dep’t stores, drug stores, eateries, etc.
All in all, the perfect way to start and/or finish a trip to Costa Rica!

review_text:
The Grano de Oro is a charming hotel, formerly a private house. It is located in a quiet area of town, tough a bit far from the centre (I don't mind walking for a mile to get to the city centre, but some people might find this too far away, and in the evening you have to take a cab to go to restaurants as it would be a bit dangerous to walk).
The rooms are relatively small (I recommend you opt for the deluxe rooms as the standard rooms are definitely very small). They are nicely decorated, not luxurious but charming. Be aware there is no air con, but it is usually not that hot in San Jose so you are OK without AC.
The front staff is very friendly and helpful.
The restaurant serves delicious food, the service is good. Only downside: the waiters are not particularly friendly, they never smile and have absolutely no charme, what a pity for a country where people usually are extremely friendly. But this is the only point I can raise, the rest was fine.
There are limited services as it is a small hotel (e.g. if you look for gym, pool, business centre etc, this is not your place), but very charming and for me the best option in San Jose (actually there are not that many options) - definitely the most luxurious you can get in San Jose.

review_title: A charming hotel, great standard of service and opulence
review_text:
The building, the rooms & the service were all of a high standard for Costa Rica . The staff in particular were extremely helpful and knowledgeable, nothing was a problem. The restaurant menu looked really good but we decided to go out and explore so didnt eat there. We did however go in for a glass of wine at the end of our evening out - wow, so expensive - they even charged $6 just for a sample taste !!!! The cost of the room along with the level of service received was worth the visit - a great hotel.
There is not very much in the immediate vacinity with the exception of a few restaurants - we went to a peruvian restaurant 5 minutes from the hotel which was really interesting, good food and live music. It is only 15 / 20 minutes walk to the main shopping street & tourist attractions. The walk to the tourist area was busy, the sidewalks were crammed with people and the roads were extremely busy and in parts difficult to cross.
We stayed here on the last night of our vacation prior to flying home. We had been to Monteverde, Arenal and Guanacaste prior to arriving in San Juan which were all amazing. If I did the trip again I wouldnt have stayed in San Juan at all - it was a scruffy city with a bit of an edge to it but the hotel was a really welcome surprise so if you find yourself needing an overnight stay in San Juan this hotel is a great option. Costs around $20 - $25 to get to the airport.

review_text: The Hotel Grano de Oro was an excellent stopping point during my recent stay in Costa Rica. I stayed in San Jose on the days after/before flying in/out and I couldn't have been more impressed with the service and accommodations. The staff was exceedingly professional and quickly responded to all of our needs. The rooms were large, clean and luxurious. The beds were amazingly comfortable, which was much appreciated after 10 days in the jungle! The roof top hot tub was a perfect place to unwind after a long, cold day of white water rafting. The location is a bit removed from either the airport or central downtown, but both were a short trip and hotel's rooms and service more than made up for location.

review_text:
If Grano de Oro was located in a chic part of New York, Chicago or LA, it would be extolled as the perfect boutique alternative to the local Four Seasons. The hotel and restaurant are gorgeous and the welcome is warm and genuine. I have been in more opulently luxurious hotels and many hotels have longer lists or services and facilities, but few nicer hotels exist. I LOVED this hotel! I have stayed at several Relais and Chateau properties and this hotel fits that model to a T.
San Jose is not a tourist's city. It is the humble capital of a developing nation. One visits for a specific reason. Consequently Grano de Oro came as a surprise and delight. It is an oasis in San Jose. The good news about San Jose for me was that I never felt threatened or unsafe.
The hotel (30 to 40 rooms) appears to have been two grand, circa 1900 homes that have been artfully joined by a 21st century glass addition. The interior features abundant use of gorgeous wood columns, moldings, bannisters and floors set off against beautiful silk draperies and lush upholstery and enhanced by tropical plants and flowers. The architect and designers deserve awards and bonuses. The website's pictures do not do it justice.
The restaurant is the most beautiful room in a gorgeous, small hotel. The food is also excellent. I had three dinners and two lunches and every meal was good. Dinners are definitely a 'fine dining' vs 'getting something good to eat' experience.
Being by myself I opted for an entry level 'standard queen' room. It was smallish (perhaps 12 X 14), simply (but very tastefully) furnished with wicker table and chairs, antique armoire and a very comfortable bed. It was not air conditioned, but a/c wasn't needed at all in October. The colors, art and juxtaposition of styles made for a very pleasant space. The bathroom was very Restoration Hardware, neither large nor small, and had a shower, but no tub. It was fine for just me, but would have been a bit tight had I not been traveling alone. FYI- they have 3 or 4 categories of larger rooms.
The very best feature of the inexpensive room was that a modest price enabled me to stay at a gem of a hotel without being in a closet. The price/value balance is perfect.
I have been talking about this hotel for two weeks now. I was so impressed. If you prefer brand new Westins to boutiques, this may not be for you. However, if historic character and charm combined with the finest materials while avoiding glitz of any kind is important to you, make a point of staying at this hotel when you are in San Jose.

review_title: When I die and go to heaven, it will be Grano de Oro
review_text: That may be an overstatement, but here's the deal: we had spent several days on the coast and loved it, but excellent food and superb lodging were not on the list of things we were able to enjoy there. On our way out of Costa Rica, we decided to treat ourselves and stayed at Grano de Oro. I can't describe just how delicious the food was, how divine the rooms with their open windows on the patio, the jacuzzi, the totally charming wait staff in the restaurant--it was all too too dreamy and we fell totally in love with it. It was the perfect close to a lovely CR trip.

review_text: The moment you pull up in front of the Grano de Oro hotel you know you have arrived at some place special. You are greeted; curb side, with warm smiles. Suddenly your luggage and all other arrival incidentals are taken care of as you are helped out of your vehicle and assisted in every way possible to make your way to reception. Our first impression (and always is) “We’re going to like this place”. We stayed at the Grano de Oro three (3) nights, Oct. 10-11 and again, Oct. 16, 2009. The first two nights on our arrival into Costa Rica, from home. The last night, a week later; the night before our departure home. We love the Grano de Oro for its excellent service, gracious attention to detail, wonderful open air, or covered dining, and wonderful menu with many delicious selections, and comfortable rooms. The restaurant serves great fare, breakfast, lunch and dinner. The wait staff will even work with you, the night before, to insure that you have a good breakfast, or snack before your (our) early airport departure, or early morning tour pickup. We’ve found the staff always ready to please, no matter what we needed; wake up calls, faxing, or leaving one of our suitcases for a few days, as we traveled to a more remote part of the country, restricting “so many” suit cases in the small boats or planes we would be taking. Our favorite room is the Garden Suit, with attached small garden patio. Located in a stately remodeled mansion, in a quiet neighborhood, the Grano exudes class and is a welcome haven for tired travelers, looking to recharge, after a long day of air travel or busy day of local site seeing. For us, it offers a relaxing and sophisticated atmosphere that’s a joy to return to, time after time. We are personally welcomed by Christian, front desk, and many of the staff, even if it’s been a several years since our last visit. When in San Jose, we won’t stay anywhere else. The Grano de Oro embodies the comfort, services and attention to detail that we look forward to and appreciate.

review_text: We stayed at the Grano de Oro on our first and last nights of our 10 day vacation in Costa Rica . The bellstaff greeted us at our car and were very nice and the front desk staff was very pleasant . Our first night we stayed in room 15 , a small ( very small ) poorly ventilated room . Our window open to a small area with exposed pipes , plants and we shared this avenue of fresh air with another room whose open window was a couple of feet away . With paper thin walls and a window so close , we now know more about our neighbors that night than we wanted to , including how much they enjoyed their active sex life . The resturant was georgeous to look at but the food was terrible and the "service " was poor at best . My wife had the encrusted sea bass . They should change te name to crusty sea bass , it was so overcooked that my wife had to carve it . I ordered a coffee cocktail off the drink menu that my waiter not only could't describe but he admitted that he had never heard of it . After dinner I requested or check , when our waiter went to get it he must have forgotten what he was doing . After waiting for him to return I went to find him and found him with our check in hand shooting the breeze with the bartender and another waiter . On the last day of our vacation we were again back at the Grano de Oro ( we had prepaid for the 2 nights prior to our vacation , or we wouldn't have ever come back ) . This time we were given room #35 ( even smaller than our first room .) The windows opened into the second patio area / hallway . We didn't have to share our much desired peace and quiet with close neighbors this time , just with everybody that walked to their rooms . We stayed in 4 hotels during our stay . all with 4 or 5 star ratings . But with the Grano de Oro I must say that no matter how much you polish a turd it is still just a piece of crap .

review_text:
We spent one night at Grano de Oro and were amazed by how nice the hotel was for such a reasonable price. It's a beautiful hotel, a careful combination of modern and historic, and I wish there were more hotels like it everywhere I travel.
Nearly everything about our stay was perfection. The reservation process was simple (with confirmation within 2 hours), check-in was smooth and we were given a complimentary upgrade for our anniversary. We had booked a standard room, but I'd recommend paying a little extra for a superior. The room was charming, with a nice patio and fountain that had small fish. The bed linens are high quality, and even the soap in the bathroom is above average. We had dinner at the restaurant; the waiters seemed indifferent but the food was delicious and reasonably priced. The rooftop jacuzzi deck is an incredible little gem, I wish we'd had a morning to spend there.
There were traces of construction, with a small amount of noise in the morning, but nothing interfered with our stay. Even the contractors were polite, greeting us with a smile when we passed them in the hallway. I've never experienced that before, but it definitely left an impression.
Although San Jose isn't much of a destination, we did venture into the neighborhood a bit. It's a safe area, with a few shops and a strip of rental car shops (which was perfect for our needs) within a few blocks. The front desk recommended two grocery stores in the area, Pali and Mas x Menos, where we picked up food for breakfast and lunches over the following days.
Even if you only have a night in San Jose, Grano de Oro is a must-visit hotel. From the staff to the rooms to the luxe public spaces, this hotel is fantastic in so many ways.

review_title: Peace and tranquility in the city
review_text: We spent our last night here before flying back to the US. After a week in the jungle it was bliss to walk into this beautiful hotel. We had two rooms, one with 2 adults and 1 child and the other with 2 adults and 2 children. When we booked all that was left were two rooms with 2 queen beds. The rooms were very large compared to the standard hotel room so we didn't feel cramped at all. Very quiet hotel considering you are almost in the middle of San Jose. There is no pool but there is a rooftop garden with two hot tubs. The kids loved this during the day but I can see it being a very romantic spot in the evening for adults. We had our final evening dinner in the hotel restaurant which is considered one of the best in town. Very elegant, top notch service and outstanding food. Very pricey, especially after $4 arroz con pollo most of the week. Nice final evening after a spectacular week. The hotel is really not near anything for tourists but a 5 minute taxi ride gets you into the heart of San Jose. Very nice gift shop with surprisingly good prices. I got a banana paper pad as a last minute gift for $4 and it was $14.99 at the airport. If you've forgotten any gifts, know you are not getting ripped off here. Staff was very good about giving directions and advice and setting up car service and ordering taxis. Great way to end our trip.

The room was perfect for us and our two children, ages 8 and 10, but even more, we LOVED our fabulous drinks and dinner at the restaurant Saturday night - the server was attentive to all of us, including our kids, and our food was fabulous. It was the perfect way to wind down from our travel from the states and begin our trip. Our room was very nice and just the right size for the 4 of us.
Our bright, fresh and scrumptious breakfast was almost as good as our dinner...a wonderful way to start the day travelling to the mountains. Everyone made our first night in Costa Rica so special. My husband and I stayed here about 11 years ago and the improvements and expansions made enhanced the hotel, but kept what was so special the first time! Even my kids said it was one of their favorite hotels!!

review_text:
Wow. I really wasn't expecting anything like this when I decided to check in to somewhere nice for my final night in Costa Rica. I only wish I'd found it earlier on in my trip. It's a beautiful building of a certain age which has been renovated and maintained in an extremely stylish way; very sympathetic to its original structure.
I had a plush room on the ground floor which was set in a courtyard that had plants aplenty. It felt very tropical. It was a good size (by my UK standards) and I wanted for nothing. The communal areas are lovely and peaceful.
The restaurant and bar are amazing. The right side of upmarket without being stuffy. Felt very special and the food and cocktails did not disappoint. Really, really good.
The location is not why you choose this hotel, but taxis are plentiful to get you into town and back without it marring the experience.
Loved it.

review_title: Nice hotel, but not for resting nor walking around
review_text:
The good: This hotel is very pretty and staff was always welcoming and helpful to us. Bathroom was big and the rooms, although not big, have enough space to feel comfortable. Also have a closet to put your things inside. Most of them have a window which is nice as you can see the garden and listen to the birdies singing. They have a flat panel TV with plenty of cable channels.
The Bad: Location: It is located in the center, and even though that could be nice is some places, not in San Jose, it is a very busy, contaminated and unsafe city to walk around, so, you will either need to get a cab or stay confined in your room, and just so you know we are not easy to feel intimidated as we are from South America, but believe this city is not nice to go your own.
Breakfast is not included. And, although is it not expensive, the rate (we paid $115 per room), would be more reasonable if BF was factors in
Noisy: There is no soundproof so, you will hear all the walking and talking in all the rooms around you, also, as rooms DO NOT have air conditioner, you also hear the birds that start singing at 5am, this is unavoidable as you must sleep with the window open unless you wanna cook yourself to death, which brings me to the last bad.
Heat: Rooms can get very hot, San Jose has a pretty tropical weather and depending on the day temperatures can be quite high. Honestly i should have know there was no AC i would have picked a different place. Other than in a front beach place a Caribbean hotel without AC is a no no for me. My husband was sweating all night and when it started to get fresh it was almost sunrise time and birds started singing lol
Maybe it is better in another time of the year, maybe if you get one of the top floor rooms, maybe if they instal AC in rooms, then maybe it would be nicer to stay here.
Best thing of the place is the restaurant for sure, dont leave without dining there

review_text:
We stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro our first night and our last night in Costa Rica. The architecture, decor (Victorian), the finishes (dark wood and marble), all the small intricate tiled courtyards with fountains scattered around the hotel … it is absolutely delightful. We wandered around the hallways and you never knew when you would come across another courtyard and fountain. And they are all different and all beautiful.
We had two different rooms (arriving and departing) and both rooms had their own private enclosed courtyard with a fountain and plants outside of the room. Glass doors open into the courtyard from your room. Ornate wrought iron extends over the top of the courtyards that are open to the sky.
Our rooms were especially comfortable and very clean. The bathrooms have a soap, shampoo, and conditioner dispenser. Our bed was fantastic. We couldn’t have been more comfortable.
The restaurant has outstanding food. It is on the expensive side, but well worth it. We had breakfast, lunch, and dinner and everything was delicious. The center of the restaurant is an open courtyard with tables. At night there are fairy lights in the plants … it is magical. But you can also sit inside looking out to the courtyard. The service is faultless. My husband and I aren’t used to places like this. My husband asked repeatedly, can we afford to stay here?!
Our reservations were made through Costa Rica Expeditions and everything went so smoothly. We were not concerned about the hotel being in a bad part of town. We aren’t city people so we just stayed in the hotel. We took one walk around the block and it did not look too bad to us … but any city in the world can be dangerous.
If you ever have the chance, stay at the Hotel Grano de Oro, it is beyond doubt a great place to stay. We highly recommend this hotel and we would love to stay here again. Please feel free to send me a message if I can answer any questions.

review_text:
This restored mansion is very beautiful with modern conveniences and indoor and outdoor gardens make this a unique property.
However, there was a mix-up about a breakfast voucher. Rather than acoomodate us or figure out a way to resolve the matter, the staff was stiff, didn't know how to handle the situation and after talking with 4 people at the front desk, no one seemed to know what to do, including an assistant manager.
At these prices, this was an unnacceptable response and a very awkward circumstance for a guest to face. Breakfast is pretty cheap: but this review will stay on the site for some time. Plus, service in their dining room for both breakfast and dinner was a bit slow and inattentive.
With some front desk and dining room training, the place could surely improve another guest's experince in the hotel.

review_text: I loved this hotel! Approximately four years ago, I visited Grano de Oro Restaurant for dinner. I was very impressed with the service and the meal itself. Because I live in the US, I compare the prices to American prices. I thought we got excellent value for both the meal and the service. We were four women, at one point the waiter overheard us talking about needing to get two cabs, (We were going in different direction) he immediately offered to get the cab for us. We had a complete three course meal plus drinks...we were so impressed we talked about it for days... Last month, my husband, two friends, and me, decided to travel to Costa Rica. Because of our past experience in the restaurant, we decided to try the hotel....It was fabulous!! I felt has if I was staying in someone's guest room. The rooms were beautiful!!... small, but beautiful and clean. My husband and I had a queen size bed, with a beautiful iron headboard... I don't believe we had air conditioning, we had an overhead fan. Because the weather was so pleasant in San Jose, we did not miss the air conditioner. The room also had a little sitting area, an armoire, and two glass topped side tables with an iron base that matched the headboard. The wood floors were beautiful, and so was the beautiful beaded board used in the ceiling. The walls were painted a nice pale blue with white trim. The bathroom was small but very efficient and also very nice. The room had a sort of Victorian feel to it. We also had the little patio, and I loved the sound of the birds waking me, after all this is Costa Rica!! My Husband and friends all feel the same way. We wished we could have stayed longer

review_text:
We needed to stay one night in San Jose simply because we were being picked up from there for our trip to Tortuguero. Largely based on reviews on TA, we chose Hotel Grano de Oro.
First impressions were good, it is a lovely building and our check in was handled efficiently and pleasantly. We booked a superior room (one up from the bottom category). It was reasonably compact (therefore I think the base grade room would be just too small, even for one night) but the room was clean and had everything we needed for a single night stay. Since we had a few hours to kill we decided to take a stroll to downturn San Jose. Based on what we’d heard we didn’t have high expectations and I would wholeheartedly agree that it’s not a particularly alluring city. We actually decided to return to the hotel after just half an hour as we were attracting lots of attention on the street and were starting to feel not overly comfortable or safe. This was without question the only time we felt like this during our two and a half weeks in Costa Rica. So we returned to our room and watched a bit of TV before dinner (plenty of cable channels but predominantly US – no BBC). We were booked into the hotel restaurant for dinner as we’d read the great reviews. The restaurant itself is very beautiful and plush, and both the meal and service were very good, but not mind blowingly good. It was however, a pleasant evening and we felt the prices were quite reasonable given the restaurant’s reputation and capital city location (we actually paid more for a meal in Manual Antonio).
We returned to our room for an early night as we needed to get up the following morning at 5am. It was at this point that our stay started to become a bit of a disappointment as the hotel did not deliver the one thing that we really wanted from it – a good night’s sleep! We had two problems:
Noise: our room was on the ground floor and the room immediately above us was occupied. As we learned, there is no soundproofing between the upper and lower rooms and regrettably the couple above us stomped around, threw things on the floor, moved luggage etc until about 1am. Whilst this somewhat comes down to bad luck in getting neighbours who had no consideration for others I think that the hotel is also to blame for not investing in reasonable sound proofing for the comfort of their guests. Building standards for a house (which the hotel originally was) are different to what is needed in a hotel and it seems that in the conversion process soundproofing wasn’t considered a necessary investment. So our tip from this experience is, if you do decide to stay here, make sure you book a top floor room.
Heat: The other reason that we didn’t get a good night’s sleep is that we were uncomfortably hot all night. Until we arrived I was unaware that the room would not be air-conditioned (guess I should have asked the question but because of the standard of the hotel I naively assumed). It was a rather warm, still night when we visited and I imagine that this is the case most of the year. The ceiling fan didn’t cut it, and the only other option was to open the windows which I have no objection to in principle but the windows are unscreened and opened onto a lush green courtyard with a healthy mosquito population. So the choice was to be eaten alive or to sweat it out.
My final comment about the hotel is that it was the only hotel we stayed in that did not include breakfast in its room rate. Everywhere else we stayed offered something, ranging from a modest continental to a breakfast fit for a king. Although we were leaving early it didn’t really bother us but do factor the extra cost in if you are planning to stay in this hotel and would like to have breakfast.
Overall, a bit disappointing really.

review_title: Elegant but Quaint, Beautiful Cafe, Small room
review_text:
My wife and I stayed here one night before catching a bus out of the Coca Cola terminal for Manuel Antonio the next morning. It was only a five minute cab ride to the bus station, and about a 25 minute cab ride from the airport.
We loved the architecture, the elegant cafe, the food, the service and the location. The room was clean, the bed was soft, the shower hot. The room itself was tiny, as was the bathroom. Not a big deal for one night, but if I was staying in San Jose for a longer time, the cramped room might give me pause.

review_text:
We booked this hotel simply because our flight got in late, and we didn't want to drive to the Pacific Coast until the next morning. I wasn't expecting much, but when we pulled up and saw this beautiful hotel I was pleasantly surprised.
The staff was very professional, and quickly checked us in and helped us get our bags to our room. The room itself was amazing, with a private enclosed patio and a huge luxurious bathroom.
The next morning we had breakfast in the restaurant and it was fantastic. The hotel is really beautiful, with a really nicely designed courtyard in the middle. I didn't want to leave!
I would DEFINITELY stay here again if I were to spend any time in San Jose, and I was sad that we only spent one night here.

review_title: Fine for quick stop in San Jose
review_text:
We needed to be in San Jose the night before and after rafting the Pacuare, and Grano de Oro was on the list of hotels for which we'd have the latest pick-up (6:15 a.m. vs. 5:45 a.m.), so we opted to stay there.
On our first night, we booked a standard room, as that was all that was available. Due to a delayed flight (int'l), we didn't get to the hotel until 10 PM, and were given room 2, which is basically the closest room to reception on the 1st floor (besides room 1), and not where you should stay if you stay at Grano de Oro. It was a plain, very tiny room (my husband joked that he could reach both sides of the room with his arms - not quite, but almost!). Positive aspects of Grano de Oro rm 2 were the windows that opened (although the birds kept me up half the night), and the shower water pressure (with plenty of hot water). Later in our trip we stayed at the Beacon Escazu for about the same price ($139 vs. $130 incl taxes) and had a huge junior suite (check my other review), so I felt the value in this case was very poor. If I were grading my experience on this room, my overall score would have been lower. However, we were only in this room for 8 hours, so it wasn't the end of the world.
Upon our return from our overnight rafting trip at Pacuare Lodge (which was amazing), we had booked a superior room ($153/night w/taxes), which was all that was available at the time of booking. Perhaps because it was our honeymoon, or perhaps because I had made the request for the room based on pictures I'd seen, thinking that it was a superior room, or perhaps because they seem to upgrade a lot of people according to these reviews, we were supposedly upgraded for free to a deluxe room (normally $175 w/taxes). Going back to read reviews, I'm not convinced it was in fact a deluxe room. Booking told me that only deluxe rooms have gardens, yet all these reviewers mention having gardens with superior rooms, and posted photos of superior rooms similar to our room. Anyhow, we had room 7, which was on the second floor. The room was still small, but bigger than Room 2 and adequate in size. The room had a lot more character (loved the wallpaper choice), and a cute garden patio and fountain (we slept with the doors open and it was lovely). The bathroom had a shower/tub (room 2 only had a shower), and was much nicer, with wood floors and design. We really enjoyed this room and I'm basically basing my overall rating on this room experience.
Although the hotel didn't have a gym or pool, we didn't really have time for such things anyhow. What we did have time for was dinner and breakfast at the Grano de Oro restaurant. Dinner was lovely, with formal service and nice atmosphere. We felt the food was good, but not anything amazing, as all these other reviewers seem to think. We loved our salad, but my fish and my husband's steak were just good. Dessert was tiny, and in retrospect, I would have skipped it. The wine was quite good. Anyhow, we enjoyed our meal, and the menu has a great selection, and if you're staying at the hotel, I'd definitely recommend eating here, but don't go out of your way to stay here just so you can dine here. I felt the prices were reasonable considering the type of food and ambiance of the place - I think our bill came to around $85 including 1 appetizer, 2 entrees, 1 dessert, 4 drinks, tax, service charge, and extra tip. A little pricey for Costa Rica I guess, but the restaurant at our next resort (Florblanca) was very overpriced and expensive, so in comparison, it was reasonable. Breakfast was delish - I had the veggie omelet and my husband had the pancakes. Coffee was not very good. Courtyard was very lovely.
Check in/Front desk varied - our first check in was by a very cold man who was not friendly at all. The second check in (upon our return) was with two really sweet women, and much nicer. Also, we stored our bags overnight with the hotel with no problems.
Time from San Jose airport to hotel at Friday night was 15 minutes, closer than I thought (no traffic).
There is a shared computer in the lobby you can use briefly if you need to check the internet (although there is no privacy, and you have to stand).
In summary, if you need to be in San Jose for a pickup or something that prevents you from choosing a more nature oriented hotel outside of the city, this is a fine choice, but avoid the standard rooms, and verify whether or not you're getting a garden patio for your superior or deluxe option.

review_text:
We really liked this hotel and have no doubt that it is the best hotel in San Jose. I think that the discrepency in reviews can best be explained by the rooms that one stays in. We stayed in two different rooms as we stayed one night at the start of our Costa Rica trip and one night at the end. As a result, we had two very different experiences. Our first room..room 16 I believe... was fantastic. I think someone here described what seemed like our room. A gorgeous room on the second floor complete with a indoor terrace with water fountains and a lovely bathroom. We paid a little more for a room just above standard and were actually upgraded into this lovely room.
Our second room was not so nice. It was room no. 1. It was as if we were staying at a completly different hotel. It was VERY old fashioned with a very old fashioned bathroom. Not modern at all like the first room. No air conditioner and only a sfe that required a key. Our first room had air conditioning and a room safe that did not require a key. Don't get me wrong, teh room was clean, but very basic. To be fair...we only paid for a basic room. We also saw some of the other rooms on teh first floor near the spa...again...not as nice as our first room.
The restaurant is supposed to be among the very best. We ate here twice for dinner and although the food was good, it was not great and bit high in price. The serve was excellent. One good surprise is that it appeared as though we received a 10-15% discount on all meals here as our bill was always that much less than the menu prices. Breakfast here was our favorite meal. It was great and very reasonably priced. BTW...Lots of fast food options within blocks of the hotel..Pizza Hut, KFC and Subway were all nearby.
The hotel has two jacuzzis on the rooftop. In addition, the hotel has a single computer in the lobby that guests are free to use at no charge.
There is NOTHING to see in San Jose except a nearby National Park. We went there during the day. Although the park was not very clean, it was great to mix with the people of the city. Many tourist were even doing zip-lines in the park and the park had a lake and horsback riding.
IMHO..if at all possible...skip staying overnight in San Jose and take the ride or plane to your real destination. I felt that staying overnight twice in San Jose was a complete and total waste of money. Of course, this is not the fault of Grano de Oro. If you must stay in San Jose, this is a very elegant hotel.

review_text: We stayed only one night at Grano de Oro as we traveled out of San Jose, but it was really marvelous! The hotel's amazing concept is the indoor/outdoor spaces. You're walking, and all of the sudden you notice fresh air, look up, and there's the moon! The restaurant was phenomenal, and the rooms were extremely cute -- they had a real bed and breakfast sort of feel because of their cozy decorations. There was lot of art, beautiful lush plants, and I wish we would've stayed a little longer at this amazing hotel.

review_title: Great for a short stay, but the food was a perk!
review_text: My new husband and I flew into San Jose from Miami and spent our first night in Costa Rica in this hotel. We had a pre-arranged flight for the next day to the Osa Peninsula and just needed somewhere to stay for the night. As we were traveling through San Jose to the hotel from the airport, we were a little concerned at the surroundings and at first thought our taxi driver was taking us to somewhere we didn't want to go. However, in the middle of nowhere there was this beautiful hotel. The exterior was very inviting and well kept. It was drizzling so someone met us with an umbrella and someone else carried our bags into our room for us. Everyone was very friendly and hospitable and the desk clerk spoke enough english for us to check in. The hotel was very charming and nicely decorated. The rooms were small but clean. It was so quiet, we didn't even know anyone else was staying in the hotel until we went downstairs to the restaurant and lobby. We were able to take an uninterrupted nap at 3 o'clock in the afternoon. We were exhausted so we ate at the hotel restaurant and the food was delicious and service was incredible. We felt safe enough in the hotel to leave our window open while we slept that night. I would definitely recommend this hotel if you need somewhere to stay for a day or two.

review_text:
Spent one night in Grano de Oro upon arrival to Costa Rica and would have loved to have stayed longer.
The staff were great, and upgraded us to a superior room because it was our honeymoon. The rooms are very well presented, not huge but big enough, ours also had a little terrace with a fountain, which we found a lovely unusual characteristic.
There are 2 outdoor jacuzzis on the roof which is a lovely addition to this small hotel which cannot accomodate a pool.
The restaurant is excellent, one of the best in San Jose, but not cheap.
If staying there to visit San Jose city center, be aware that you will need taxis as it is probably a little too far to walk comfortably.

review_title: Charming Hotel in the bustle of San Jose
review_text:
Stayed at the GDO for 2 nights - 30 Mar - room 36 (our friends room 29)
Lovely rooms - no air con but ceiling fan. Bathroom slightly tatty, with scuff marks on door and tarnished sink. Furnishings very good. 2 large beds.
Included: Fridge, TV, safety deposit box (free), towels for the hot tubs on the roof & chocolates left at night !
WIFI connection - medium. Had use of laptop at reception (free to guests)
Reception staff would help with anything and were very pleasant.
Downside: Our room had obviously been rejected by an earlier guest, as upon check-in we found sand all over the chair and unflushed toilet paper in the bowl! I can only assume that they did not like the sound of the fountain outside the room, as it flowed day and night - therefore for anyone requiring a quiet room, don't stay in room 36.
Food: Breakfast was good - particularly the granola (which had in the breakfast box they provided for our very early departure)
Dinner was less good ! The prices far out weighed the taste - although presented beautifully. We would give it a miss if we travel there again. Sad to say this was a particular disappointment as the restaurant had rave reviews!

review_text: We read all these great reviews so we were expecting a great hotel, we got an ok hotel. We were only there for one night and we did not try the restaurant. The plus side, it's clean, has a new feel to it, you feel comfortable, lobby looks good and the staff at check in were helpful. But the room was super small, barely had room to put your luggage. No style at all, looked like grandma's room with grandma's furniture.I think there are two parts to the hotel and we had the crappy room side. They also failed to wake us up as agreed one hour before our bus pick up. That was upsetting. They called us 20 minutes before our bus departure, not a lot of time to get ready. We wanted to get some food to go, since we wouldn't have time for breakfast, but they didn't have anything to go. In the end we ordered two yogurts, they cost $4 each, kind of crazy, but cheaper than the $5 croissant. When they brought them they were both expired over two months ago. We got them replaced but the overall experience dealing with the restaurant breakfast staff was unpleasant, they seeemed they could care less. Also at checkout, I asked for their exchange rate wanting to exchange $$ into colones, they quoted me a rate and when they gave me back the change, I noticed that the calculation was wrong. Turns out that they used another rate, and the rate they quoted me was only for paying the room or some story that didn't make any sense. It felt like being lied to straight to your face and there was no reason for this at all. It's a popular hotel, they might have forgotten how to treat their customers. Next time, we'll try another place.

review_title: One of the best hotels in San Jose
review_text: I have stayed at many different hotels in San Jose (in the center and outside of San Jose) and this is by far one of the best hotels in San Jose. I would definitely recommend it. The staff was excellent and very helpful (they helped us from finding restaurants to gyms), the food was amazing (the restaurant is know to be one of the best in San Jose) and the room was spacious, clean and very quiet. I have to admit that the location is not optimal, but it is only a quick taxi ride to the center, and definitely worth it.

review_text: We stayed here on the last leg of our honeymoon. Simply put it was the best food either of us have ever had and we live in DC and have dined at places like Citranelle. It was worth staying there rather than elsewhere and taking a taxi for breakfast and dinner and at $150 a night it was the best bang for our buck of the whole trip. San Jose is NOT a pretty town and most of the other hotels are right in the middle of all the trash that litters the otherwise beautiful streets. The Grano de Oro is 5 minutes outside the historic center and in a much cleaner district. The room was large and comfortable but the only downside was it was located on a side of the building that faced a busy street. We were woken up by 6 every morning. Most of the other standard rooms had their own little garden patio and if we ever go back to Costa Rica we'll either get one of those or the hotel's master suite. Service was excellent. One day we left our camera in the taxi that the concierge hailed for us. We simply called the hotel and they tracked down the cab that they hailed. 15 minutes later our wedding pictures were back in our possession. If you must stay in San Jose stay in The Hotel Grano de Oro.

review_title: grano de oro - a golden hotel
review_text:
This is one of those old hotels that has been refurbished and updated. They did a splendid job. Lots of old wood throughout the hotel. When we got to our room, it was raining out and the windows were open to see lots of greenery, there was a cool breeze blowing in and it was beautiful. There is no airconditioning that we could see, however.
The restaurant is more than 5 star. The service is highly professional and extremely friendly. The food!!!! It is as good as any food we have eaten anywhere - exquisite!
Even Anthony Bourdain would like it.
The staff was very helpful. We were there less than 24 hours, but they did all they could to help us.
It is close to Paseo Colon, the main street in San Jose. So I suppose shopping is close by.

review_title: There can't be a better spot in San Jose than the Grano de Oro.
review_text: This was probably our 6th stay. We have stayed in both the old and the new part of the hotel. This time we were in the new part with a very nice, spotless room, with a private courtyard patio with fountain and plants. The bed was great and there was AC. The room is quiet and nicely decorated. The restaurant is wonderful with a very professional staff. You can eat in the open courtyard with lovely plants and flowers. It is hard to believe when you are sitting there that right outside is the noisy city of San Jose. A great spot.

review_text:
My wife and I just returned from an 8 night trip to Costa Rica, the last of which was at the Grano de Oro. The hotel is very attractive in an old-world sense. I enjoyed the small porches and spa with live plants. The room was small compared to the other hotels we stayed at in La Fortuna and the Central Pacific. The bathroom was a bit rundown, and definitely would benefit from updating-new tile etc. The shampoo/conditioner/soap dispenser reminded me of a cheap fitness center. The bed was not particularly comfortable. Overall, for the purpose of a good night's rest in a beautiful hotel, this experience did not have great value. It seemed to be more of a place to be seen as opposed to a good place to actually stay.
The restaurant on the other hand was spectacular. The ambience was perfect - a beautiful setting. The food was very good, and while a bit pricey did not seem outlandish compared to a similiar meal in most countries. Even if you do not stay at the hotel, I would definitely consider a meal there. You do need reservations.

review_text: We really enjoyed our stay here - decided to splurge (a bit) and pay the slightly higher price - really feel it was worth it. It is not a 5 star hotel and doesn't pretend to be - but it is a lovely hotel in an old estate - so the character makes up for any shortcomings. It's good to keep in mind that you are basically staying at a very old house, which has been fixed up and made very comfortable. San Jose isn't a beautiful city anywhere - so for us the "grittiness" of the location was never an issue (rather to be expected) - but once inside the Grano de Oro you'd never know you were downtown in a major urban centre. It's centrality was good, however, and part of the reason why we chose to stay there for few nights. If you have to stay in San Jose... this is the place to do it...

review_title: A gem in a rough city

A surprise was the $26 (USD) departure tax at the airport.

review_text:
My wife and I stayed at the Grano De Oro twice in February 2009. We have been visiting Grano De Oro for 4 years now and we have always been impressed by the consistancy of this wonderful little hotel. On the first night in Feb we were in room 23 which is one of the older rooms. It opens to its own little patio and was quite pleasant. We ate breakfast in the restaraunt the next morning and it was great. We have been visiting this hotel since before they built the current restaraunt. The old one was nice, but the new one is incredible. It is rare to see so much pride in quality of service.
On our second night in February we stayed in room 8 which is one of the more modern rooms up above the restaraunts courtyard. This room was so nice it bordered on opulent. It was a mix of classic Costa Rican wood work and nice modern amenities. The bathroom was quite nice with lots of counter space and a big bath tub. The room also had nice windows that gave a great view of the mountains south of San Jose.
If you are considering staying at Grano De Oro I highly reccomend it. You might consider asking for one of the newer rooms or at least ask for an upstairs room. That will be the best way to avoid the rooms that some trip advisor members have complained about.
Another new addition to the hotel is shuttle service to the airport. Thay have a driver that was very accomodating and the trip cost $25 in a van as opposed to a teeny cab.

review_text:
This is a classy little hotel on the edge of downtown San Jose. In any more tourist-oriented metropolis, this place would probaby cost $250/night.
The front desk staff are strong English-speakers, good at giving directions and writing upside down. Our room was modest in size, with attractive furniture and a spotless private bathroom.
We spent a relaxing, romantic evening in the jacuzzi and then the outdoor restaurant. The next day we were able to walk to the city center, the zoo, and back without exhausting ourselves.
The hotel is two blocks from the Calle Central, Paseo Colon, in a commercial area with a few banks, restaurants (real and fast food), and a convenience store within a few blocks. Parking is limited, but there is a security guy in the evening watching the cars who will help you find a spot. Very convenient to Highway 1 if you're planning to drive; 10 minutes from the airport.
If we find ourselves back in San Jose, not sure why that would happen, we would stay here again. Also, I have no idea what Costa Rican TV is like in general, but we were able to watch lots of American programming in English, even the new episode of LOST.

review_title: Pleasantly suprised by the quality of the hotel and the restaurant
review_text: Wow - this was a great find! This hotel was recommended to us by the staff at Hotel Cuna Del Angel, near Dominical. We needed to be near the airport for an afternoon flight back to Canada, but we didn't really want to stay at the airport. This gave us the opportunity to drive into San Jose and stroll around a bit and it was a great value. Although we had a standard room the accomodation was very nice. I love the way they have kept the distinctive details of the old building intact, while making it feel very modern and updated. The fountains and gardens are wonderful; but most of all I loved the restaurant! The decor, the service and the food - was amazing - on par or better, than many other high-end restaurants that I have eaten in in Paris, London, Toronto, New York. Definitely a place to keep in mind.

review_text: This was the 4th and final stop in our Costa Rican honeymoon and San Jose was only a 1-night stay originally intended as a rest day before we headed back for NY via San Jose "Aeroporto". Upon arrival, the bellboy was friendly and courteous and with our very first step into the air conditioned lobby through the huge glass automatic doors- my wife and I immediately wished we'd booked an extra night. It looked and felt luxurious, grand, and charismatic. The quick glimpse of the restaurant to the left of the lobby prompted an immediate reservation for dinner in an hour. We were not let down. We ordered grilled scallops, sea bass, and a chicken pastry plate that left our hunger more than satisfied - but still yearning for more. One Tres Leches and 3 Coladas later, we felt the irresistible urge to rush to our rooms to luxuriate in their impeccably clean tub. Set up a 7AM wake-up call for one of the better breakfasts of our stay in CR and walk up to town by 9am for some impossibly inexpensive souvenir shopping.

review_text:
On our way to San Jose (we did know the way), we met a lady who had stayed at the Grano d’Oro. Her opinion was “it looks nice from the outside, but inside it’s old and shabby”. When we arrived, it certainly looked very nice from the outside, and inside it was definitely old and full of character. However, we would strongly disagree on the word ‘shabby’. Everywhere there seemed to be tasteful elegance. Yes, the furnishings had seen some use, but everything worked properly and nothing looked past its best. True, the rooms don’t have air conditioning, but the heat in San Jose is not oppressive and there are continual cool breezes, so the twin ceiling fans worked fine for us. We found the rooftop spa pools (there are 2) very relaxing after a day travelling or walking the busy streets of San Jose.
The restaurant is quite exceptional. There is a lovely open courtyard in the middle, with comfortable, sofa-style alcove seating in the ‘indoor’ area around the outside. The furnishings are tasteful and opulent, with lots of polished wood and stained glass in evidence, and the menu is extensive and imaginative. The prices reflect this, but not unduly so; I’ve probably paid more for sea bass, less imaginatively prepared in ‘gastropubs’ at home, and we had an excellent bottle of Chilean Sauvignon for around £16. Our only quibble was that the service was a little slow and rather aloof. This was particularly evident at breakfast, when our waiter would disappear for long periods, and staff seemed more focused on setting tables than serving guests. However, the reception staff were very friendly and helpful, and the whole ambiance was one of relaxed, old-style sophistication.
We found little to recommend San Jose as a city; our travel agent (Alan Prendegast at Costa Rica Vacations) had been right to suggest we spent the majority of our time in the rest of the country, with just one night in the capital, However, if you need to visit or pass through, we found that the Grano d’Oro is an excellent place to stay.

review_text:
You absolutely cannot go wrong with a stay at this charming hotel! We only stayed here for one night (as we were leaving for Los Suenos the next morning) but I wish we had been able to stay for many more! We booked at the last minute and therefore were not able to get the room we wanted (#5), but were still not disappointed with the quality and cleanliness of our suite. Our room (#17) opened up to a beautiful and quaint courtyard that was teaming with plants, trees and birds chirping in the morning. During this time of year, we slept with the windows open and never got hot or uncomfortable. We enjoyed a lovely breakfast in the courtyard (don't order room service and miss this great part of the hotel) before we were on our way to Los Suenos. When we return to San Jose, this will be the only place we would even consider staying. It is truly a gem in the middle of an ugly part of the city, but that is quickly forgotten the moment you step through the doors of this hotel!!
The only thing I would do differently would be to book much further in advance to be sure I had choices of rooms - this is a popular hotel and you may miss out if you don't book ahead!

review_title: The best hotel in San Jose
review_text:
My wife and I loved this hotel! We loved everything about it...the rooms, the restaurant, the service, everything. Esteban checked us in and was incredibly helpful throughout our stay. Not only did he surprise us with a free upgrade, but he booked our rental car, made dinner reservations, and gave great advice. We think that Esteban should be the general manager of the hotel because he was so good!
The rooms are all different and while we only saw two of them, we would guess that they are all fantastic. We had two of our best meals in Costa Rica at the hotel restaurant. Breakfast and dinner are highly recommended!
We plan on staying there again.

review_text: We stayed at the Hotel Grano de Oro in a “superior doble” (room 5) the night before our flight back to the U.S., but we wish we'd spent more time here! The hotel’s web site doesn’t do it justice—it’s much grander than it appears online. The lobby is beautiful and modern, but the rooms are very old-world. Ours had beautiful colors, a fabulous bed, and our very own private courtyard with fountain! Just lovely. We had dinner at their restaurant and realized we saved the best for last. DH enjoyed a salmon tartare appetizer (that I wish I’d ordered too!) and lamb chops; I had a wonderful salad with blue cheese, blackberries, and macadamia brittle with scallops and risotto as my entrée. We “shared” (DH is laughing) a Grano de Oro pie for dessert, which was a luscious confection of coffee mousse with a chocolate cookie crust. Perfección! The staff is amazingly attentive and took care of every detail we could thing of: printing our boarding passes, arranging for our rental car to be picked up so we didn't have to waste time returning it the next morning, arranged a private taxi for 5:15 in the morning, and rearranged our dinner reservations so we could get to sleep earlier! We'll stay longer next time to take full advantage of this lovely treasure.

review_text: My husband and I stayed here in November for our honeymoon before and after a 2 night rafting trip. The hotel itself is gorgeous-and does a nice job of bringing the outside in. It is designed with walkways that open up into outdoor areas with fountains and garden-type design, then back inside the building without walking through any doorways. The first night we booked the most economical room and were upgraded to a King bed upon our arrival. The room itself was fine- but we were up all night with what sounded like a creaky weathervane twisting over our heads. It was very loud and kind of offputting for the first night of our honeymoon... however, we didn't report the noise and the hotel probably would have gladly moved us, we just didn't feel like packing everything up again and moving in the middle of the night. BUT- when we came back, we stayed in the Vista de Oro Suite- WOW! I did not want to leave. Initially I was reluctant to book the suite because of the price, but if you have the means, book the Vista de Oro, or at least a garden suite. We had an amazing view of the city and the room's decor is so luxurious. In the morning, we tried to order room service for breakfast, but it didn't work out so well, so we just decided to go down to the restaurant. We ate at the restaurant both nights, and the food was delicious. The hotel gladly stored our bags for our return trip. FYI- if you are up early enough- drink the coffee in the lobby; it was the best I had in Costa Rica. They also have a great gift shop.

review_text:
A lovely hotel-we had a beautiful room, the staff was extremely helpful, the food was excellent. We did find the dinner a bit overpriced. This is not a bargain. It's a bit of a walk into the center and one day in San Jose was enough.
Note that not all the rooms are the same. Our friends had a dark, noisy room with low celings on the bottom floor. They were not happy.
Ours was airy with high ceilings and had a beautiful little enclosed patio area for the same price. Ours had a large lovely bathroom while our friends had a small cramped bathroom.

There is a jacuzzi on the roof and a spa but we used neither. We loved our stay here at the beginning and end of our trip to Costa Rica.

review_title: Top notch hotel in the heart of San Jose
review_text:
My wife and I stayed at Grano de Oro for 4 nights during our honeymoon. The hotel is very charming with its colonial decor and style. But don't be fooled, the hotel is thoroughly modern and the accommodations are exceptional.
We stayed in the Vista de Oro suite which is huge and has an in-room jacuzzi. One night we also stayed in the Garden Suite which was also very nice. Both rooms are highly recommended!
The staff was very friendly and helpful. They helped us make dinner reservations and confirmed all of our activities for us. The restaurant is great as well. The open-air patio is beautiful and provides a pleasant atmosphere for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The full menu has many delicious offerings and is pretty reasonably priced given the high caliber of the hotel.
The location of the hotel is good as well. It is walking distance to the city center, central mercado, and other main attractions. Overall I highly recommend Grano de Oro if you are staying in San Jose proper.

review_text:
We stayed here twice and stayed in two different types of room.
The hotel was a pleasant surprise. Much nicer than we were expecting, with a modern entrance and reception blended very well with the Victorian body of the hotel.
As others have said it's not in a beautiful part of town, but then San Jose is probably not the most beautiful of cities. However taxis are plentiful and cheap, so getting around is not a problem.
The reception staff were extremely good. Friendly, courteous and very helpful. Likewise the porters.
I would recommend that if you can you stay in one of the higher standards of room. We were lucky to get upgraded to a better room for our first night (#5, I think) and it was great - walk-in shower/ wet-room, huge bed, private fountain.
Second time round we were in a standard room (#3 I think). Fine, but much smaller, and with a regular bath/shower. We were a little spoilt first time round.
Finally we'd definitely recommend the restaurant. Superb food. As good as anything in London.
If you don't eat there, I'd also recommend Tin-Jo (Calle 11, Ave 8) - great range of Asian food. It's on the other side of town, but only takes about 15 mins in a taxi (about $4) and well worth it.

review_text: My husband and I stayed in this hotel on our last night in Costa Rica. It was a little difficult to locate since there are no street signs. The people navigate using landmarks...anyway, once we found our way there, we were amazed from the moment we stepped out of the vehicle. We had arrived a few hours early for check in and my husband went to see if we could store our bags safely while we headed downtown to await check in time. Well, not only did they allow us to check in, we were upgraded to a larger room. The staff was friendly and courteous. We stayed in room #10. I was appreciative of the large king bed with a very comfortable mattress. Everything in the room was well appointed. The ambiance of the hotel is very inviting and relaxing. We ate dinner in the restaurant (reservations highly recommended) and the food and service were supurb! I had the beef medallions and my husband had the rabbit. Imagine eating a 5-star dinner with wine, dessert, taxes, and tip for under $90 US. It was amazing to say the least. We usually stay in 4 and 5 star hotels in the US (not because we can afford them, because I just get lucky with internet specials!!!) and this hotel is by far nicer than most we have stayed in. I will always stay at the Grano de Oro while in San Jose, CR. Very good value for the money!

review_text:

Stopped at the Central Market, too.
The attached pictures are of the hotel room, restaurant courtyard and the Central Market. Would definitely recommend this hotel.

review_text:
High ratings, but WHY? We dined here 7 years ago, in a tropical garden setting. Wonderful food, and we were totally impressed. We even got a peek at Harrison Ford dining there, too! They let us look at one of the rooms, showing us gorgeous antique furniture and telling us how each room was totally unique. Little waterfalls in the hallway, hidden gardens.
BUT they have "improved" the place all out of recognition. The dining room is now enclosed and hoity-toity. Which would be fine, if the food lived up to the surroundings. It does NOT. They added a big entrance and hotel lobby which totally destroyed the whole idea of staying at a secluded private estate turned hotel.
Hubby and I (based on our inflated impression from the first trip) made reservations for the night of 10/21/08. Our room was small and dark, nothing particularly impressive about it, with no air-conditioning and one queen size bed. Think Motel 6 decor. Doors slammed loudly in the corridor all night, and we had to leave the windows to the corridor open or smother. That didn't give us a very safe private feeling. We just hoped we wouldn't accidentally flash someone while getting dressed.
No complaints about the staff. Looked like about a 1 to 1 ratio between guests and staff. Very friendly and helpful.
As to the restaurant, the service was good but the food was mediocre. We ordered two different fish dishes, and they were both bland and tasteless, served with what appeared to be instant mash potatoes. The only good dish was the soup of the day. Might not have been so bad except for the high prices. For example, the drinks, about 2 oz each by our estimate, cost around $8 each!
The gift shop on premises had very little to choose from, no cold drinks or snacks. To smoke, you had to got outside with rain dripping down your collar.
We won't go back.

review_title: very nice, worth it even though out of the way
review_text: Nice staff, accomodating, easy to upgrade to a suite -- and worth it! Stayed here in early July - during rainy season, 3 of us, 2 adults, one 5 year old. End of our tour around Costa Rica, so it was a very pleasant surprise, especially after some of the lodging we had stayed at. We had to wait for our room for a few minutes (we did upgrade so it was worth the wait) in the lobby. Complimentary coffee/beverages while we waited. Room was behind the front desk. "Room" is not an accurate description. We had our own entry hall, waiting area, main bed area, sitting area, and garden patio with seating. Very private. I felt like a princess, 4-poster bed, ornate decor through-out. Bath was very comfortable as well. No air conditioning in the hotel, I was nervous because I need AC as my escape, but I didn't find it a problem since it cooled down at night. Also traveling with a young child is always interesting - the staff was VERY accomodating. The restaurant in the hotel was so delicious that we ate there both nights, and our 5-yr-old even loved it - we dressed up in our best clothes (not very dressy considering we were on a hiking trip) and enjoyed being pampered by the restaurant staff. Our daughter is pretty well behaved and experienced in nice restaurants so I think that helped the experience. We did have to take taxis to the sights, but ok by us! No "activities" for kids except hot tub (not good when raining!) and tv (learn Spanish!).

review_text:
A few things to note about the Grano de Oro:
1. There is no A/C, so ask for a room on the first floor. We had room #11 upstairs and it was too hot. Our new room was much cooler.
2. The neighborhood isn't very good, but I didn't find it any worse than anywhere else in San Jose. San Jose is not a very prepossessing place. Because it is a relatively new city, it doesn't have colonial buildings like some other Latin American cities. There is lots and lots of barbed wire. The Grano de Oro, as others have noted, is a nice 'oasis' in the middle of the mayhem.
3. There seems to be somebody outside at all times to ensure that everybody who gets in to the building belongs there.
4. Service at the hotel is exceptional. The staff was courteous and accommodating, but somehow managed to seem genuinely concerned and not affected.
5. The restaurant has got to be the best in San Jose. It's very good and reasonably priced for North American standards at least: (bottle of wine, 2 appetizers, 2 mains (including chateaubriand) for about US$70 including tax and tip). Note that taxes and tips are included in all prices.
It's not a five-star hotel by North American standards, but that's not really the point. I doubt that you'll find a better hotel in San Jose, and if you are jumping off from San Jose to other places in Costa Rica you'd do extremely well to stay at the Grano de Oro. If you really want a more North American experience there are quite a few hotel/casinos near the airport, including the Radisson and the Holiday Inn.

review_title: A Little Oasis in the middle of San Jose
review_text: I have nothing but great things to say about this hotel. I was a little skeptical about staying in San Jose and a finding a good hotel, but because of our arrival flight we had no choice. This hotel is a true oasis in the middle of the city and far surpassed my expectations. The rooms were spotless and very comfortable. As you navigate through the hallways you find yourself in open air courtyards with running water fountains and tons of plants. The jacuzzi’s on the roof deck are lovely! I definitely recommend having dinner at the hotel which was spectacular! Great food and great wine list- if the weather is nice you can have dinner in their open air courtyard. This hotel certainly won’t disappoint and it was nice beginning to our honeymoon.

review_text:
We arrived in San Jose at 10pm and went directly to a "hotel" ringed in barbed wire that our cab driver warned us against. One look and we left for his recommended hotel a few blocks away - it was equally shady.
So after a quick Rough Guide check and phone call, I told him to take us to the Grano de Oro. The difference in price was $105 vs. $80 night. The difference in accomodation was enormous. The outside is spectacular, the restaurant is one of the most beautiful and romantic I have ever been to and the staff is friendly and helpful. The charming rooms are not airconditioned but the evenings were always a perfect temperature making a/c unnecessary (and I sweat ALOT in Costa Rica). We stayed here on three different occasions and used this as our base camp as we went to different parts of the country over 12 days.
Note: The outdoor hot tub deck is cute but not a reason stay here. If you are not going the hostel route, I would doubt there is a better hotel in or around San Jose (unless you prefer a more antiseptic travel experience - i.e. The Marriott). Even if you don't stay here, the restaurant is worth the taxi ride over.

review_title: This Golden Grain Needs Some Polishing!!!
review_text:
This Golden Grain needs some polishing!!! Our stay was a complete and utter disappointment and an anticlimactic end to our visit to this beautiful country and stays at other really exceptional locations. After reading myriad reviews on trip advisor we were ready to swept a way by GDO’s charm and the welcoming and accommodating staff but unfortunately that just wasn’t the case. Our room was small by any standard and it was very humid and stuffy even with the ceiling fan at full tilt. We thought that we would just try and “make do” as it was only for one night but the room was so uncomfortable I started to feel sick. So, I went to talk to the staff at the front staff about it and inquired if we could borrow another fan and/or switch to a room with at least more of a cross breeze to which I was simply told it wouldn’t be possible, we even offered to pay the difference for any kind of upgrade there appeared to be a number of bigger, breezier, vacant room. The response to my complaint was, “you are the first person to mention any problem” to which I responded, “does that somehow invalidate my complaint?!” After that I was simply ignored and dismissed, it was if I had somehow turned invisible, neat trick—huh?!
I guess you could describe the hotel as charming but I wouldn’t exactly characterize it as unique. Many of the rugs in the hall looked as if they needed replacing, the ever-mentioned sun deck and hot tub area looked like it needed a good scrub, I could go on but… you get the idea. Perhaps some of the charm others reviews described was tarnished for us by the inhospitable disdain we experienced during our stay, I know I won’t ever be returning or recommending this location to friends!!!

review_text:
When I stayed at Grano de Oro I really felt like I was staying in the best hotel in San Jose. It is beautiful inside and out and has a wonderful feeling from the moment you walk in.
The location is very central and within walking distance to everything if you're daring enough to walk the streets of San Jose. We walked to the National Theater and the market where the locals shop. The hotel is also within walking distance to fast food like Quiznos, KFC, and Subway. There is also a little convenience store down the street to buy snacks.
We dined at the restaurant one night as a special meal. It was our one fancy dinner, and it was amazing. The food was spectacular and the service matched. The restaurant was better than any of the fancy restaurants I've dined at in La Jolla, Ca.
I would definitely recommend Grano de Oro to anyone staying in San Jose. It is really a beautiful hotel!

review_title: Grano de Oro gem in otherwise dull San Jose
review_text: We stayed our last two nights in Costa Rica in San Jose after a 10-day honeymoon trip and loved the Grano de Oro. Our room was nice with a little patio and fountain, the house was beautiful and the restaurant/courtyard was amazing. We had dinner our first night there which was delicious and in a great setting. We walked around San Jose that first day and weren't too impressed, so we decided to take a day-trip to Arenal volcano, which the hotel set up and was a nice way to spend our last day in Costa Rica. Overall, I would highly recommend Grano de Oro if you have to stay in San Jose, but it was nothing compared to Mal Pais where we were for the bulk of our trip!

review_text:
Our third trip to Costa Rica within 8 years. We always try some place new each time. This hotel is beautiful and so out of place to where it was located. The first night we met friends and ate somewhere out of the outskirts of town, not sure where, Los Cebollines..a Mexican restaurant. It was expensive and ok food.
The second day we rafted Pacuare and it was as always excellent, with Rios Tropicales. After a long day, we opted to try the restaurant at the hotel. The place is beautiful. The rooms are ok, nothing great, but clean. The bathroom can be renovated a little bit more. We had drainage problems in the shower as well as some of the water spraying out of the shower head rather than on us. The walls are thin and the doors slam a lot. You can't help the sound of the doors, they stick a bit. There are signs to tell people to be silent, as everyone has their windows open..and it's hard to sleep when kids are running around, but that is to be expected, I supposed when the rooms are in a courtyard setting. The food was very good. Dinner was expensive but not for what you were given. I can see why so many people rave about the place. The ambience really was lovely. As for dinner service, well we had to ask for things three or four times before we received what we wanted but it was always done with a smile and a "I'm sorry". We wouldn't mind staying there again except we didn't care for the location. It suited our needs and everyone was very kind and friendly.
Overall, this is a lovely hotel and for the price, you really can't go wrong.

review_title: Grano de Oro is a diamond in the rough
review_text:
First time visitors to Costa Roca, my wife and I just returned from an incredible seven nite adventure, where the first two nites and dinners were at the wonderful Grano de Oro Hotel.
The building, inside and out, is well maintained and decorated with plants and flowers. The interior open courtyard is surrounded by the bar and restaurant where tables are open to the sky if not raining or give the dining room tables a Spanish-style courtyard view during the frequent rain showers.
Our room was modest in size with a nice open walk-in shower with interior windows facing a space with a fountain and more plants. Only complaint is that the walls are thin and, though the place is mostly quiet, we could hear voices of guests walking to their room. We did take advantage of the rooftop jacuzzis where, like in the rest of the hotel, great care has been given to block out views of not very pretty San Jose and the somewhat commercial neighborood.
Food and service in the restaurant were outstanding, though not inexpensive. They had live musicians one nite playing violin & guitar mood music while we lingered over dinner, drinks and dessert served by a very attentive staff.
Front desk staff could not have been more helpful and the computer with internet access also at the front desk helped us keep in touch.
Our only negative is San Jose itself. The area around the hotel is not spectacular and the city is dirty.
Overall a great experience for us and we have visited many cities and hotels around the world. We felt we were in Costa Rica while staying at the Grando De Oro, not just staying at another chain hotel in a foreign country.

review_text: In June, my wife and I went to Costa Rica for the first time. The over-all experience of the country was positive. Read about the Grand de Oro Hotel, so we stayed there after we flew in and before we left the country. Don't get me wrong, it is not a bad place. However, the hotel is basically a three-stars bed & breakfast but charging a five-stars hotel price. To be polite, I call it over-priced. In street term, it was a big time rip-off. Don't go there unless you want to waste your money.
