review_text:
I stayed one night with my family (my husband and my daughter) in this hotel after reading all the wonderful reviews on tripadvisor.com. What a big disappointment! We purchased a ticket at the airport booth for a cab to get to the hotel. It was a 20 mins. ride and costed 20 US dollars.
Pros and Cons:
Pros:
1. Newly renovated hotel lobby.
2. Check-in staff friendly.
3. Walking distance to the "Mercado Central" market. 20 mins. By cab $3 distance.
Cons:
1. Very small and old rooms. Our room had 2 double beds, a TV, no A/C but 2 ceiling fans, no bathroom amenities and no hairdryer. It costed $145 plus tax.
2. There was renovation going on somewhere during the day, expect banging loud noises.
3. Hotel dinner was OK but over priced. We order 2 appetizers, 3 main courses, 2 desserts and no alcohol. The bill was $150 dollars. And my husband's chocolate cake was still frozen in the center, it's obviously that it came from a box but not freshly bake. Super slow service! Staff was too busy talking among each others than providing services. If you have a choice please
DO NOT eat in this hotel. Big ripped off. We went to the Central market and the local food there was a lot better and it costed less than $10/pp.
4. If you have time shop some where else for souvenirs. The same T-shirt costed $10 dollars more in the hotel shop. The shops in central market has a lot of choices.
I would definitely stayed somewhere next time. I don't mind paying this kind of $$ if it's worth the stay. This is just a marginal 3 star motel charging 4-5 star hotel prices. After one night we then moved on to the Marriott in Los Suenos. Wonderful resort by the beach! No complaints at all.

review_title: Great Accomodations At Grano de Oro
review_text:
My two friends and I stayed at the Hotel Grano de Oro during our first and last nights stay in San Jose. The hotel was a part of our tour package with 'Tierra Verde.' (I would highly recommed that tour group - we were given a guide for each day and it made the trip all the more special). The hotels staff was very helpful. On the first day we arrived at approx. 11:15am and we were given a room within 30 minutes of our arrival. This was greatly appreciated as we were extreamly tired from our 12 hour journey. The room we were given was slighly older than the other rooms, but nonetheless clean and very comfortable. My only complaint was slamming noises I heard throughout the evening. I thought this was the closing of a supply closet door, but later learned that it was the closing of hotel doors. If you stay in one of the hotels' newer rooms (as we did on our last night), you will notice that the hotel doors do not easily close, hence, the slamming noise. It's an unforchante situation of an otherwise wonderful hotel.
We recieved breakfast on both our first and last day. It was very good, if a bit small.
My only other suggestion is that they move the computer with internet access to an area where one can sit to use it. It is currently attached to the reception desk. But, the internet access was still greatly appreciated. (We were charged $2 for 15 minutes at another hotel!)
All, in all, a great, clean, hotel with close proximity to the San Jose airport. 4 stars!!!

review_text: we loved it the minute we walked in the lobby. Fresh exotic flowers all over the hotel. Restaurant is superb. Rooms are nice. We stayed for two nights in room 14. The fan was noisy but otherwise the room was fine. It was a small room and no air conditioning but that is not uncommon in Costa Rica. front desk staff is very friendly and helpful. They helped us practice our Spanish. It rained heavily the one full day we were there so we actually sat in the lobby most of the day and read, people watched and surfed the internet on the laptop they make available for guests. It was a guilt free day to rest up before our three week adventure. San Jose itself is not worth more than 1or 2 nights, but this hotel makes it a treat at the beginning and end of a vacation. We picked the hotel because it is the #1 hotel on TripAdvisor. The reviewers are right on! Call the hotel directly if other websites indicate it is full. That is the only way I got a room and it was the smallest room in the hotel, but we really didn't need any more space so I was happy to save on the expense and put it towards a great meal in the hotel restaurant.

review_text: We stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro for two nights in May. We had arranged with the hotel for a car to pick us up at the airport- however, no car was at the airport when we arrived. We ended up taking a taxi to the hotel. When we checked in, we told the clerk that no car was at the airport. He looked up our reservation and he indicated that a car was to pick us up- he did not find out why the car did not show up. We made reservations for dinner and they confirmed our reservations for dinner at check-in- when we arrived for dinner, they did not have our table. We were asked to wait and told that the manager would explain why we did not have a table- we waited but no one came to explain what had happened to our table. Finally, we were given a table by the silverware station. The food was not nearly as good as it was two years ago. When we checked out, our bill was incorrect and it took about 30 minutes to correct the bill. Overall, a disappointing experience.

review_text: Had been here a few years back just for dinner but had the opportunity to stay for 3 nights, May 8th-11th. The hotel had expanded since I had been there, it is still as beautiful, even more so, than it was. The staff was outstanding, our room, #5, was beautiful, we even had a good sized outdoor courtyard with lots of plants and a fountain, glass roof and glass French doors. If you don't have the opportunity to stay here at least dine in the restaurant. We even had room service from the restaurant delivered one night. The rooms were very affordable, $140.00 per night for a deluxe room. Saw the other area hotels and ours was the best. Restaurant can be pricey, each night was approx. $100.00 for two but well worth it. I would most definitely return and recommend this hotel. You can walk to everything, the Jade museum, Gold Museum, National Theatre and shopping. The only place to stay in San Jose.

I can't honestly think of anything bad about this hotel - I absolutely loved it. If anything, the fact it was in San Jose (the city wasn't for me!!)
The staff were fantastic and the hotel itself was beautiful. We booked a table in the restaurant and the food and drinks were brilliant and good value for money too. And that's the surprising thing, if this hotel was in New York or London it would be a fortune to stay there. It had a great little gift shop too.
My tip for this place would be to book a massage. I'm a connoiseur in massages and I think this one tops my list of favourites!
I say go and enjoy ;-)

review_text: My husband and I only stayed at the hotel for one night as we were traveling through San Jose so I can't really speak to what San Jose is like but the hotel is beautiful. We stayed in a room that had a little patio with a waterfall which was very beautiful although we didn't get to enjoy it that much. Overall, we really liked the hotel and would definitely recommend it.

review_title: Nice oasis in a mediocre city
review_text: The Grano De Oro hotel certainly exceeded my expectations. For a very reasonable price I stayed in the Garden Suite during the in-coming aspect of my trip (I was going surfing at Mal Pais) and then a Deluxe Room on the last day in Costa Rica. The hotel was such a nice escape from a non-glamorous city. The Deluxe Room was my favorite--Room 6 on the second floor with a beautiful sitting area that had a fountain. The photographs on their website (as of 5/2008) do NOT do this property justice. It is such a cute, friendly hotel with a fabulous restaurant and outstanding staff. They even found us a yoga class!! The rooms in the newer section of the property have a nice style to them and overlook a little garden patio and the restaurant. The entrance was refreshing and welcoming with flowing water next to the entry staircase. If you need to stay in San Jose--this is the place to go!

review_text:
My wife and I are seasoned travelers, and the Grano de Oro, in San Jose, is one of the nicest hotels I've stayed in, with a great amount of charm and character. The hotel has a very cozy feel to it with exceptional service making it a nice blend of a 4-5 star hotel and bed and breakfast. The restaurant is fantastic. My wife and I had lunch there and returned for dinner after an afternoon of sightseeing in San Jose because we enjoyed the food and drinks so much. Its pricey but not outrageous and the food and drink are top notch. Best of all is the hotel's staff. The hotel employees, from desk clerks to waiters, all speak excellent English and are very friendly and welcoming. We stayed here on our first night in Costa Rica and I believe it to be one of the best choices we made all trip. It is an excellent place to relax a bit, get your bearings after hours on a plane and adventure a bit downtown. I can't imagine staying anywhere else in San Jose.
A few tips to any travelers considering a trip to San Jose and Costa Rica: We went to Costa Rica on a whim, based on an inexpensive price for a package of two round-trip flights. What a wonderful idea! Costa Rica had a bit of everything: culture, adventure, romance, food. We booked through the website latindestinations.com, who subcontracts Swiss Travel in Costa Rica, and I completely recommend them both. We were greeted at the airport, the reservations were correct, and transportation was always on time. Customer service was available 24/7 if we needed it.
While in San Jose, do not be wary to sightsee downtown. Just use red taxis, stay in well-traveled areas, keep your wallet and purse close, and you'll be fine. Be sure and visit their gold museum (great displays of pre-Columbian native art), sightsee around the theatre and churches near the museum, and stop by some of the markets and vendors for a snack. The Costa Ricans (Ticos) are friendly people, even if you do not speak Spanish.
I'd be glad to give answer questions or give advice. Just drop me a note.

review_text:
First of all, the photos of Grano de Oro from Expedia are outdated. While the rooms look fairly similar to the way they look in the photos, the rest of the hotel has experienced a "makeover." The front lobby is impeccable and gradiose - modern and extremely well-
decorated. Free coffee is offered late at night/early in the morning. Free internet is provided via a laptop on the counter of the front desk. There is an amazing pair of jacuzzi spas on the roof with a fantastic view of the city lights in between romantic Grecian pillars. My boyfriend and I were the only guests using the jacuzzi at the time so it was incredibly romantic...I don't think the hotel advertises it so make sure to ask about it when you check-in.
The rooms themselves vary in size, but the quality is amazing regardless of size. We had the standard double room, which is probably one of the smaller rooms offered. While not big, the room was comfortable for two people and was impeccable as far as cleanliness and decor. The bathroom and shower (steamy hot) were great. One nice thing is that the room had a big rug so it felt as though the room was carpeted...something that lacked at all of the other hotels we stayed at in Costa Rica. There was no A/C, but this was not a problem when we were there because (1) it was not that hot and (2) there was a nice window offering ventilation.
As far as location, Grano de Oro is not far from downtown (about a 20 minute walk down the main Avenida Colon/Central), but far enough to be away from the noise. The street is quiet and residential, but still close to a busy street with restaurants. Unfortunately, many of the food joints on Avenida Colon close at before 10 pm, which made it difficult to find food after getting home late from day trips. The hotel's own restaurant has a very nice ambiance and offers some decent choices (although the food is not amazing). There are also a couple of restaurants within walking distance, but not super close and not super good. However, downtown is not very far and cabs are cheap.

review_title: The Best Hotel in San Jose
review_text: In the USA this would be a 5-Star hotel and if TripAdvisor had a 6-Star rating this hotel would get it!!!! The hotel staff was very helpful when checking in and spoke excellent English. A map was provided of local restaurants and walking paths. The hugh park, approx a mile by a mile with a lake, was within walking distance. The neighborhood surrounding the hotel toward the park was upscale with business-attire people. The restaurant??? We didn't dine there at night- wanting a local flare, what a mistake. We ate there for breakfast. Appprox $8.00, that included tax and tip. Take away $2.00 for what that would have been and this leaves a $6.00 breakfast. Juice AND coffee was included at no charge, thus this makes a $4.00 breakfast, in the most beautiful setting we have seen in our whole trip. The room was beautifully appointed and we had the standard room. We took a dip at night in one of their two hot tubs, very romantic. Book this hotel if you can and you won't be disappointed.

review_text:
We arrived late (after midnight) and were greeted in the lobby. The lobby is beautifully redone with seating areas, lots of windows. We were escorted to our room. The pictures on the website don't do it justice. Although smaller, the room was lovely. The furniture was dark wood and the bed linens were light blue. The floors are also wood and were covered with a large woolen rug. Everything looked very pulled together. The bathroom was much larger than I anticipated. The shower was large and my husband really liked the soap/shampoo dispenser. I thought that the antique windows and tile were the best features.
We requested and received an early wake-up call. Check out was quick and easy. We wanted to try the breakfast but didn't have time. I would love to return to this property when I have more time to enjoy it!

review_title: They Should Up the Star Rating!
review_text: I have stayed here several times and ulike other places I have stayed it have gotten better. I miss the old bed and breakfast style but the new appointments are more then a pleasure. The hotel now boast a really nice outdoor and indoor dining are but is a bit on the pricey side. If you like a tart drink order the limonade. It is a great place to stay in the city but not in the muk proper. It is a great starting point to get you going and unlike others say about not spending all your time in the hotel it could be well worth it here, when you need to rest up. I would suggest booking this towards the end of you adventure as a treat or a place to recoup, but do note that you really don't want to be in the the city. Check out the other hotels affiliated. They are just as good and somewhat better. They have internet in the lobby and two hot tubs on the roof. Convienent location for arranging tours and surpasses almost everything in the vacinity for value and accomodation. They will even hold your luggage if you have breaks in your stay.

review_text: We stayed at the Hotel Grano de Oro on April 4th. It was our last night in Costa Rica after a week of vacationing, and it was a wonderful stay. The restaurant was fantastic, and the hotel was beautifully decorated, and we loved our garden patio. We were fond of the sign in the main hallway asking guests to be silent in the nighttime so as not to wake up sleeping guests...if only hotels in the US were as considerate. While we likely wouldn't return to San Jose, if we ever do, it will include a stop here.

review_title: Great gem in an otherwise uninspired San Jose
review_text:
Grano de Oro is an excellent hotel. The rooms are very elegantly appointed and while there is no A/C, the breeze and the ceiling fan kept the room pleasantly cool. The statff is great; when American lost our luggage a staff member called the counter throughout the night to get status updates. The gift shop also is an nicely edited collection of Costa Rican souvenirs and very reasonably priced.
Last, the restaurant. If you stay at this hotel, please do not go anywhere else for dinner! The restaurant is richly decorated and the food is equally delicious. The food itself is electic; as an indication, we had foie gras, tuna tataki, steak in a gorganzola sauce and rabbit in a mushroom sauce. Breakfast is excellent as well, as was the service at both meals. I highly recommend staying here!

review_text:
We stayed here on the last night of a 2 week trip. They've managed to accomplish that often-failed project of converting an old building into a hotel - keeping the charm of the building and making it work as a hotel.
We usually don't eat at the hotel restaurant, but the reviews of restaurants in San Jose indicated that we shouldn't pass up the chance - and it was the best meal of the trip.

review_text: This hotel has a beautiful lobby and front area. Rooms are quaint, newly painted. No AC, delux room had windows that open to a courtyard. Overall not bad. We walked to the city center, bars on windows but we were told it was safe. No problems, but didn't feel like the neighborhood you'd stay out and have a beer. No pool & roof top deck, jacuzzi all closed for remodeling, which I'd been told this upon booking, might of chose differently. Staff tried to be helpful, but told us the Central Mercardo was worth checking out. I asked if it were open on Sunday and was told yes, only to find out while walking there it is not. Overall staff tried to be helpful, but don't take advice on when to leave for airport, not sure they've travel abroad and they'll tell you an hour is fine when actually you're 20 min from airport, need to purchase departure tax, check in, security. Don't cut it close, leave 2 hours before flight if early AM flight.

review_text:
First let me say that I have worked in the hotel business for nearly 25 years. My wife and I spent 10 days in Costa Rica and decided to stay at the Grano de Oro our first night in the country and our last night prior to leaving. The property is about 15-20 minutes south of the airport direclty in San Jose, but is easy to find.
The minute you see it you know you're in for a treat. The exterior is beautiful and the limited landscapping they have is done very tastefully. The hotels staff is friendly and efficient and you feel that they truly enjoy their profession. The property offers a wide range of guest room types. We had the privealiage of sampling two different types during our visits and we peaked into several others. They are all special and it is easy to see that the owners and property and management pay attention to every detail- I do mean every detail.
Our favorite was the suite overlooking the city. It's worth every cent. The unique decor, the beautiful furnishings, the seperate elevated whirlpool bath area surrounded by windows with great night views of the city and mountains in the distance, all lead you to believe you are truly special. Something all true hoteliers hope to accomplish for their guests but all to often fail at delievering.
Becasue I know those of you who use this site are interested in more than one opinion I'll cut my comments short about the other rooms but I want you to know that there isn't a room my wife and I saw that we wouldn't have liked. They're all special and you'll fee that way too.
One final comment about the restaurant-it's magnificent! My wife and I were celebrating our 20th anniversary and we chose to have our last dinner in Costa Rica in the htoels restaurant. That wasn't our intital plan when making reservations prior to arriving in the country but after our first experience with their restaurant all my wife talked about was returning for our last night. It helped us have something to look forward to as our trip ended and the experience the second time was as memorable as the first. Do yourself a favor and dine at the Hotel Grano de Oro. I can't imagine anything better.
Thanks to the staff for making our 20th anniversay so perfect.

review_text:
Everything at this hotel was perfect. I stayed here for one night at the end of my holiday in Costa Rica and it ended my holiday on a high.
From the moment I arrived, in the pouring rain, and was met by the porter with an umbrella as I stepped from the car I knew I was in for a treat. The historic building in which the hotel is located has been beautifully and sympathetically decorated, and the hotel has volunatrily introduced a total smoking ban to protect the building.
I stayed in a standard room which is the basic room but was still beautifully appointed with a luxurious bed, and had plenty of space.
The restaurant is possibly the best in San Jose, and is very reasonably price for the superb service, and excellent food which they serve.
It's simple - if you are staying in San Jose, stay here.

review_text:
We have travelled extensively both for business and pleasure, and the restaurant at the Grano De Oro compares very well with top choices in London, NYC, Hong Kong or Tokyo. The service is outstanding, while the Costa Rican fusion choices are both interesting and well matched with a good wine list. Recommend the cheese plate that includes local cheeses and fruits. The courtyard dining al fresco is candlelit with a fountain, surrounded by balcony tables, very romantic. Ladies are offered pashmina wraps to ward off any hint of a chill. Prices are very reasonable and outstanding value.
The hotel is within walking distance of the downtown pedestrian mall and museums, tucked on a quieter side street. It is a secure and pleasant location. The rooms are not outstanding but very clean with plenty of bottled water and an in-room safe and minibar. The staff is extremely pleasant and helpful, with excellent English at the front desk. Good value and the restaurant is not to be missed.

review_text: We stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro the last night of our Costa Rican trip. We were exhausted from the drive from Manuel Antonio to San Jose--if you've done it, you will understand--and the staff was so welcoming and helpful. Our room was too small, but for one night it was fine. We had some hot beers, and the desk allowed us to drink the beers in the room fridge and put our warm ones in--no charge. The restaurant was just beautiful and a super menu. We were too tired to really eat, but ordered some appetizers. We were treated as if we ordered the top items on the menu. Breakfast was outstanding, too. Hotel is not in a good part of town, but that didn't matter. Cabs are not expensive and can take you anywhere. I would stay there again, for sure. Also, they have a computer at the desk which one can access for no charge.

review_title: Lives up to and surpasses its reputation...
review_text:
Grano de Oro is a well oiled machine with courteous staff ready to go that extra mile. The ambiance and eclectic decor in Moorish/Victorian Tropical style is what really makes it special. We were there in the Christmas holidays and the hotel was beautifully decorated.
Try the Tico breakfast, it's good value, tasty and quite filling so you'll only need a light lunch. Food in the hotel is excellent and very popular so reserve dinner in advance. It's quite amusing watching the Josefinas dressed to the nines and the tourists moseying in wearing shorts and flip-flops. Take one smart outfit with you so you don't feel too out of place.

review_title: Great property, location and value for money!
review_text:
This hotel is a member of the small distinctive hotels of Costa Rica (I would highly recommend checking their properties in the areas you plan to visit and if you don’t know which areas, check there properties to se if you can build an itinerary around it as we visited three out of six and they are in great locations. They have two more locations currently under development). Anyway, back to this property, it was excellent value for money we paid around $125/night. It is in a quite neighborhood of San Jose but very close to the centro (20 minute walk, 5 minute cab ride (less than US$3). We debated staying at the Mariott San Jose v/s here and chose this for location as the Mariott is close to the airport. Also, none of the room are air conditioned but the weather is very pleasant and all rooms have fans.
The dinner at the French restaurant was decent but the service was poor – amuche came after appetizer and breads came after both).
General tips: We were in Costa Rica for a week and rented a car. If you rent a car, do get GPS as signs are rare and far in-between. The GPS was a life saver. Roads were not terrible as I expected although I would not compare it to any thing in the US or Europe. People seemed friendly and we did not feel scared or threatened at any time and we drove to every where (local restaurant in La Fortuna and in San Jose). I would not recommend driving in San Jose down town area unless you have already driven in other developing countries with aggressive driving. If you are renting with Europcar, be aware that they do not have a counter at the airport (most other car rental companies do) and you have to call they to be picked up or take a cab. It was very frustrating as we called and were told 10 minutes. We called every 10 minutes and were told the same thing with no shuttle 90 minutes later when we took a cab. The office was very disorganized. The car was nice and return was easy. Most car agencies have similar cars so go with any reputed rental agency.

review_text:
My husband and I stayed at the Grano de Oro for one night when we arrived into San Jose, and begin our trip to Costa Rica. The hotel was beautiful and the staff was very kind. It was quite late when we arrived from our day of traveling. We were hoping to get something to eat, but room service and the restaurant were both closed. We were unfamiliar with San Jose and did not want to venture out at midnight, so we settled for a snack from the minibar. Our room was stunning and incredibly romantic. The bathroom was very modern, yet blended perfectly with the colonial feel of the rest of the hotel. There was a small private “sunroom” in our room which had a working fountain and was full of tropical plants and flowers. The next morning we had breakfast in the restaurant. The food was very good, particularly the fresh orange juice and the coffee.
We stayed there again for a single night on the night before we left Costa Rica. The second room was not quite as romantic or luxurious as the first. It was, however, very cute and unique. It was upstairs, and had a window overlooking a very pretty common area with a fountain and tropical plants. We also ate at the restaurant for dinner, and it was by far the best food we had on our entire trip. It was also reasonably priced. The mushroom crostini appetizer was fantastic, and the tenderloin and the sea bass were both perfectly prepared. I highly recommend the Grano de Oro.

review_text:
We just returned from our first trip to Costa Rica...with a 1 night stay in San Jose at the beginning and at the end. I've had several friends tell me that San Jose is just filthy. So, I had my concerns about spending part of our vacation there. But, I also wanted to get the "feel" of Costa Rica by not staying in some corporation-owned hotel like a Marriot or Sheraton. Just like any large city, San Jose has it's pretty/wealthier parts and it's older/impoverished parts. Hotel Grano de Oro is located right where those 2 parts of the city meet.
The hotel is beautiful and the lobby is newly remodeled. The front desk staff and employees throughout the hotel were very friendly and helpful. Each room in the hotel is decorated differently. We stayed in the Vista de Oro Suite...gorgeous! The hotel is so beautiful and comfortable--you won't want to leave. The hotel's website has pictures of many of it's suites. Grano de Oro's restaurant has excellent meals (and very affordable prices compared to the hotels we stayed at in Quepos). I will definitely stay at Grano de Oro on future trips to Costa Rica.

review_text:
We loved the hotel. The service (both in the restaurant & the hotel) were excellent. They helped us find a new way to get to Limon (through the old highway) and assisted with other minor problems efficiently. The hotel itself is going through a renovation right now (mainly in the back) but they only work during the day (and not in the mornings). The room we had was sufficiently large and looked out into their courtyard. They have a jacuzzi (two of them in fact) on the roof, which during a good day can be quite enjoyable.
The restaurant is very nice and we found the service to be quite prompt. Their drinks are quite good (including their Mojito's) along with their food. I would highly recommend eating at this establishment, just be weary of their prices, as they are quite expensive compared to the rest of San Jose.

review_title: Our favourite hotel in Costa Rica!
review_text:
We stayed in the Grano De Oro on the first two nights of our honeymoon, and then another later on before going to Manuel Antonio. We were extrememly impressed with this hotel, and it set a very high standard for the rest of the places we were staying.
The room was perfect. comfortable, clean (even under the bed!), cool and airy. The staff were fantastic! They were so friendly and very helpful.
The building is beautiful, the court yard is a lovely setting for breakfast and dinner.
The restaurant was superb too. It was more expensive the anywhere we ate in Costa Rica, but it was well worth it, and still very cheap compared to UK prices!
The hotel is also an easy walk into central San Jose for a spot of shopping!
We are a couple in mid to late twenties, but reckon that this hotel would appeal to all. Pura Vida!

review_text: We were told that this was the place to say in San Jose. Hardly. There was an ant investation in our room so they moved us because I am highly sensitive to extermination chemicals. They moved us a few hours later...to a room that was JUST BOMBED. There were hundreds of dead ants all over the floor. The rooms are small and the restaurant is overpriced and does not offer food for people who do not like fancy foods (duck, rabbit, etc). If you do not have to stay in San Jose I would recommend staying outside of it. If you are forced to stay in the city (which has nothing to due) than go somewhere else.

review_title: Beauty and serenity in a crazy city
review_text: We stayed at Grano de Oro in July-07 because we wanted to experience San Jose but didn't want to sacrifice on clealiness or comfort. Grano de Oro was much more than we could have hoped for. The hotel is beautiful, with fresh flower arrangements all over the place. The staff was excellent, giving us tips on where to go and things to do, helping us confirm reservations in other destinations, and giving superb service with a smile. The restaurant, while pricey, is excellent and worth a visit, at least for a drink or dessert. We ate breakfast there every day and the tipico breakfast (typical Costa Rican food) was the best!! There are 2 hot tubs on the roof which are perfect for evening relaxation, but I recall that glass is not permitted on the roof, so we didn't drink wine. We enjoyed the hotel's location, just 2 block off the "main drag" and about a 10-15 min walk to the city center. It was perfect for a day-time stroll through down and a return to a quiet, peaceful and luxurious evening. The beds were comfortable, bathrooms plenty large, and property very well maintained and clean. We HIGHLY recommend this hotel! You won't regret it.

review_text: We stayed at the Grano de Oro to see a little of San Jose before our trip to the Pacuare. The restaurant was very nice--food was better than other restaurants we encountered in the rest of our trip, but we stayed in one of the cheaper rooms, which weren't especially nice. They were interior rooms with a lack of windows. The jacuzzi was a portable spa in their rooftop garden. But then you don't go to San Jose for a jacuzzi. We probably would have had a better experience if we booked a more expensive room. Their gift shop was one of the better ones we saw in Costa Rica.

review_text:
We stayed two separate nites with our 2 daughters (1 and 3) and had a wonderful and delightful stay. Everyone was extremely helpful, pleasant, and went out of their way, especially with a toddler in tow.
TACA airlines had lost one CAR SEAT, but we had 3 days before renting our car. The front desk helped make all the calls to find the luggage, confirm where they were going to bring it, confirmed our car reservations, they made sure we were all settled!
The restaurant has a fabulous menu, and beautiful courtyard. We treated ourselves to the famous chocolate cake each nite. My oldest daughter upon first entering the hotel immediately stated she liked the "other hotel" better (referring to The Venecian in Las Vegas!). But as soon as she got her first bite of cake she exclaimed, "I like this hotel!"
The upper courtyard with the two hot spas is beautiful. Totally unexpected from the online pics which I guess are not updated. It's a very pretty place to relax.
Everyone at the hotel gets 5 stars for courtesy and friendliness. We would definitely choose this place again for our stopovers in San Jose.

review_text: We spent our first night in Costa Rica at Grano de Oro. Very solid, architecturally distinctive hotel. Our room was good, but the distinctive feature of the hotel is its common spaces: courtyard restaurant, rooftop jaccuzzi with a mini tropical garden as an ante-room, spiffy lobby and the entryway. Breakfast at the restaurant was very good. Good service with maybe just a whiff of snottiness. It is located about 20 min walk from the center or $4 dollar taxi ride. Good if its just a layover point as you don't have to go through San Jose to get to the airport. Less convenient if you're planning to walk around San Jose.

review_text:
The first night I was there (on the way to Osa Peninsula) -- no problems. The room was nice and clean and somewhat pretty -- but I was expecting something more. The jacuzzis on the roof are very cool. Got room service; food was good but it certainly wasn't the best food I've had -- but then in California, we have a chance to eat at a lot of nice places.
The second visit (on the way back from Osa), I was treated like a second-class citizen. I went into the restaurant for lunch at 2 pm (again, I'm alone), and I asked about dinner that night (I didn't want to do room service again, and thought maybe i could just eat at the bar within the restaurant). Shockingly, I was told that it would be best if I got room service as it got "very busy" at night. I was stunned. Can you imagine them saying that to a man, a couple, or a family!? So, then, I'm sitting at the table for lunch...the restaurant is not busy. I had a glass of water and menus. Then I waited for someone to take my order. And I waited. And I tried to make eye contact. And they were setting tables around me. Walking right by me. Not a word. Not a look. Not a "un momento". So, gathered my things, got up and left. I thought for sure they would catch me and ask what was wrong. But nope. Nothing. I was invisible. The next morning I had 30 minutes to eat my breakfast before catching the plane. I asked if there was time to get breakfast. They told me I could only get the continental breakfast. Since that's not what I wanted, I said I'd just have coffee then. The guy then turned around and started walking away. I assumed I was to follow. A moment later, it was as if he caught himself being surly and rude to me and forced out a "right this way." I've never been treated that way in my life. Personally, I don't think people should support establishments that treat women so poorly. So, please try somewhere else. Thanks.

review_title: Nice hotel, even though no a/c
review_text: We enjoyed our stay at the Grano de Oro in May. We stayed a total of 3 nights - not consecutive nights, and had 2 different rooms. The hotel is very clean, the staff is very friendly and accommodating, but without A/C it can be a bit uncomfortable. There was also no elevator access to our 2nd floor room, but the bags were delivered to our room. The hotel is very impressive looking, but most of the glitz is reserved for the lobby and restaurant - the rooms we had were just standard rooms. If I were to go back to San Jose, I would consider staying there again, particularly if it were not in their rainy/humid season.

review_text: We stayed at this hotel for our first 2 nights in costa rica. It was simply beautiful! If it were not for san jose itself we would have loved to stay longer. It is not in a very nice area, but for san jose it is probably ok, reasonably close to town anyway (easy walking distance to shops etc).The hotel itself is like a refurbished victorian mansion, mixed with all the exotic flora and fauna of costa rica. The staff were all incredibly helpful. We were travelling in low season and had decided to plan the holiday as we went. The front desk staff were more than happy to help us with booking other accommodation and tours as we didnt speak spanish. The restaurant setting was amazing, perfect for a romantic dinner. The food although excellent was perhaps a little too up market to eat everynight. Overall wonderful hotel, great value for money.

review_text:
My boyfriend and I spent the first night of our Costa Rica vacation at Hotel Grano de Oro. What a fabulous start to an amazing trip!! Grano de Oro is truly a first class establishment. While San Jose leaves much to be desired, this hotel is like a breath of fresh air. It is a beautifully restored large Victorian mansion. We do not typically prefer bed & breakfasts or boutique hotels and we LOVED this place. We reserved a Standard room and it was perfect – very clean! They also have really relaxing music piped into the rooms which was a nice touch. The restaurant in the hotel is excellent. We had dinner there and then breakfast the next morning. Very romantic! Staff was very helpful with directions and restaurant recommendations. As for San Jose…not much to see there, but go to the “central” area just to check it out. I was disappointed that there were no real bargains, as you would typically find in other Latin American cities. You do not need to spend more than one night here.
Also – we rented a car at the airport to tour the country. Take cabs in San Jose – there are no street signs and even the taxi drivers had trouble finding their way around! One note on driving – if you are uncomfortable with windy, steep two lane highways in some areas and massive crater potholes in others, you might want to think twice about renting. I would always prefer to drive myself, so I did not have a problem with it, but heard complaints from others. Also – if you do rent a car – definitely rent a very sturdy 4 wheel drive. We sprung for the Toyota 4 Runner and were SO glad we did!! The road from Arenal to Tamarindo was the worst!! We rented from Thrifty and had no problems. We originally booked through Advantage/Economy online – note that the “total” price is going to end up being at least twice that with the insurance in the fine print. We were unpleasantly surprised upon our arrival and switched rental agencies.

review_text:
First impression.....the hotel reminds me of a home from San Francisco. Very cute. The lobby and dining room...very beautiful. The rooms...there a re a few newer deluxe rooms that have air conditioning. While you may have reserved, paid and confirmed your reservation for one of these you may not get it. If you are not able to get an a/c room you are forced to open the windows and breathe in fumes from passing cars. If the traffic bothers you can close the windows and crank up the fan. The restaurant is another adventure. It took 45 minutes to order, 1.5 hours to receive food and another 30 minutes for them to correct the order. I'm deathly allergic to avocados (this was explained in advance) and instead of giving me a new salad they must have just picked out MOST of the avocado slices. Needless to say I was not happy. Normally I would just change hotels, but now I was to sick to endure moving hotels.
Outside of that, the neighborhood is not the greatest. During peak traffic times the hotel is a 45 minute drive from the airport. There are several very nice hotels right by the airport that would make a good pitstop before and after your flight.

review_text: The hotel was beautiful! We stayed here 4 nights total (3 nights on the front end, and 1 night right before we flew out). We stayed in the Garden Suite. Very dark wood, very library-esque. The only thing w/ this room is that it is just below the stairs that lead to the 2nd floor. So...you hear people walking upstairs at times...creaking steps. It isn't terrible, but not the best! The lobby however is very modern! The restaurant at the hotel is the best food we had all trip! Inexpensive! It is a bit more fancy than we anticipated (we brought 1 pair of water/walking shoes, and flip flops). Could have dressed up a bit here, but really…it wasn’t a big deal! The 2nd day here, we had in room massages ($70 each)…great! Staff at the hotel is SO friendly and accommodating! They speak wonderful English. We stayed 3 nights in the Garden Suite, but changed our last night here (on the return trip) to a lower grade room (save some $, and the huge room wasn’t necessary b/c we were getting up SO early to go to the airport)

review_text:
On the suggestion of the agent we worked with in Costa Rica we stayed
at the Grano de Oro on our first night in San Jose and the last night
before we came home (April 26th and May 7th). What a fabulous little hotel downtown.
As we pulled up to the front I pointed the building out to my husband
because it was so lovely only to find that it was our hotel. So pretty! We found that it was a restored mansion and boy was it done well. Although not completely original, there was a definate attention to detail. We loved the courtyard area in the restaurant and the large wooden windows that opened up onto it allowing for a cool breeze if you were seated just inside. All of the fabrics and texture in the restaurant make it feel very luxurious. Even the china
was beautiful...such attention to detail. We heard before the trip that this hotel's restaurant was one of the best in the city and we found it to be delicious.
Upon arrival on the 26th, we were an hour later than we expected arriving just before 10pm when the restaurant was scheduled to close. After getting checked in, the front desk staff (all who were warm and very friendly and helpful) asked if we were hungry and wanted to go to the restaurant. After a long day of travel we said yes and she called to see if they could stay open for us. The restaurant said yes so the bellman showed us to our room where we quickly changed out of travel clothes. We headed down and sat at the bar. The front desk had told us to take our time, but we decided not to keep them waiting since they were staying open late. We ordered a mohito and mora (blackberry) margarita and both were delicious! We also had a fruit plate (the first of many) and a great dip made of heart of palm and cheese served with crackers. After our snack we retired for the night. Our room was relatively close to reception so we didn't wander much through the rest of the hotel but the hallway we did see was lovely and we really enjoyed all the old historical pictures of the area that were displayed.
We had a standard room for the first night since we were really only there to sleep. The bed was a little hard but the linens were clean and soft and the room was nice. Although there was no A/C, we really didn't need it with the fan and a breeze from the open window. The bathroom was good sized and the water was hot.
We had breakfast the next day in the hotel restaurant. A yogurt and fruit parfait, bagel (ask for cream cheese or jam or else it will come dry), smoked salmon omelette and pancakes with plantains (like bananas) and of course our first taste of CR coffee (cafe britt). All was delicious.
We headed back to the Nature Air terminal to head to Arenal, then Tamarindo before coming back the early afternoon of May 7th. This time we had a superior room further back from reception. What a lovely place. We were already pleased from the first stay, but getting the chance to walk through the halls further back we really got to see the rest of the place. There were a number of little courtyards with fountains as we walked along. I checked out the roof-top jacuzzi and although we didn't use it, the area was really nice.
This time we were in town to shop. We had a private driver arranged through Latitudes Adventure Travel that took us on a tour of San Jose, to a local place for lunch and then to the market so we could shop for coffee, rum, cigars, etc. Before heading out we made a 7:30 pm dinner reservation in the hotel restaurant...we wanted to try out the real thing and have dinner at the place that was one of the best in the city.
After shopping, a rest and catching a movie (much of the TV was in English) we showered and changed for dinner. We were not disappointed. The service was impecable...we started with a bottle of wine and a plate of 3 cheeses. Both were wonderful. I ordered the spinach ravioli stuffed with cheese in a marinara/tomato sauce and my husband had lamb of some kind, shank I think. We finished with 2 desserts, Tres leches (3 milk) cake and a French apple tart. All were delicious. The service was excellent and the waiter seemed pleased that we ordered all in Spanish although quite obviously tourists and not very good at it. When we struggled he helped us and when we were very confused he spoke English. A perfect balance though especially for a pair that tries hard to speak the language even though we have far from mastered it. Our bill was $99 (with tax and 10% service) and to show our appreciation we left our waiter a $20 bill for his excellent service. Still less than we spend on a meal like that at home.
The next morning, another delicious breakfast this time of pancakes with mora syrup (blackberry) and smoked salmon benedict. A perfect meal to end the trip! We loved this little hotel (even though a pool on the last day would have been nice) and would stay here again. Highly recommend!
One small note: the 2nd day after arriving in Arenal my husband was sick for a day or 2 with an upset stomach. After some imodium he was fine and we finished the trip. One the plane home he started getting sick again and stayed that way for 4 days before he decided bland food was enough and ate a heavy meal that didn't sit well. After 5 hours of vomiting (3 hours of vomiting blood) violently, he ended up in the emergency room the Sunday after we got home (we got home Tuesday night). I have never seen him so sick and he was begging for an ambulance. Before he got so ill he had figured out that the only thing he had eaten the first few days and the last was the smoked salmon. review_title: an absolute gem of a hotel
review_text:
My spouse and I stayed at this hotel for a total of four nights -- two at the beginning of our Costa Rica trip, and two at the end. It is a lovely spot -- quiet and serene -- and our rooms during both stays were well-appointed, comfortable, and even elegant.
The staff is extremely friendly and helpful. Everyone at the front desk speaks excellent English and is willing to assist with taxis, restaurant recommendations, touring advice, and anything else you might need.
The restaurant in the hotel is also top-notch and very reasonably priced. On my last morning there I had rice and beans, fried plaintains, blackberry juice, and coffee, all for less than $7 US. I sat in the lovely outdoor courtyard in the center of the restaurant , which is beautifully decorated and very peaceful. It made me never want to come home!
For our last two nights, our room had a special little private patio with its own fountain, where we could sit outside. (It even had a plexiglass canopy so that we could sit out there in the rain.) We had our last Costa Rican dinner (room service) out there on the patio, with the lights dimmed and the fountain playing. It was really delightful.
We will definitely stay in this hotel any time we return to Costa Rica. San Jose (the city) isn't much to look at, but the stay at Grano de Oro is worth it.

I have to say that by reading the reviews i was expecting a nice decent hotel but when i walked in to the lobby i was very much impressed with the look and feel of the hotel, it was more then i thought it will be, the staff in the hotel are the nicest. One thing i was not very happy about is the short amount of irons they have , when i needed one i was told that they didnt have any left.
The restaurant was good but a little overrated by the staff, i was told that the restaurant was one of the best 100 restaurants in central america , i dont feel it was that way, also expensive for what you get, the portions are very very very very small, so if you stay there try another restaurant , they forgot our soup and the waiter gave us a hard time when asked to change an ingredient in our meal.
The rooms are small but for what you pay is more then perfect , i felt like i was staying at a family member's house and not in a hotel. Give it a try, you will like it and for the price! you cant beat that!

review_text:
My wife and I spent our last night in Costa Rica at Grano de Oro and loved the hotel and restaurant. After a dusty trip from Montezuma, it was nice to feel civilized again.
The hotel is beautiful and the service is excellent, especially in the restaurant, which may be considered expensive for CR, but very reasonable when compared to NJ prices. I definately would recommend this place over a comparable or higher priced chain hotel.
That being said, I would mention that we flew in from Montezuma (Tambor) and landed during Friday evening rush hour. The taxi ride to San Jose was about 40 minutes. If I had to do it over again I would have stayed closer to the airport for one night.

review_title: This is the place to stay - rich or poor. Wonderful value.
review_text:
Without a doubt this is a little gem in San Jose. If you are thinking of stay here and aren't sure - do it. It is charming and elegant and stunning - all the while affordable.
This boutique hotel offers excellent service, pleasant room and drop dead gorgeous restaurant and some of the best food we have ever had.
We stayed 4 different nights as we were in and out of San Jose. Stayed in rooms 18, 21 and 40. 18 and 21 faced the charming little inner courtyard and were great. At that time the restaurant was still being held in the little courtyard but that has now changed. Room 40 is nice and large and bright but a bit on the noisy side as a main street goes by it and the bed shook each time a truck or large vehicle went by. We advised staff that the bed shook and we felt we should be moved and they said they couldn't because the hotel was full. They said no one had ever expressed concerns about the bed shaking. We find that hard to believe. We were a bit upset as we had already stayed 3 other nights with them, this was our 4th and we had eaten at the restaurant. Felt they should have moved us and put someone who had not checked in yet - in our room. They didn't. We felt angry, but somehow after we settled in our room and the traffic died a bit we slept okay and it did not disrupt our sleep. We still think proper service would be to have moved us - even upgraded us, but that is our opinion. This was the only negative we have and felt that the front desk should have been more empowered to handle customer recovery rather than the blanket statement of "you would have to address your concerns to the manager (who isn't here right now) if you insist on being moved or require a discount." Since we slept okay, we didn't do anything and since we had already complained, we sometimes get tired of fighting for things and we just forgot about it.
Outside of that - the hotel is a perfect place to stay and everything else was wonderful. Rooms are clean!!!! and spacious and nicely decorated. They have nice "quite please" signs that they put in the halls in early morning and at night to remind guests to be quiet which is nice. The hotel is actually very big and many rooms are hidden from initial view. There are touches of beauty and character and just a very stylish boutique hotel with a real Costa Rican feel. Well recommended.
We found this hotel highly rated in our "Costa Rica for Dummies" tour book and it was everything the author said it was and we are so glad we stayed her. Staying downtown San Jose is a mistake and not suggested. This is the perfect location and not too far from the airports but not so close you hear planes.
The newly moved restaurant is unreal. It is breathtaking and the sense of luxury is everywhere - yet one can afford it. Meals are some of the best we had in Costa Rica and the service is all performed by mature and good looking Costa Rican men. No bored teenagers working here like in the US or Canada. These are professional wait staff and they are great. Food is beyond good and we ate so much b/c we couldn't resist. Very affordable and we at our fill and ate beautiful food for $40/couple. Really good.
The hotel is finishing up with renos but they are mostly over and should not be a problem. Go and enjoy and write a review as you will be very happy. They offer blow dryers at the front desk and they arrange private taxi's say to the airport or Monteverde or Arenal and they are just wonderful that way. Only $130 per couple for a large mini van private taxi to Monteverde. Excellent cost and so comfortable and no bus and no other people bothering you. Way to go for sure.
They have a great little gift store on sight and even after 2 weeks in Costa Rica we came back and picked up some things there that we didn't see elsewhere.
This hotel is one of the neatest we have stayed in and made our times in San Jose very enjoyable and we felt safe and everything is spotless and professional and great front desk staff and we can't suggest enough to stay here.
Enjoy!!

This boutique hotel offers excellent service, pleasant room and drop dead gorgeous restaurant and some of the best food we have ever had.
We stayed 4 different nights as we were in and out of San Jose. Stayed in rooms 18, 21 and 40. 18 and 21 faced the charming little inner courtyard and were great. At that time the restaurant was still being held in the little courtyard but that has now changed. Room 40 is nice and large and bright but a bit on the noisy side as a main street goes by it and the bed shook each time a truck or large vehicle went by. We advised staff that the bed shook and we felt we should be moved and they said they couldn't because the hotel was full. They said no one had ever expressed concerns about the bed shaking. We find that hard to believe. We were a bit upset as we had already stayed 3 other nights with them, this was our 4th and we had eaten at the restaurant. Felt they should have moved us and put someone who had not checked in yet - in our room. They didn't. We felt angry, but somehow after we settled in our room and the traffic died a bit we slept okay and it did not disrupt our sleep. We still think proper service would be to have moved us - even upgraded us, but that is our opinion. This was the only negative we have and felt that the front desk should have been more empowered to handle customer recovery rather than the blanket statement of "you would have to address your concerns to the manager (who isn't here right now) if you insist on being moved or require a discount." Since we slept okay, we didn't do anything and since we had already complained, we sometimes get tired of fighting for things and we just forgot about it.
Outside of that - the hotel is a perfect place to stay and everything else was wonderful. Rooms are clean!!!! and spacious and nicely decorated. They have nice "quite please" signs that they put in the halls in early morning and at night to remind guests to be quiet which is nice. The hotel is actually very big and many rooms are hidden from initial view. There are touches of beauty and character and just a very stylish boutique hotel with a real Costa Rican feel. Well recommended.
We found this hotel highly rated in our "Costa Rica for Dummies" tour book and it was everything the author said it was and we are so glad we stayed her. Staying downtown San Jose is a mistake and not suggested. This is the perfect location and not too far from the airports but not so close you hear planes.
The newly moved restaurant is unreal. It is breathtaking and the sense of luxury is everywhere - yet one can afford it. Meals are some of the best we had in Costa Rica and the service is all performed by mature and good looking Costa Rican men. No bored teenagers working here like in the US or Canada. These are professional wait staff and they are great. Food is beyond good and we ate so much b/c we couldn't resist. Very affordable and we at our fill and ate beautiful food for $40/couple. Really good.
The hotel is finishing up with renos but they are mostly over and should not be a problem. Go and enjoy and write a review as you will be very happy. They offer blow dryers at the front desk and they arrange private taxi's say to the airport or Monteverde or Arenal and they are just wonderful that way. Only $130 per couple for a large mini van private taxi to Monteverde. Excellent cost and so comfortable and no bus and no other people bothering you. Way to go for sure.
They have a great little gift store on sight and even after 2 weeks in Costa Rica we came back and picked up some things there that we didn't see elsewhere.
This hotel is one of the neatest we have stayed in and made our times in San Jose very enjoyable and we felt safe and everything is spotless and professional and great front desk staff and we can't suggest enough to stay here.

review_title: Great Food, Comfortable Room, Helpful Staff
review_text:
We spent a night at this hotel on the way to a cruise. The hotel is clean and attractive in dark woods and colors. It looks much nicer than the pictures. It is very much a boutique hotel, and is a great alternative to the American chains.
The restaurant was great -- and they donate the profits to victims of domestic violence. Staff was knowledgeable, the food was very good, and very reasonably priced.
The hotel arranged a transfer to the cruise for us, and it went without a hitch. We asked the driver to pick us up at the end of the cruise, but neglected to get a card from him. We found after boarding the cruise that the time we had asked him to come was well after the required disembarkation time. We got back in touch with the hotel by email, and they (1) tracked down the driver; (2) rescheduled the time; and (3) took care of the billing and payment arrangements for us. I thought this was service above and beyond the call.
Our room was clean and comfortable. We had some noise issues from people dragging luggage across the floor above us, but I'm not sure that would have anything to do with the hotel itself.

review_text:

review_title: Exquisite restaurant in a great hotel
review_text:
We stayed at the Grano de Oro for 3 nights in December as the start of a 19 day trip through Costa Rica. Our flight was scheduled to get in late, so I contacted the hotel and arranged for transport from the airport, which was quickly reserved, and at a very reasonable price. I had also noted that our arrival was after the hours of the restaurant, so I asked if there was any possibility of either having some food left for us or if there was another restaurant nearby that was open late. The hotel allowed us to look at their online menu and select some cold items to be left for us, which we did- I got the spinach salad with gorgonzola, avocado, and pears, my husband got the chicken and brie sandwich, and we shared a fruit plate and cheese plate. When we arrived, check in was quick and easy, we were shown to our room, and told that our dinner was waiting for us in the dining room, which it was, on a beautifully set table. Everything was fantastic! What a great first night.
Our room (#15) was comfortable and clean, although it was fairly close to the dining area, which meant that there could be some noise around meal times.
I also had a massage arranged by the hotel, which was inexpensive and quite pleasant, although the temperature in the room was a bit on the cold side.
The restaurant was so good, we ate there every night we stayed there. Incidentally, the hotel restaurant donates a percentage of their profits to a women's charity, which I thought was fascinating and showed a real sense of community responsibility. The breakfasts were innovative and exceptionally tasty (from the granola to the banana macadamia pancakes- yum!), and our dinners there were always prepared exactly to order with fresh ingredients and staff that was attentive but not overbearing. And the desserts!
I highly recommend the Grano de Oro and its exceptional restaurant!

review_text:
My friend and i just returned from Costa Rica and booked the first 2 nights and the final night of our vacation at the grano de Oro.
What a beautiful little hotel. Because we stayed twice, we were able to experience 2 different layouts of the standard room. We thought the rooms were adorable, and had everything we needed for a comfortable stay.
The best part about this hotel was definetely the staff. The front desk and the restaurant staff went out of their way to make us feel at home. What an amazing bunch of people!
And the food in the restaurant is UNBELEIVABLE!!! The best food we had while in Costa Rica BY FAR! AMAZING. And almost too inexpensive -- I felt as if we were robbing them!
I would highly reccomend this hotel as a jumping off point and as a great final destination on your Costa Rica holiday!!!

review_title: A bit noisy, but still lovely and charming
review_text:
My husband and I spent a night here at the beginning of a 9-night Costa Rica vacation last fall, and were pleased overall with the property. Check in was fairly quick and quite friendly, and the public areas of the hotel are lovely, with several small foliage-draped courtyards.
The superior room was not large or fancy, but was certainly comfortable enought for the night. We had a window looking out onto a pretty open air courtyard, and a spacious-enough bathroom. The shower was large and the water pressure was good. The only real complaint we had was that it was very noisy in the morning (starting pretty early). Not sure if they were doing construction to the hotel itself or just nearby, but there were a lot of chainsaw/jackhammer type sounds in the hours before we checked out.
We had already eaten dinner by the time we arrived, but did partake in a couple of cocktails--the mojitos were especially delicious! Breakfast the next morning was very good as well, and we were shocked at how inexpensive it was.
Transportation between the airport and hotel will be somewhere around $15-$20, and the ride is around 20 minutes or so.
I would say GdO is a very good choice in San Jose, and we'd absolutely stay there again.
Please feel free to email me (address in profile) if you have any questions!

review_text: The Grano de Oro is a great little hotel. We stayed two nights, one when we arrived in San Jose and one the night before we left. Recommended for a first night in Costa Rica after arriving by plane.

review_text:
In my opinion, there isn't much to do in San Jose. We spent 4 nights here, but we left the city everyday to explore different parts of Costa Rica. I made the mistake of booking my hotel before I did my research on Costa Rica. There is no way I should have stayed in San Jose for four nights. Of course, none of that is the hotel's fault.
Now on to the review. We a mixed group of mid-20s travelers. The Grano de Oro is an awesome hotel! It's a very quaint, homely hotel. The rooms were spacious, and clean. It had a very Victorian feel to it. From the moment we arrived, the staff was extremely helpful. We arrived early, and they accomodated us immediately. There is a upstairs area with two small hot tubs. These things were tiny, but surprisingly, I really enjoyed. It just felt like a really good escape.
The restaurant is wonderful. Good food and great service. By the second day, the service staff knew our group name. Definitely dine out on the patio if weather permits. Absolute treat.
On a side note, I'd highly recommend visiting Tabacon Hot Springs. Get there by mid afternoon and stay until dinner (make your reservations before you arrive). This place is incredible. Feels like tropical paradise!

They also have a computer in the lobbey with free internet. The front desk is very helpful and will organize anything you need. It is also close to the airport if you need to catch a flight. A very nice hotel.

review_title: Truly an oasis in San Jose
review_text:
We stopped her on our first night in a regular room and our last two nights in the Vista de Oro suite, while on honeymoon. We are so glad we did as it helped us recover from long journeys and prepare for the next.
The rooms were clean, well maintained and full of charm & character. The colonial style architecture, plants, artwork, old photos and decor make this a truly beautiful building in what is a fairly austere city. They do have some building going on as they expand currently but you don't notice this once you are inside and there's little or no noise.
The staff were all delightful, friendly and willing to assist in any way. The Canadian owners have certainly recruited well, especially the dining room staff who were extremely professional.
The food is cooked by a french chef and you can tell, as everything we tried was well cooked and presented, with a good selection of wines (for Costa Rica) and not expensive considering what you would pay for similar in Europe.
Try the Cardenal Mendoza brandy after dinner. It is as smooth as they come and full of flavour. I am now tracking it down in the UK.
San Jose is not much to write home about, but there are some interesting markets to visit. Just don't make eye contact with the shop owners on the doorstep or they'll have you in the shop for hours, trying to sell their entire stock. The English football shirts are largely fakes as well. I know as I have the real thing.
I would be surprised if there is a more delightful place to stay in San Jose, so I recommend it to you all.

review_text:
Stayed here for two nights at the beginning of a trip to Costa Rica. San Jose is not a great place to visit but is worth a day tour downtown and the Grano de Oro makes a great refuge.
This is a lovely hotel but I have a major criticism of the room, which opened onto a dark corridor and had virtually no natural light so you could not tell if it was night or day outside. The hotel was full and we may have had the last and poorest room - apart from that, the hotel is very good with helpful and friendly staff.
However, what you have to do if you stay here is have dinner in the restaurant. The food is fantastic and the whole experience first class. You would pay four or five times as much in a comparable restaurant in London or New York.

review_title: The best room in the world
review_text:
My daughter and I have just returned from a 2 week trip to Costa Rica. We stayed the last night of our trip in Grano de Oro. Upon our arrival at the hotel, we were told that the deluxe room that we had reserved was not available due to construction. They instead gave us the best room in the hotel--room number 25. I have stayed in the best hotels all over the world, and I have never stayed in a room as beautiful. The room was on the top floor of the hotel, accessible by an outside stairway above the terrace and hot tubs. The room was over 24 feet by 14 feet, furnished with 2 ultrasuede couches, oriental rugs, 7 silk shaded lamps, a large kingsize bed in dark wood, and a wall of windows 24 feet long overlooking the volcanoes and twinkling lights of the city. At the end of the room 3 steps led up to a large jacuzzi, surrounded by tropical plants and large pottery urns. A separate bathroom included a shower, toilet, sink and dressing table. One coffee table held a bromeliad in a planter and a china tea set. There were several dark antique chests and dressers. One at the end of the bed was covered in a small oriental rug. Beautiful camel colored draperies stretched across the windows and also surrounded the jacuzzi for privacy. Other urns of tropical plants were spread throughout the room.
The restaurant was exquisite. Our lunch was superb. Our 3 course dinner with 3 accompanying wines was perfect in every way. The dining room staff and its manager were as professional as you will ever find. This is truly a gem of a hotel. I noticed some of the interior rooms are dark, and if I had stayed in one of those, I would have been truly disappointed. As it turned out, I have now experienced one of the most beautiful rooms in the world.

review_text: My husband and I stayed at Grano de Oro on the last night of our Costa Rican vacation in order to avoid doing the long drive from Manuel Antonio on the day of our flight home. The hotel is charming - built in two old mansions - and has lots of twists and turns. Our room was at the top of its own little staircase. The service here was phenomenal and everyone spoke fluent English. Within minutes of check-in, a delicious fruit plate consisting of pineapple, mangoes, etc. arrived at our door. Such a welcome surprise since we hadn't had time to eat. Our room had a bathtub - nice ammenity that we missed at some of the other hotels we stayed in on our trip. I noticed a lot of other little touches around the hotel that made it feel homey - they even had bookshelves of free books for you to read and a note asking you to leave behind books for other travellers. Don't miss the rooftop hot tub/garden area - it's very pretty. The only negative we noticed was that our room did not have air conditioning. As it turned out, it rained during our stay, and we just opened the windows for ventilation. We would definitely stay here again.

review_text:
My husband and I stayed the last night of our honeymoon at the Grano de Oro. We've already vowed to come back to Costa Rica and the Grano is on our list of must revisits.
The hotel staff was professional and helpful. They gave us many helpful tips on shopping in San Jose though we never actually went; we spent our time in the hotel rather than going out!
Our unique room was beautifully appointed, and the water fountain in our garden was soothing after our tumultuous drive from Playa Ocotal to San Jose. We spent a few hours out in our garden area listening to the fountain sprinkle down to the fish swimming in the pool. It was perfect!
The food at the Grano de Oro was by far the best food we ate in Costa Rica. My husband had seabass for dinner, and for breakfast, I highly suggest the traditional Tico breakfast.
Take the time to look through the entire hotel. The black and white photos of Costa Rica's history are beautiful and insipring. Visit the Grano de Oro. It's worth any amount of time one could spend there visiting.

review_title: One of the best in Boston
review_text:
We stayed at Grano de Oro for a total of three nights in May 2006. It is an excellent base in San Jose for the beginning and end of your trip in Costa Rica.
Rooms are clean and comfortable and have character. The hotel has a good restaurant-- the banana macademia nut pancakes at breakfast are fantastic!
What really makes this place is the staff. Everyone was kind and helpful. We arrived late the first night and they arranged for us to have a lovely dinner delivered to our room with wine and candels. There is no problem having laundry done, storing luggage, getting restaurant recommendations and taxis. On our last night we were upgraded to their best suite.
The hotel was completing major renovations/construction in May 2006. They are completely rennovating one wing and building a new restaurant and lobby.
We enjoyed our stay and would go back. Recommended

review_title: A wonderful place to end a trip
review_text:
We stayed here during the last two days of our honeymoon and I wish we had gotten the chance to stay longer. This place gets good reviews for a reason.
It's in a beautiful mansion and each room is different. It was such an interesting and charming spot to stay that we enjoyed just walking to our room because there was so much to see in the hallways -- from the paintings on the walls to the fountains and flowers.
The place is really classy and the staff is friendly and helpful. You shouldn't stay here without trying out the hotel restaurant. We had dinner and breakfast here and, although I am a big fan of checking out different restaurants around town, I would have eaten here for another couple of meals.
It was also fun to hang out at the rooftop spa. There are two spas so you can still have a little space if another group or couple is already on the roof when you arrive.
The location is great. It's not in the center of town but close enough for a short cab ride. We explored the area around the hotel on foot and felt perfectly safe. It was nice to wander an untouristy neighborhood.
I must highly recommend this place along with everyone else.

review_text:
Grano de Oro, San Jose, Costa Rica March 2006. ----. This hotel is a treasure. In contrast to the glitz and hustle of modern glass and steel hotels, this is a breath of fresh air. The Grano de Oro is an old mansion, expanded over the years, with winding passages and delightful rooms, comfortable and well appointed. There are lovely plantings everywhere, arrangements of heliconia blossoms, fountains and soft lighting. The hotel is close to, but not exactly in, downtown, close to museums and the National Theater ($ 1.00 cab ride). You can also walk it in 20-30 minutes or take a local bus.
The restaurant is marvelous, beautiful, with very attentive service from a personable staff, excellent food and modest prices. It was so good and so reasonable that we were not motivated to go anywhere else to eat. And there is a frosting on the cake; all the profits from the restaurant go to a non-profit foundation to assist and house children of sexploitation and abuse. It’s easy to eat breakfast and lunch, since few others eat here. But dinner brings in a lot of people from outside, gringos and Ticos, so make reservations in advance.
We used Grano de Oro as our base, as we went off on two different directions (diving in the Cocos Islands on the Sea Hunter liveaboard and another 10 days exploring far northern Costa Rica). Each time we left some bags in their storage room (at no charge), which we did not need for that leg of the trip. We stayed 3 times, a total of 4 nights. There are 3 levels of room, Standard, Superior and Deluxe; the cost difference is not that great, so we went for the larger better rooms and it was worth it. Compared to other hotels, prices are reasonable.
Front desk staff could not be more accommodating and pleasant. From calling a taxi to arranging a rental car, they were efficient and responsive. If there are any downsides to this place, it’s that they are very popular and reservations in advance are essential; don’t expect to drop in and get a room.
By the way, we travel a lot, all over the world, and I’ve never recommended a hotel so highly. We are usually much more critical, but Grano de Oro is truly a grain-of-gold.

review_text:
We stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro for two nights at the end of 2005. The hotel is as described: Rooms are clean, comfortable, and elegantly decorated. The bathroom was huge with a tub and enough space to spread your stuff around. It was a nice luxurious treat after spending 1 week in the Osa Peninsula.
They have a great restaurant which we ate at a couple of times and celebrated New Year's eve. The food was more continental and upscale. It was very good and affordable.
Check out the gift shop. It has a lot of great crafts from local artist. I am still regretting not buying that Jaguar print hanging behind the reception area. Wonder if it's still there.
The center of downtown San Jose is about a 15 to 20 minute walk from the hotel. The staff was friendly and helpful in giving us directions, recommendations to eat or getting a cab.
Only one minor complaint. The rooms on the left side of the restaurant (I believe rooms 1 to 4. We had room 2) are above the kitchen area. So you will hear kitchen noise starting from 5am lasting to 11pm. So unless you're a heavy sleeper I would asked for a room away from the kitchen or pay the extra $20 to upgrade. We booked the standard room. Also, I noticed that people's experience in hotels vary considerably based on the type of room they get. I usually book the cheapest room but sometimes its not alway the best since the room may be located in a heavily trafficed area, etc. It would be nice if people can mentioned what room they got because I think that makes a difference in peoples perception of the hotel.

review_text: We had been planning to stay at the Grano de Oro in San Jose since our trip to Costa Rica the previous year when we'd visited Villa Caletas, a fellow member of the "Small Distinctive Hotels of Costa Rica." The Grano de Oro lived up to our expectations, for the most part (in its defense, our expectations were probably unrealistically high). The property is undergoing renovations--an addition is being added--and so isn't quite as lovely as its picture on the website would have you believe. The interior, however, remains beautiful, elegant, and tropical. We were first given a room located adjacent to the cafe and were thus worried about noise late at night; the desk staff graciously offered us a better room, on the second floor, and we were quite pleased with it. We had a light lunch in the cafe--the quality of the food is very, very high--and made use more than once of the complimentary Internet access in the lobby. The only caveats I'd offer to travelers staying at the Grano de Oro is that its location vis a vis the downtown shopping area is not as central as some other hotels--plus, walking around after dusk in the Grano de Oro's neighborhood doesn't seem like a very wise idea (I guess, though, that you could say that about any part of San Jose). Fortunately, it's easy to hail a cab and it's just a short drive to the center of the city, if you wish to see it. The Grano de Oro is certainly the most luxurious establishment in San Jose, and travelers will find it well worth the few extra dollars to stay in its restful, relaxing environment.
