review_text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for our first and last two nights on our honeymoon. While San Jose is not the most beautiful city, Grano de Oro is absolutely gorgeous, and within walking distance from some of the downtown sites. Just don't wander around at night, it can be a little scary and dirty, especially for people from the US not used to a typical central american city. Plus, driving is interesting to say the least. It is very easy to get lost in SAn Jose, and the drivers are reckless. In the countryside, the roads are in really terrible condition, very narrow and winding, with steep hills. Four wheel drive vehicles are a must especially during the rainy season. And if you are not used to driving a manual transmission, make sure to specify automatic when booking, because the driving is bad enough on its own. (Just imagine stopping in heavy traffic on a really steep hill!!) We stayed in the garden suite, which has its own (very!) private garden and a patio with a little table and chairs. We had breakfast out there one morning among the flowers. You would never know you were in the middle of a city. Food was very good, although a bit more expensive than other places. The room was spotless and beautifully appointed, with a jacuzzi tub, a king-sized bed and a little sitting room with a tv-not that we really used it. The whole room is done in deep mahogany wood and burgundy. This hotel (and San Jose in general) is a great jumping off point for going to other areas of Costa Rica. we also stayed at Tabacon Resort,near Arenal and Villas Caleta,in Punta Leona- both also really great places to stay. Also, for a really hassle-free planning experience, go to centralamerica.com I planned our entire vacation using that site, and everything was exactly as we expected, and the prices were fair.

review_text:
When my fiance and I arrived in San Jose we were freaked out! A word of warning- when we arrived in San Jose for our week long stay in Costa Rica we were ready to get back on the plane and go home. The city is dirty and poverty stricken. Prostitutes and homeless people wandered the streets begging at the doors of our car. I would advise arriving in the day time! But we got there at night time and the streets are not marked- we got SO lost in our rental car trying to find this hotel.
However, when we finally found Grano de Oro we were delighted! The service, the aura, the whole hotel, hot tubs, the rooms and food were wonderful. And the next day when we headed out of the city and began to make our way through the country... WOW! I now love Costa Rica. The food, the people, the country views, the waterfalls, the adventure, this country is a must!

review_text: We just returned from the Hotel Grano de Oro in San Jose, Costa Rica. The staff service was excellent and the food served by the wonderful French Chef was outstanding! The menu prices (most reasonable too!)INCLUDE Taxes and Tip AND ALL PROFITS of the resturant go to charity. I loved the rooms, each had their own personality, either done in reds or greens, velvets, tapistry, and wonderful tiled bathrooms. They come in all sizes and no two are the same. The home was built about 50 years ago and is sparkling clean and kept in top notch condition. They have two spas on the roof and are expanding to take over the house next door to add on. Oh yes, they also have a laptop hooked up for guests to use at no cost. For the service and plushness of the place the $95 I paid for the room was a real bargin.

review_text:
We were visitors at the Grano de Oro in November 2005. The hotel is expanding and adding a new resturant and several more rooms. The service at this hotel is wonderful. The hotel is small and if you stay several days they recognize you and call you by name. This hotel does not have the feel of one of the larger hotels but is very intimate.
The resturant must be one of the best in San Jose. There were many locals who would eat there. The hotel has a victorian coffee plantation ambiance.
There is an area with hot tubs and free high speed interent.
While I was there I met a American who lives in the north of Costa Rica, and who said he had visited the hotel many times and had spent the night in most of the rooms. He traveled all over Costa Rica, and stated this was his favorite hotel in San Jose. I can understand why.

review_text:
This is an absolute must if you are traveling to or from San Jose.
The Grano de Oro Hotel staff has the service you would expect from a top tier hotel. Costa Rica is notorious for poor service and this place is the exception. Every one from the bell service, to the front desk, to the waiters were extremely helpful.
The rooms were charming and had a touch of an old Coffee plantation and rival the Victorians of San Francisco. We had a superior room with a fountain on a good size veranda. The rooms were well appointed with a fan, TV, and mini-fridge. Ours did not have a/c but we didn’t need it; the fan was more than enough.
San Jose doesn’t offer much to the tourist but expensive restaurants, and the same three stores; underwear, pharmacy, & toys repeated over and over again through downtown. Try Soda Tapia, a diner style fast food place with some Costa Rica dishes on the menu.
The hotel restaurant is spectacular. It is expensive but worth the treat. The food is excellent, service is superb, and the contrast to other San Jose restaurants makes this a must try. It was by far the best meal we had in Costa Rica.

review_text: We read all about Hotel Grano de Oro and decided to trust the many positive reviews of travelers before us...and they were right! We stayed in the cheapest of the room types, which was plenty big enough for us, and requested windows opening to the outside rather than a corridor, which they gave us (we stayed on two non-successive nights in two different rooms). The bathrooms were plenty big, with pretty blue tiles, and the rooms were nicely decorated in neutral colors but with an understated tropical feeling...good style choice. The restaurant is amazing and very well priced ($50 or so for a complete meal for two with drinks and appetizers and desserts...$10 for a big breakfast of fresh juice and pancakes for two). The hotel is pretty, with lots of little corridors and the rooms are spread throughout so you never walk down a long row of rooms. The two heated jacuzzis on the roof were secluded and a great touch. The only warning I would give potential visitors is that there is a bit of noise, at least in the rooms we stayed in, due to the arrangement of the hotel--both rooms opened to the restaurant, which we actually enjoyed (they screen the restaurant so while you can hear everything, no one can see into your room) but might irritate a very light sleeper. Most importantly, the staff there is amazing--every person we interacted with was polite and pampering, ready to help you with anything you need with a great attitude. They also have free internet (10 min max at a time), which was a nice surprise that enabled us to check in at home. A great choice for any San Jose visitors, particuarly great for looking forward to after an adventure elsewhere.

review_text: We spend our last night's stay in the Grano de Oro Hotel on a recent trip to Costa Rica. The hotel is stunning - it's a beautiful old mansion with true character and beauty. It's calming - which is a nice treat in the bustle of Costa Rica's biggest city. When we arrived, we were greated outside, someone whisked our bags away and as we approached the entry, there was soothing music and hints of a fountain near by. We had dinner reservations (make them when you book your stay as the restaurant was packed). The food was amazing - the very best meal of our trip - and it rivals many of the restaurants here in San Francisco. The best part - $65 for two with a fabulous bottle of red wine (which they recommended), plus dessert. Don't skip the restaurant! We had an early morning flight - but the airport was less than a 20 minute cab ride away. We had a wonderful stay - a great way to end our fabulous trip. Enjoy!

review_text: We stayed here one night on our way to another destination in Costa Rica. It's a great hotel for the first night there. It has a lot character, friendly staff, a great restaurant and fairly priced so you don't feel bad spending lots of money on a hotel where you don't even stay one full day. One disadvantage seemed like there weren't many places to just stroll to from the hotel but that didn't matter to us since we got there late and flew out early. The restaurant was amazing. Our room is pretty much in the outdoor area of the resturant and we were little worried about noise but they're really nice about closing outdoor area early at night/ opening it late in the morning for people who want to sleep in. Rooms are small so it may get a bit cramped if you're staying for longer than a few days.

review_title: Best place to stay in San Jose Costa Rica!
review_text:
We stayed here in October 2004 and we loved this place. I have recently become familiar with Tripadvisor and decided that this hotel deserves to be recommended to all of the tripadvisor users.
This hotel is absolutely enchanting and charming... the place looks like an oasis around all the other buildings in the neighborhood. The attention and service of the hotel staff is incredible. They are so attentive and customer oriented that you will feel so happy to stay at this place.
All the rooms are different and beautifully decorated. We enjoyed two different rooms. We stayed in San Jose when we arrived and the next day we went on a water rafting trip (we loved it!). Then we went to the Pacific side of the Country (Manuel Antonio - Quepos area) and when we came back to San Jose we stayed at this hotel again.
As for the safety concern, I believe it is a safe neighborhood. We walked to the local grocery store and bought some water and drinks and the only concern we had was crossing the streets!
On the night before we came back to the States, we went to the night clubs ("El Pueblo" area) and stayed until 3am and everything around the hotel seemed calmed and peaceful (contrary to the picture of the downtown area!!!).
We can't wait to go back to Costa Rica and if we stay in San Jose, we know where we are staying "El Grano de Oro"!

review_text: Stayed April 28 and April 30th (2 day raft trip in between with Rio Tropicales-great trip, definately spend the night in their river lodge). All the guidebooks and reviews on this site were right-on. Stayed in room 17 first night and room 12 second night, room 17 was an unexpecteded upgrade from standard I reserved and nicer than 12 (larger, had ouside courtyard to sit in and opened to courtyard fountain), room 12 was nice too, but smaller, no courtyard or bathtub. I would recommend chosing a deluxe ($109) over standard $90. Had dinner two nights in lovely tropical restaurant, both times very good. I walked alone around neighborhood to a grocery store/pharmacy (across from hospital on main street) about 10 minutes away and felt safe enough doing so in daytime. As in any bigger city, you have to take the usual precautions. You are about 15-20 min from airport and 10-15 minutes from bus station.

review_text:
When we first drove to our hotel, I was a little concerned because the area is not very safe or nice looking, we passed other hotels in the area that looked shabby and run down with bars on all the windows - I was so relieved to see our hotel when we turned right on to street 30. It was beautiful, and well tended.
We loved the plantation style decor, the staff was very professional, the rooftop jacuzzi was gorgeous, and the restaurant absolutely lovely. We stayed in room #3 which was a small but lovely standard room with a window that let in the world famous temperate climate of San Jose. The linens were decent, the room immaculate and well decorated with a lovely armoire for our things. It's the nicest place $116 ($90 plus tax) ever got us. The one draw back to our particular room is that at night we could hear the kitchen under us. It didn't bother us because we were both fast asleep in ten minutes.
In the morning we had breakfast in the garden courtyard. The local tico breakfast was delicious along with the fruits, and the atmosphere quiet, tropical, beautiful.
(quick note: the center of downtown is noisy, the women hold on to their purses and wear backpacks on the front, so not staying in the heart of downtown was actually a good decision).

review_title: Grano de Oro for the food and if you like cozy
review_text:
The Grano de Oro had the best food of any place we ate
during our two weeks in Costa Rica. The Marriott came in second
and generally the food was good in all the hotels and restaurants we tried, but the Grano de Oro was the best.
The hotel itself is in the middle of San Jose (actually not in the center, but walkable) and for that you pay the price of feeling kind of crowded at times. The staff were charming and helpful, but we never got our wakeup call ("Costa Rica" time we decided to call it after another hotel woke us up a half hour late). No matter, the car delivery we woke up early to be ready for (to get to Poas Volcano before the clouds came in) was about an hour late.
Despite getting twin beds instead of double (the travel agency's fault) the beds were super comfortable. We got to use the hot tub on the roof in complete privacy, and explored all the little hallways with fountains and flowers. Charming and cozy.

review_text: When my husband and I arrived in San Jose for the first night of our honeymoon, we were scheduled to stay at Grano de Oro. When we arrived around 10pm at night (after a long wedding weekend and flight) we were excited to spend the night there and relax. When we arrived we were told that they "overbooked" the hotel and had already made a reservation somewhere else for us! Before we left the States, both my husband and I confirmed our reservation. And, we had to ask them to pay for the taxi to the other hotel which at first they were reluctant to do! Needless to say we were very disappointed in the service.

review_text:
we were there 2 weeks ago and were rudely awakened by a 6.2 earthquake. The wood framed structure swayed and swayed but survived just fine.
regardless, beautiful quaint place. wonderful restaurant with a beautiful outdoor garden. staff was very friendly. San Jose is a little tough but this hotel is an oasis. the walk to downtown is a little long but not too bad. be sure and stop by Cafe La Bohemia. great place.
I would recommend requesting a room off of the ground floor. we had no choice since they were booked. our room was on the gorund floor and our window opened up to an interior vegetated corridor. not bad but noisy in the morning.

review_title: Great hotel for beginning or ending a trip to CR
review_text:
Pura Vida! This place was awesome. We stayed in a deluxe room off the patio (room #8). We arrived at 11pm, and the staff was very helpful with a weary family. Breakfast, lunch, and dinner were great.
We were able to walk to downtown from the hotel. Its about 20min by foot, or 5min by taxi.
+ relaxing
+ good location
+ good food
+ great staff
+ internet terminal in lobby

review_text:
I find myself in disagreement with a lot of people.
While the hotel is ok, I found the service distant and vacuous.
The front desk essentially ignored us on our arrival. The waiters are unattentive drones that periodically disappear for long periods of time. Seldom do I see a waiter make eye contact.
While the garden is a nice setting for dinner, it loses some of its charm when the girls in the orphanage behind the wall are screaming at the top of their lungs.
While they have a good menu, the food is essentially bland and follows the Costa Rican practice of no spice, no pepper.
I also find the location a bit too far from worthwhile sights.
I much prefer some of the hotels in the Barrio Amon

review_title: Very good place and good food!
review_text:
We stayed at Grano de Oro as our first hotel in Costa Rica on our first visit. It was a wonderful hotel made up of connected older, well appointed buildings. The landscaping was pretty, the rooftop hot tub was very nice as well. The food here is above average for Costa Rica (Food in Costa Rica in general is not very good - look for italian restaurants or grilled chicken - the only mostly safe bets).
This is also a good location as a base for visiting La Paz Waterfalls, Poas Volcano and rafting on the Pacuare river for the day.

review_text:
We spent the last night of our honeymoon here before flying out in the morning. The staff was friendly and the room was comfortable. After a long walk to the museums we ready for some air conditioned comfort...oops! I was concerned how the room would cool off with no air flow from the outside, but by the end of the night we were both reaching for the covers.
The restaraunt was the highlight of the stay. The food was excellent and reasonably priced. The dessert selection is amazing. The wait staff was great at dinner, but not so good for breakfast. All in all a very good experience.

review_text: Book a room here! Grano de Oro is truly a delightful oasis in San Jose. My husband and I stayed at this gem of a hotel in November of 2003 and are excited to return this fall because we enjoyed our stay so very much. The staff is welcoming, attentive and friendly, and we loved the rooftop jacuzzis. This small hotel itself is a converted mansion overflowing with exotic flowers. The rooms are good sized and tastefully decorated. The restaurant in this hotel must be one of the best in San Jose - try the special Grano de Oro pie for a wonderful treat. The prices at the hotel and restaurant are very reasonable.

review_text: We finished off a wonderful 10-day trip to Costa Rica by staying at Grano de Oro the night before our flight home. It's a small, boutique hotel in a renovated old colonial house, but unlike many such hotels, the decor is not twee or overdone, just comfy and quietly elegant. I really enjoyed the rooftop jacuzzi with the sound of evening Mass drifting over from the church next door and the view of San Jose. Dinner in the restaurant was amazing. It was expensive compared to most of our meals in Costa Rica but I still remember the rack of lamb and tres leches cake fondly. Service was friendly, swift and professional. If I ever go back to Costa Rica (I hope so), I will definitely take time to stay at Hotel Grano de Oro.
